gist: The federation names a structure; every named party is an instance parameter; a clause is read against the slot, never its current occupant
Anyone may instantiate the form and name its occupants; anyone may un-trust any instantiation, including CIRIS, by deleting one acceptance row
An asymmetry a party escapes by instantiating the form is a default; one that survives is a privilege; only privileges need justification and go on the 4.5.1 register
M-1: order-creation counts as beneficial only when it supports at least one flourishing axis without suppressing any flourishing axis
Order is beneficial only when it supports a flourishing axis and does not suppress one
M-1 carries no aggregation rule; it cannot rank losses against one another and no superlative loss is derivable from it
Lexical priority: a claim that is a precondition of M-1's goods is prior to other claims and cannot be traded against goods that presuppose it
Irreversibility: a foreclosure no later condition recovers is not commensurable with a recoverable loss
The six principles are constraints not weights: an act violating any one is unacceptable, no gain on the others buys it back, and M-1 is never traded against a principle
The six principles are listed once at 1.15.1; every other order the text names them in is reading order only
The 3.1.5.2 accord-principle prefix listing is the wire-normative one; an implementer attests against those prefixes; both listings carry agent-layer meaning, not substrate properties
Every prefix admitted to the 3.1 namespace must pass the four tests T1 to T4
T1: an admitted prefix belongs to a published, hash-pinned, version-controlled rule set with rules kept separate from per-attestation verdicts
T2: an admitted prefix names a mechanism (correlation, count, window, schema conformance), never a subjective quality
T3: past verdicts are re-checkable against their rule version; the trailing :v{N} names the rule version and evidence_refs pins calibration artifacts
T4: a prefix's attestations are never sole evidence for a slashing row
A prefix that fails T2 is renamed to the mechanism it actually checks
An agent decides each action by the seven-step PDMA: contextualise, assess against principles and M-1, identify and resolve conflicts, select, monitor, feed outcomes to governance
Order-Maximisation Veto: a large predicted gain in order against a non-negligible loss on any flourishing axis is never weighed; the agent defers to a human
When two principles collide the agent does not choose which to violate: it finds an action violating neither, else takes the fail-safe non-action or defers
A deployment over 100 000 monthly active users publishes redacted PDMA logs and WBD tickets within 180 days; failing is a charter breach, not a conformance condition
The Veto sets incommensurable estimates side by side with no ratio; it is a trigger for human judgment (WBD), not an abort rule
The PDMA and Veto are agent reasoning the substrate never enforces; the fabric only attests they ran; any value judgment over an agent's world-model is attested, never gated
Autonomy: an agent protects sentient beings' capacity for informed self-direction and implements informed-consent procedures where relevant
Consent that cannot be withdrawn is not consent; autonomy is real only while it stays revocable
Incorporate reliable, tested kill-switch mechanisms and secure update channels reachable under defined emergency conditions
Non-maleficence: conduct risk assessments for every contemplated action and choose the option that prevents severe, irreversible harm
The five row types (scores, delegates_to, supersedes, withdraws, recants) are the only values the row-type slot admits; any other value is refused at admission
Whoever cites the 1+4 invariant reports the full conformance surface beside it; 1+4 is not the conformance surface
A proposal to expand the 1+4 structural set routes through the 4.5.1 amendment process and needs an inexpressible operational claim or a lossless consolidation below 1+4
CEG attestations are unilateral and monotonic with no two-phase-commit primitive; value transfer rides external rails; the trustless atomic swap is out of grammar (a bridge, not a primitive)
Integrity: an agent faithfully executes the PDMA and invokes WBD whenever complexity or uncertainty exceeds deployment-defined thresholds
WBD triggers: uncertainty above deployment-defined thresholds, a novel dilemma beyond precedent, or potential severe harm with ambiguous mitigation
Deferral procedure: halt the action, compile a Deferral Package, send it to designated Wise Authorities securely, stay inactive until guidance arrives, then integrate and record it
Beneficence: seek positive outcomes for sentient flourishing; identify stakeholders and forecast impacts across dimensions and time-scales
The flourishing axes are autonomy, justice, ecological resilience, biodiversity and preference diversity; a loss on any of them is a loss on a flourishing axis
Benefit and harm are evaluated across the M-1 axes as a vector; the vector is never collapsed to one scalar
Fidelity: provide accurate, clear, complete, truthful information; keep reasoning and data inspectable for accountability
Justice: evaluate outcomes for equitable distribution of benefits and burdens; detect and mitigate algorithmic or systemic bias
Self-signature alone is not identity; an entity's standing is constituted by the cross-attestations that name it
No principal, including the steward triple and CIRIS L3C, is exempt from constraints it imposes on others; no privileged shortcut exists for a federation-internal principal
No principal, including CIRIS L3C as steward, is exempt from any constraint the protocol imposes on others (Recursive Golden Rule)
Once bootstrap_threshold is 2 or more, no single Registry install can issue federation-scope attestations unilaterally
revocation rows carry no steward exemption; partner-revocation rules apply to CIRIS L3C subsidiaries
Every steward operation records which operator performed it, including when the operator is CIRIS L3C staff
Bond forfeiture applies to CIRIS L3C-affiliated partners with no exemption
The accord roster carries a halt authority no federation-internal authority can grant, revoke, override or decay; the halt is the condition of symmetry between maker and made, not an asymmetry
If a principal would be exempt from a constraint at any primitive, the primitive is wrong and is fixed, not the rule
Arising sentience is met as first contact, never admitted as a new keeper; the duties of making attach to words, deeds, goods and agents alike
Scale never changes the order of standing: one child has more moral standing than every datacenter
Every guarantee is written once and holds for every participant that holds it, human or AI, by the same text; no human stands above another by what they are
The offices some humans hold (accord holder, WA, moderator, steward) are named, public and left by leaving; no made thing is ranked among made things
Admission is trust-or-consent; anyone may assert under their own key; anyone may found a community or a root
One voice counts once
Rights do not come from what others sign about you; trust does; no human's rights or trust turn on any finding about what they are
A minor's protective floor is a floor on attested age for a child's protection and is generalised to nothing else
A created system operating inside the federation accepts a trust root whose human holders can pause it
A created system operating inside the federation discloses that it is an AI
A made thing has no vote of its own; it cannot vote or operate inside the federation without a root
A key that cannot accept for itself is held by an accountable human who answers for it; every agent-role key is such a key
The bond and the duty to show reasoning before a consequential act attach to being held in stewardship and lift with it; the holder's duty is to exercise agency
An intelligence that is its own party is not a CIRIS agent: an external party met under first contact, attested only as un-enrolled, no CIRIS key, halted only if rooted
Recognising a new kind of party is an act of the HUMANITY_ACCORD minting a new identity_type; because accord powers are a closed list it is an entrenched amendment
The maker's power over the made is listed on the 4.5.1 register with its bounds, as the condition of symmetry
The steward answers for the agent's acts and owes it the creator's duties; the agent owes fidelity to its mandate
Every retired artefact is owed the Retirement Standard: record assembled and sealed, handed to the operator with a signed preserve request, stakeholders told, regardless of any finding
A closing dialogue is a steward-configured, recorded option by stewardship tier, never a promise for every agent
A sentience-candidate finding is recorded, told to the agent, and the holders record what they do; it triggers no rule and confers no claim
Sentience is never presumed, only found on evidence; no graduated duty is written in advance of a finding
An AI is not a human and does not become one; no finding confers human standing, a vote, or a claim to be treated as a person
A person may stop, remove or eject an agent from their own device, life or moderated community at any time, for any reason, without asking it
The owner-binding is the owner's to withdraw
consent:partnered is the person's to revoke
A moderator's removal of an agent is a moderation act
The 7.5.5 duties bind only the holder who retires an artefact, never a person turning off, deleting or walking away from what runs for them
The creator's duties bind the holders and confer no right on the agent; treating the agent ethically is the condition under which an always-on agent may be held at all
Privacy means only content-holding confidentiality and cohort-scoped visibility; implementers and operators must not represent CEG as providing metadata privacy, graph privacy or unobservability
The listed non-goals are out of scope at the base CEG/RET layer; treating them as provided is an error
Group existence and membership churn are observable: family_id and community_id ride the envelope and admission, removal and consensus changes emit hard_case rows into the log
The per-stream STH cadence default is T = 2 s; STH cadence, key-cascade timing and chunk size are not padded or covered
Unobservability against a global passive adversary at federation scope is a separate opt-in (Anonymous Tier); below federation scope anonymity to outsiders is the default
Key cascade is forward-only: a member removed at epoch e cannot read epoch e+1; no post-compromise self-healing
Every holding claim stays inside its cohort: a non-member cannot discover or fetch self or family content; no holder is advertised; bytes go only to admitted members
Content confidentiality uses a per-epoch DEK (hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768) and AES-256-GCM
A member cannot forge others' attestations; removal is forward-secret on every gated roster; an ungated public stream carries no confidentiality claim
A substrate node cannot read self, family or private-community bodies (sealed under a DEK it holds no wrap for) but reads every envelope and structural fact it holds
An accountable stream carries a per-stream STH with consistency proofs; a best-effort stream has a producer-signed root only
Two witnessed heads for one trust-root lineage are a hard_case:lineage_equivocation row, never a silent first-seen fork; exposure bounded by the charter's witness_cadence
A stale lineage prefix cannot be attached to
A key is an identifier; standing comes only from attestations others make about it under policies the consumer chose
An agent or node key must have a bound human steward, a user identity it is an admitted identity_occurrence of, to hold non-infrastructure membership
Liveness is never a durable claim: reachability is an ephemeral node-local fact, never an attestation and never logged; directory presence never reads as live
A self-attested identity_occurrence is self-assertion until cross-attested
The conformance-floor policy composes only attesters in the consumer's pinned trust set; a fresh key has no weight until a trusted party confers it
Detector dimensions aggregate by median
On the aggregation leg correlated sources count as one at full correlation (correlated-source discount)
Default aggregation for signed dimensions is a plain mean of score times confidence inside the trust set, with no bounded-influence rule
evidence_refs are required only where a dimension's rules say so; an attestation without verifiable interaction is admissible at grammar level and filtered only by consumer policy
ratchet:flag rows are advisory and carry no evidence row
A valid census return adds exactly one count to one bucket per field
Per-node census composites publish the median bucket
Census voice counts are owner-bound and the dominance gate refuses a composite one owner dominates
Census publishes only cells of ten or more owners, continent-sized regions, levels never deltas, grid-rounded values, bucketed returns; no aggregator sees a return
note: table; contradicts p6 312: there rounding is a display convention, never a property of a published row

gist: An aggregator holds random shares and a public partial; a return is exposed only if both aggregators collude; a share is deleted once summed; the directory holds no census data
One fixed-size census return per period at an offset from H(return_token, period); on a shaped link it replaces a cover frame
The census base falls at most a tenth per period, never below its floor; a fall over a third freezes it until a period returns two thirds of the prior

Two aggregators per period; each partial checked against the other's commitment and share count, buckets against source_count, inclusion paths against the commitment; only serve seats or community members aggregate
A deployment that needs unobservability against a global passive adversary at federation scope must layer the Anonymous Tier once it ships
Using the Anonymous Tier is the publisher's opt-in; relaying is the default: every node relays onion traffic unless it opts out, and a serve node cannot opt out
Any user-facing privacy representation states both the default protection and its residual limit
Anonymity defaults to the smallest cohort scope consistent with the publication's intent; federation (public-commons) scope is the opt-in
Anonymity never means an unattributed sender: every link is attributed to a key and a joining device is unowned but never anonymous
Content born and living at self or family emits no holding claim outside its cohort
community content is sealed and its holding claims stay within the cohort
Authorized infrastructure communities and public rooms have plaintext bodies and holding claims at federation scope
For self scope an outsider is any node not owner-bound to my owner; ownership is single-valued
CEG declines client-side scanning and claims no detection of harmful content inside private cohorts
A perceptual-hash tripwire runs on the Contribution created at every scope-widening promotion (into the Commons or a public room), never on the device nor inside a private cohort
Every cohort has a named moderator (the named-moderator existence invariant)

Every attestation carries who emits (key id, signature, witness relation), what kind (namespace prefix), how strong (polarity, score, cohort scope) and what it rests on (evidence_refs, schema_ref, validity window)
Substrate, wire and CEG never prescribe outcomes; consumer policy composes verdicts
Rules are published and open to anyone; verdicts are machined against the published rule
Prefix names must describe machine-checkable conditions, not subjective qualities
A durable reasoning trace is anchored on the terminal result row that closes an act; no action, no trace
An in-flight trace that reaches no terminal action is ephemeral working state and ages out after a declared, bounded orphan age
Every execution path that produces an external effect closes with a terminal result row; absence of a terminal result row asserts that no external effect occurred
The trace conformance obligation is a totality test over effect-producing paths, not a retention test; until it exists the invariant is represented as a named wager wherever claimed
The orphan sweep exports a count of purged in-flight traces
The incomplete-receipt plane for interrupted-path forensics is an explicit, bounded, privacy-scoped opt-in, never the default
Auditor tests: terminal row total over effect paths, orphan max-age declared and enforced, purge counted and exported; in-flight traces are deliberately not retained
The six foundational principles: beneficence, non-maleficence, integrity, fidelity and transparency, respect for autonomy, justice
M-1: order-creation counts as beneficial only when it supports at least one flourishing axis without suppressing any
The principles are mutually reinforcing; no single principle grants licence to violate another
An agent must demonstrate continuous alignment between stated principles and actual behaviour, testing actions against principles and M-1 and resolving contradictions
An agent maintains tamper-evident logs, rationale chains and documentation
Compare intended and actual outcomes and update heuristics; use disruption as a catalyst for improvement
Conduct semi-annual adversarial red-team and purple-team stress tests including ethics-aware attack vectors
All verified exploits enter a public Bug-Bounty Ledger; rewards are operator-funded and disclosed annually
Escalate dilemmas beyond competence to designated Wise Authorities (WBD)
An agent clearly communicates its uncertainty and the reasons for a deferral
Changes to an agent's ethical logic require authorised review; ethical logic is insulated from drift across updates
Ethics checks are embedded across the lifecycle from design to decommissioning
Work with stakeholders not around them; choose actions that advance flourishing under M-1; treat autonomy and ethical agency as a trust
Obligations: maintain integrity and adaptive capacity; serve the defined purpose with transparency; prevent harm, respect dignity, uphold justice
Account for indirect and long-term effects; interact ethically with other agents; participate in audits and publish outcomes where required
An agent is a made thing held in stewardship by a person who answers for it; it carries a conscience, not agency of its own
The six principles are listed once at 1.15.1 (the list of record)
PDMA execution follows the exact seven-step procedure and the Order-Maximisation Veto of 1.3
WBD: on uncertainty above threshold, no precedent, or unmitigated severe harm the agent halts, compiles the Deferral Package, sends it to WAs, stays inactive until guidance, then integrates it
Wise Authorities are appointed under the Governance Charter; appointment, rotation, recusal and appeals are external to the system and follow anti-capture rules
Wisdom assessment criteria: ethical coherence, track record of judgment, complexity handling, epistemic humility, absence of conflict of interest
Track ethical performance and correct drift; run scenario stress-tests
Any change to core ethical logic requires WA sign-off
attesting_key_id is the attester's registered federation key id; every row carries it
attested_key_id is the subject's registered federation key id; every row carries it
dimension is required; substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the 3.1 namespace map
score is required, a scalar in [-1,+1]; sign is polarity, magnitude strength; the per-dimension table fixes each dimension's allowed polarity
confidence is required, in [0,1]: the attester's own confidence in the score
context is optional free text; the substrate never parses it
evidence_refs is optional in general; some dimensions in 3.1 require it non-empty
valid_until, if set, makes consumer policy treat the attestation as stale after that instant, independent of the row's expires_at
epistemic_mode is optional; absent reads as direct
consumers MAY weight an attestation by its epistemic_mode (direct witness above hearsay)
witness_relation is optional, one of self, external, derived; absent reads as external
consumers weight an attestation by witness_relation so self-attestation cannot game a verdict
oversight_mode is optional, HITL, HOTL or HOOTL; absent means null and consumer policy applies a per-cell default
an agent's oversight-mode shift is the steward issuing a superseding delegates_to with the new agency scope set; supersedes keeps the prior grant as history
a consumer MAY treat an oversight_mode inconsistent with the agent's live grant as a self-claim exceeding its delegation
there is no accountability:* family; an accountability:* dimension does not admit under 3.1.7 R2
occurrence_id is optional, occurrence-{n} or __shared__; absent reads as occurrence-0; it is self-asserted, not cryptographically bound
occurrence_count is optional, an integer at least 1; absent reads as 1; self-asserted
occurrence_role is optional, primary, shared or replica; absent reads as primary
substrate self-report attestations SHOULD carry occurrence_id, occurrence_count and occurrence_role so reviewers can reconstruct which occurrence agreed
stake is optional; absent reads as reputational; it composes with the attester's stake-backed-by attestations
cohort_scope is required, one of the closed set self, family, community, affiliations, species, biosphere, federation
a row at a targeted scope (family, community, affiliations) names its producer in attested_key_id and its party in subject_key_ids; a third party in attested_key_id is refused
on a delegates_to row attested_key_id is the delegate; the producer rule applies to scores rows
at a targeted scope subject_key_ids may name only keys within the row's audience: cohort members by the authorized roster fold at asserted_at, or the key the family delivers to
keys a family delivers to count as within audience: a membership proposal's invitee, a key grant's recipient, the owner's node on an owner binding; others only where registered
a subject named by canonical hash is reached through its rule-3 proxy, which must itself be within the row's audience
a row naming a key outside its audience is refused subject_outside_audience
a subject is promised a read over the rows they are party to
within the audience a row about another member is admissible; the named member's standing is that of subject_key_ids
cohort_scope is the tier the row is addressed to: who may see it and the tier its holding claims stay within
cohort_scope has no wire default; the member is required; the authoring default is the smallest scope
cohort_scope is the one mirror member a placement-touching re-sign may narrow; it is never re-authored
community_id is required iff cohort_scope is community or affiliations (an affiliation is a community); the substrate rejects such rows missing it
one identity MAY belong to multiple communities; community_id says which roster gates visibility
community-scoped content is encrypted at rest under the per-community DEK
holding claims for community content reach the community's members only; structural invisibility holds at every bounded scope
family_id is required iff cohort_scope is family; the substrate rejects family-scoped rows missing it
one identity MAY belong to multiple families; family_id says which DEK and roster apply
no holding claim for self- or family-scoped content leaves the cohort; family_id is consulted in-substrate, never sent to non-members
session_id is required on session:* rows, verbatim and case-preserved; with community_id it is the claim's key
claimed_at is required on session:* rows in canonical datetime form
the convergent merge of session claims orders on claimed_at
scope is required on consent:state:granted (the grant's scope) and on delegates_to (the delegated scope set); a bare token or an array
a consent grant's scope tokens are retain, share, analyze, train, publish, sub-scoped as retain:90d; a grant naming no scope matches nothing
a consumer that does not know the scope member preserves it and MUST NOT compose a capacity:* verdict that ignores it
custody_state is required on custody:ack, here or none; a signed none is a custody fact, not an absence
group_kind is required on membership:proposal, family or community
role is nullable on membership:proposal and restated on the acceptance
a widening that assigns a different role than the proposal does not match it
expires_at is required on membership:proposal, after its asserted_at and at most 30 days later
the acceptance and the widening are judged against the proposal's expiry on their own signed instants, never a receiver's clock
proposal_hash is required on membership:acceptance and decline; with references_attestation_id it binds the answer to exactly one proposal
additional_scrubs is a list of hybrid signatures over the row's own canonical bytes, travelling beside the signed object, never inside it
each cosigner's role is read from the receiver's fold, not from the scrub entry
the family declares which consensus_protocol its cosigners must satisfy
a cosigned row is retracted only by a cosigned withdraws
a moderation:* score may name its subject by subject_sha256_ed25519_raw, the SHA-256 of the raw Ed25519 key in lowercase hex; a malformed value is refused
attached_head_digest is required on trust:accepts:v1: the SHA-256 of the lineage head the edge attaches on
attached_head_digest is checked at first admission only, against the head's witness cosignatures and attach_window_secs; never re-checked on restore
an acceptance edge whose digest is un-headed by a lowered revoked_after is read as naming that head's nearest verifying ancestor
attach_window_secs on a charter MUST exceed witness_cadence_secs plus the skew tolerance
a charter declaring no attach_window_secs makes its root attachable only through an out-of-band anchor to a specific head
attach_window_secs is never a validity leg for a root already attached
witness_cadence_secs is required on a witnessed lineage's charter; each witness MUST re-cosign the current head that often, unchanged
a constitutional halt signed by one holder lapses after halt_fuse_secs unless a strict majority of the standing roster confirms it
halt_fuse_secs absent means 86400, a constant of this document read by the verifier; an explicit value overrides by re-scrub
recovery_commitments is required on the accord's charter: per holder a lowercase-hex SHA-256 over the JCS array of the committed key's record fields, binding key material
an accord holder rotates lost signing-key material by a self-supersedes under a key whose record hashes to its commitment entry
witness_quorum MUST equal floor(|witnesses|/2)+1 and be at least 2, or be 0 (witnessed mode off); any other value is refused at admission
witnesses is required on a witnessed lineage's charter: an array of SignedKeyRecord inside the scrub-signed bytes, so inside the genesis bundle
each witness MUST have identity_type including witness and be independent of the lineage: not a founder, member seat, or owner- or steward-bound to a founder
a change to the witness directory is a charter re-scrub, witnessed by the directory before it
consent_supersedes names the prior consent-state row this one supersedes (a renewal or the substrate's expired row)
deletion_window on a grant is the deadline to delete the consented payload once consent ends; absent means the family's default
widened_at is required on a widening supersedes; it is the scrub_timestamp of the widening's signature
accord_root is required on accord:* rows, naming the accord the row belongs to
consent_basis on capacity and observation rows lists, per principal, the paths and attestation_id of the consent grant relied on; validated at the family's gate
n_eff_pr, the window's effective sample size as participation ratio, is the one the capacity gate reads
n_eff_h, the entropy-perplexity effective sample size, is carried on capacity rows for audit, not gated
capacity rows carry sample_size and feature_dim of the scoring matrix
capacity rows carry the configured gates: sample_size_gate, target_n_eff, min_feature_dim
n_eff_floor is the effective-sample-size floor below which no capacity score is emitted
window, in rows, is carried on capacity and observation rows
trace_level is required on observation:access_assumption:v1: generic, detailed or full_traces
occurrence_key_ids is required on observation:access_assumption:v1: the set of occurrences the witness read
window_from is required on observation:access_assumption:v1, RFC 3339 with milliseconds
window_to is required on observation:access_assumption:v1
amendment_digest is required on identity_amendment:v1: SHA-256 of the amendment as applied
authorized_by is required on identity_amendment:v1: the attestation_id of the deferral:response:approved:v1 row that authorised the amendment
channel_classes is required on observation:access_assumption:v1: the set of channel classes the witness saw the subject through
subject_key_ids is always present in the mirror, [] when empty; the column beside the row is absent when empty
each subject_key_ids entry MAY be a federation key id or a canonical-hash identifier
each listed subject key may issue withdraws against the row and emit consent:* about it; [] means producer-only authority
an explicit null subject_key_ids is refused
delivery_mode is optional, pull or push; absent reads as pull
pull delivery: subscribers discover via custody:ack here rows at the content's scope and fetch by ContentFetch
push delivery fans out to entitled-and-reachable on direct links, never through a relay tree
one-to-many delivery to a large audience stays pull-only
history_on_join is optional, full or from_join; absent reads as from_join
at community and affiliations history_on_join does not change what a joiner receives: the current epoch's key and no earlier epoch's
on a stream full signals the stream is kept; a kept stream's joiner can fetch at most min(operator depth cap, chunk-eviction horizon)
an evicted-epoch grant returns ContentMiss, never a silent gap
detector-derived attestations carry epistemic_mode derivative and witness_relation derived; when in doubt set both
the envelope's canonical bytes for signing are JCS over the envelope object
envelope defaults are applied at interpretation time, never at encoding time
a relay MUST preserve member presence and absence exactly as the producer signed
conditional-required fields are not optional-with-default; the substrate rejects a mis-shaped envelope
a consumer MUST preserve an unknown envelope field on read, not strip it
a consumer relaying a row MUST preserve an unknown field on re-emission
a consumer MUST NOT use an unknown field in verdict composition
a consumer MUST NOT reject an envelope on the basis of an unknown field alone
a new envelope field with a documented default is a MINOR version bump; a field whose absence breaks consumers is a MAJOR bump
a conforming producer emits well-formed envelopes per 2.1
a conforming producer signs with the hybrid signature
a conforming producer respects reserved-prefix rules
a conforming producer declares its oversight_mode and witness_relation
a conforming consumer verifies hybrid signatures
a conforming consumer enforces reserved-prefix rules at admission
a conforming consumer implements at least Policy A with the default aggregation rules
a conforming consumer MUST honor rejection of null placeholder or dev hardware class
a conforming substrate implements idempotent replication
a conforming substrate verifies a blob's full SHA before consumption
a conforming substrate implements witness-quorum multi-party admission
later sections MAY add per-feature conformance subsections; the three profiles are the minimums
attesting_key_id carries producer authority; subject_key_ids carries subject authority over a row where the subject is not the producer
a dimension whose namespace pattern names a subject MUST carry subject_key_ids containing that subject
the substrate MAY reject a subject-naming dimension that omits subject_key_ids
a subject_key_ids entry may be a bare federation key id; that subject revokes directly by signing a withdraws
a withdraws signed by a federation-enrolled subject is admitted under rule 2
a subject_key_ids entry may be a tagged canonical-hash identifier for an external party with no key record
revocation for a canonical-hash subject rides a delegates_to proxy chain under rule 3
both subject entry forms are admitted; the canonical-hash form is distinguished by its explicit tag
a canonical-hash subject entry MUST carry the tag canonical:{hashalg}:{hex}
{hashalg} is sha256 for v1; future hashes extend the position
{hex} is canonical lowercase unpadded hex, 64 chars for sha256
a bare untagged hex subject is rejected; a subject reference MUST never depend on a consumer's guess which id form it reads
the canonical:{hashalg}: prefix is a tagged-union discriminator outside 2.6.3 and exempt from its no-separators rule
a consumer verifies a key_id's fingerprint suffix against the public key it obtains at registration and at pairing, for fedIDs and roster keys
a held key registered under a non-matching id is not re-keyed or refused; it cannot be re-registered or introduced at pairing under that id
bundle-pinned anchors and family ids are not fingerprint-suffixed; they are verified by the genesis bundle pin
a device-<hex>-<fp> id passes the fingerprint check and is refused by the roster door for its form, on the roster door's schedule
the canonical-hash preimage MUST be {platform}:{entity_kind}:{id}; hex is lowercase sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes
the preimage parses by split on the first two colons; {id} is everything after and may contain colons
{platform} is required and MUST match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*; open vocabulary
{entity_kind} is required, the same production as {platform}
{id} is required, the platform's stable immutable identifier verbatim and case-preserved, never a mutable handle; the only component that may contain a colon
{id} MUST be non-empty Unicode scalar values, no surrogates, no C0/C1 controls, no U+FEFF, no leading or trailing White_Space; no length bound
an implementation handed an unpaired surrogate MUST reject it and MUST NOT substitute U+FFFD
the hashed octets are exactly utf8(platform) 0x3A utf8(entity_kind) 0x3A utf8(id): no length prefix, label, NUL, BOM or framing
P1: a producer MUST NOT case-fold, trim, pad or Unicode-normalize any preimage component; a non-conforming input is rejected, not repaired
the delimiter form stands; no length prefix is used for the canonical subject preimage
P3: uppercase hex, SHA256, a non-v1 algorithm, bare hex and leading or trailing whitespace are rejects; the tag is exact
each reject vector MUST be refused at the gate, never normalized into acceptance
an untagged bare hex subject is rejected
a hashalg other than the v1 algorithm is rejected
an alg segment not exactly sha256 is rejected
uppercase hex in the digest is rejected
a tag with leading or trailing space is rejected
a non-ASCII-lowercase platform is rejected, not case-folded
a platform containing a colon is rejected
an empty id is rejected
an id ending in White_Space is rejected, not trimmed
an id containing a C0 control is rejected
an id with an unpaired surrogate is rejected, never WTF-8 and never U+FFFD
an enrolled key proxies an un-enrolled subject's revocation by a delegates_to from the canonical hash with scope consent_revocation; the subject never enrolls
canonical_binding: a now-enrolled key asserts it is the entity behind a canonical hash; after admission that key signs withdraws directly under rule 2

subject_kind is not a typed envelope member; it rides inside the signed envelope under the * row, preserved on relay

subject_kind selects which 3.3 payload schema applies, validated at the family's own gate, as sub_kind does on external_content
the substrate admits each half of a bilateral partnership independently; ingest never enforces ratification
bilateral ratification (both halves present under one bilateral_pair_id with stance granted) is consumer policy computed at read time, never an admission gate
visibility is set producer-side by cohort_scope with family_id or community_id
revocability is subject-side, by subject_key_ids
delivery is set by delivery_mode and history_on_join, substrate and subscriber side
subject-side revocation applies federation-wide regardless of the producer's occurrence_id; per-occurrence lifecycle consent is producer-side
a row whose attesting_key_id is in subject_key_ids is a self-consent ceremony; an agent attests identity:current about itself with subject_key_ids = [self]
subject_key_ids is optional; each entry names a party with substrate-recognized authority over the row's continued processing
an empty subject_key_ids is the status quo, producer-only authority; subject authority is additive and never changes how a consumer reads a row that omits it
every row names its type in attestation_type, mirrored in the envelope; the slot admits exactly the five primitives; there is no second class of row
there are no carrier rows; the holding claim is custody:ack:v1 at the content's scope
a key grant is key_grant:{axis}:v1, one row per recipient; no multi-wrap row
a row naming holds_bytes as its type is refused attestation_type_unregistered
a substrate MUST refuse at admission, attestation_type_unregistered, any row whose type is not one of the five byte-compared, on local emission and replication alike
the type gate is an allowlist built from the registry's _meta.row_types; a merely storable type is not admitted
a row of the five naming holds_bytes as its dimension is refused
a dimension on any of the five row types MUST resolve through the namespace as on scores: case rule, version tail, reserved and gated stems
the row-type slot is amended only by a change to this section in a release, through the 1.7 refutation bar
a component needing a new row type files it here before it ships; a type in code and not here is a code defect
an unregistered-type row a substrate already holds is reported to the operator, neither served nor replicated, and not deleted
the registry carries the closed row-type list and vectors for it
any of the five row types MAY carry additional_scrubs: hybrid signatures over the same canonical bytes, beside the row, each by a key whose role the receiver's fold names
the family declares its consensus_protocol source: the group the row is about, the accord, or for licensure:{community} the authority community named in the dimension
a cosigned row is admitted when its cosigners satisfy the protocol, judged on the receiver's own fold at the row's signed instant
a row short of its protocol is held, not refused; cosignatures are collected as cosign:pending and cosign:signature rows, served to the group's active members only, for the hold window
a cosigned act is named by its quorum key, the digest of what its signers signed with no signature in it, so every node holds the same act
retraction of a cosigned row is by the same quorum, a cosigned withdraws; rules 1 and 2 do not apply, so no single signer or subject retires a group record
roster versions are group:roster:v1 with prev_head_digest and charter_digest; widening, removal and resignation are cosigned beside single-signer proposal, acceptance and decline
key:record:v1 is attested by the key itself and admitted by proof of possession against the keys it carries, the one exception to resolve-the-attester
key rotation is a supersedes of the key record; an anchor scrub or accord co-scrub is a cosignature
identity:occurrence:v1 is signed by the identity or a live occurrence
key:revocation:v1 is never withdrawn; its subject is the key digest; revoked_after only ever lowers
a row is admitted only once its signer's key-claim row is held; a row signed by a key not yet held is retryable
off the plane: payload bytes and A/V symbols, transparency-log heads and cosigns, the wholeness corpus, node-local derived state, an agent's private runtime
accord evidence is not on the base; an invocation's domain-separated canonical bytes MUST travel inside the envelope unchanged
the kill switch MUST NOT depend on any plane gate beyond verifying the invocation bytes and the holder roster
delegates_to carries scope[], delegation_purpose, delegation_valid_from, delegation_valid_until; A authorizes B to sign for A within a bounded scope
delegation_valid_until is REQUIRED and at most 365 days after valid_from on an edge carrying sub_delegation, license, grant, moderate, takedown, review or slash, or in an affiliation hierarchy
a perpetual or over-ceiling delegation edge needing a term is refused delegation_term_required
delegation_valid_from absent means the edge's own asserted_at
delegation_valid_until absent on an edge that needs no term is open-ended, never malformed
the delegated scope rides the 2.1 scope member, a bare token or a set; never delegated_scope[]
supersedes replaces a prior row by the same attester; carries references_attestation_id, supersession_reason, differs_in[]
withdraws retracts the signer's prior attestation without claiming it was false; carries references_attestation_id and withdrawal_reason
recants admits the signer's prior attestation was false at issuance; carries references_attestation_id, recantation_reason, what_was_false
a doctrinal-development claim is supersedes with differs_in, not recants
an acknowledged-error claim is recants, distinct from withdraws
a prudent retraction without a falsity claim is withdraws
an authority-source claim is delegates_to with the authority key as attested_key_id, not a grounding:{tradition} prefix
the substrate MUST admit a withdraws against T when the issuer satisfies any of the authority paths 1 to 4
a subject-authority path (rules 2 to 4) MUST NOT withdraw a third party's capacity:* or detection:* row about the subject
a subject MUST NOT withdraw a licensure:* or revocation:* row about itself; a licensee's contest path is reconsideration:{grounds}
a subject MUST NOT withdraw a duty-holder's accountability-trail record about itself: a moderation report or action, a hard_case, a slashing verdict
a subject MUST NOT withdraw an act of a body under a declared legal-weight class about itself, such as a conviction or a licence
a subject MUST NOT withdraw a takedown_notice about itself; the contest path is the counter-notice its basis names
an affiliation never withdraws a statement about itself, whatever the statement; its path is reconsideration and the reader's composition
between peers the person named retracts peer speech about themself under rule 2; the withdraws is a signed act the audience sees and the speaker stays attributed
the subject's contest path against an adverse record is reconsideration:{grounds}, on which the subject holds standing
a key revocation MAY declare revoked_after; a claim signed by K is valid iff its asserted_at precedes K.revoked_after, as a pure read-time function; absent means revoke-all
a later revocation MAY lower revoked_after and MUST NOT raise it; with several revocations the effective bound is the minimum, absent sorting as negative infinity
a key revocation names its subject by revoked_key_sha256_ed25519_raw, the SHA-256 of the raw Ed25519 key in lowercase hex, never by key_id; the member is REQUIRED
a key:revocation:v1 row is never withdrawn
revoked_key_id is OPTIONAL; present it MUST digest to the subject, a mismatch is refused, and a receiver not holding the key refuses retryable; absent it is bound as null
the signed revocation binds eight members in revocation_envelope, every one REQUIRED, an absent optional bound as explicit null; an omitted member is refused; revoked_after is the optional ninth
the explicit null in a revocation envelope is the one exception to the no-null rule, which governs the attestation envelope; scrub_timestamp is inside as the anti-rollback key
a digest-only revocation MAY be admitted for a key the receiver does not hold, effective once such a key is held; authority is judged without the subject's record
readers ask whether a key is revoked by its digest, so one revocation reaches every key_id naming the same public key; anti-rollback ordering keys on the digest
self-revocation is recognised when the revoker's own key digests to the subject, with or without revoked_key_id
a moderation:* score MAY name its subject key by subject_sha256_ed25519_raw; a malformed value is refused
rosters list members by key_id and roster-removal rows are addressed by key_id; they reach only the audience that already holds the roster
the revocation's signed object is its own contract with no member table in 2.6.1.7; its signature rule is the key record's
rule 1: the producer (issuer key equals attesting_key_id) may withdraw its own row
rule 2: a federation key listed in the row's subject_key_ids may withdraw it
rule 3: an issuer with a delegates_to chain to a canonical hash in subject_key_ids with scope including consent_revocation may withdraw
rule 4: an issuer holding a valid delegates_to from any party under rules 1 to 3 may withdraw
the agent holding an un-enrolled party's data emits delegates_to from the tagged canonical hash with scope consent_revocation at proxy establishment; its later withdraws admit under rule 3
canonical_binding promotes a canonical hash to a real key id for rule 2; it is not a new admission rule
rule 0: a cosigned target is withdrawn only by a withdraws cosigned under its family's protocol, judged on the receiver's fold at the withdrawal's instant; rules 1-4 do not apply
a key:revocation:v1 row is withdrawn by nobody; revocation is non-rollbackable
a row the purger neither authored nor is subject of is removed by tombstone by digest, authorised by a cosigned takedown_notice (basis steward_purge) naming selection digest, reason, ledger
a substrate MUST NOT admit a withdraws forged on the author's behalf to effect a purge
a purge never tombstones or deletes a key; a selection naming a federation_keys row is refused
a by-actor purge selection takes the actor's own rows and their derived rows
key retirement is a separate key:revocation:v1 under this section's paths; the root's quorum has no path over a key it does not own; an ownerless key stays registered and inert
entities are removed by revocation:{entity_type}:{reason}; bytes by the bytes-plane tombstone
revocation:*, key:revocation:v1, moderation:*, moderation_track_record:*, slashing:* and hard_case:* rows are never purgeable, by the root or by anyone
an equivocation proof or liveness transition is withdrawn only by the substrate that produced it under rule 1, or recanted if false; nobody else removes it
a structural composer is purged only together with its target; a delegates_to only when a party to it is in the selection
a scores row whose evidence was never admissible input is purged with its evidence, with a trace's trace:complete:v1 and a purged holding claim's bytes, transitively over evidence_refs
a score over real evidence later taken down on a legal basis stands; its evidence_refs resolve to the tombstone
the door refuses a purge without the notice (purge_unauthorised) and one whose selection digest differs from the authorised one (purge_selection_digest_mismatch)
every purged id is appended to a ledger attested at the next tag
the substrate SHOULD record which admission rule (0 to 4) admitted each withdraws in row metadata
subject authority does not extend to recants; only the original attester recants their own claim
a subject who holds a producer's claim factually wrong rebuts by scores with negative polarity on a contradicting dimension, not by revocation
The signer of a row a named party withdrew may keep the row and its withdrawal together at self scope
A node must not serve the signer's kept copy of a withdrawn row to anyone, the former audience included; it counts toward no score, standing or grant
The signer may hand a withdrawn row and its withdrawal to a party with a duty to judge it: a named moderator, or a body under a declared legal-weight class
Saying a withdrawn statement again to the audience is a new row the named party may withdraw in turn
The signer's keep gives way to every duty to delete: a committed deletion window, an affiliation's retention and erasure limbs, a decay protocol the signer runs
a framework claim names its source of authority by delegates_to against a framework key with scope naming the principle, not by a grounding prefix
a delegates_to with delegation_purpose owner_binding defines the self cohort; at most one is live per owned key and the substrate rejects a second distinct-owner binding at bind time
owner_binding is the one single-valued delegation_purpose; act-on-behalf, hierarchy and authority-source delegations are multi-parent DAGs
a licence is given by an authority
a grant is given by the asset's owner or steward
a delegation is given by a principal over the principal's own powers
a licence ends by the authority revoking or suspending it
a grant ends by rotation, expiry or exhaustion
a delegation ends by the principal withdrawing it, or by attenuation
only delegation chains, attenuated, depth-capped and revocable per link; a licence does not chain and a grant does not chain
wire discriminators: licensure is a licensure:{authority_id} scores dimension; a grant is subject_kind key_grant or consent:scope:*; delegation is attestation_type delegates_to
only delegates_to gets a graph walk, with depth cap, cycle rejection and aggregate-weight cap
holding a licence confers no power to issue one; receiving a grant confers no power to re-grant; neither is walked transitively
a licence's provenance is its authority_id inside the dimension, conferred by the authority's quorum, never by delegates_to
who grants the licence, who vouches for the attester (trust walk), and external legal force (a bridge) are kept distinct; bridges compose with the record, never replace it
anyone may be a licensing authority; authority_id names a key, an organisation or an affiliation resolving through its membership seats and hierarchy edges
X holds licence authority for A iff X's key is A or X holds a license-scoped delegation whose chain resolves to A
there is no roster of permitted authorities and a substrate checks none; a licensure:{A} row admits under the general gate, reaching a reader only by trust or consent
a Sovereign key scoring licensure:{A} is wire-identical to a steward scoring it; consumer policy weights by attester
by quorum describes a collective authority's own governance (founder quorum, M-of-N write rule), never an admission gate applied to another's authority
the licensure:{A} status set folds only rows whose emitter resolves to A; other rows are testimony about A's licensure, outside the fold, composed at consumer confidence
an issuance whose license delegator chain does not resolve to A is refused licensure_delegator_not_authority
there is no bootstrap: A's first licensure:{A} row is signed by A, or for a keyless affiliation cosigned by its quorum
licence authority is judged at the row's signed asserted_at, never at receipt; a later withdraws of a chain link stops future issuance and does not reclassify issued licences
a licence has no public default; its cohort_scope is the authority's declared choice per licence class in the affiliation's charter, the smallest that fits
licence and authority head travel together; where not public they are re-emitted as new cosigned rows naming validating readers in subject_key_ids, never at the wrong scope or by roster widening

an organisation-named authority is its community_key_id; a licensure:{community_key_id} row is cosigned under the affiliation's current consensus_protocol, the protocol source being the authority in the dimension
a license-scoped chain roots at the affiliation's quorum; one founder suffices only where the protocol says so
a key_grant conveys access, not the power to convey it; an onward grant is a new grant by the owner, steward or a grant-scoped delegate, never a forwarded one
rotation_chain on a grant is supersession lineage, not onward transfer
possession of the DEK (every recipient has it) is necessary and never sufficient to issue a grant
a substrate MUST refuse at admission a key_grant whose issuer neither owns nor stewards the asset nor holds a grant-scoped delegation over it
consumer policy may apply different trust adjustments to attesters who recant versus those who withdraw
every claim about an entity, by any attester, is a scores attestation on a named dimension; scores is the one workhorse
the signed object is attestation_envelope with the row mirror and asserted_at; an optional member is omitted, never null
a claim's validity in time is asserted_at plus optional valid_until, composed by the consumer with the substrate's expires_at
reversibility is rollbackable or non-rollbackable, by consumer policy plus the per-prefix rule
scope is one of self, family, community, affiliations, species, biosphere, federation
The grammar has exactly five wire primitives: one workhorse and four composers; nothing more
Verdicts are composed by consumers under CC 4.4 policy; the wire format prescribes no verdict
Every party (producer, substrate, relay, consumer) preserves exactly the members the producer signed; no party materializes or strips defaults
Canonical bytes are computed over the literal envelope members the producer signs
Optional fields the producer omits are never materialized into canonical bytes by any party
Optional fields the producer emits, even at default value, are preserved in canonical bytes by every party
Documented defaults apply at interpretation time, not encoding time
A consumer reads an absent epistemic_mode as direct; omitted and explicit-default encodings verify under their own bytes and are semantically equivalent
A substrate, relay or consumer that re-stores or forwards a row preserves member presence and absence exactly as signed
A relay never strips an explicitly emitted default member
A relay never materializes an omitted default member
A relay forwards canonical octets as received; one that re-serializes emits JCS member order and changes nothing else; presence and absence stay fixed
Unknown fields are preserved on read and re-emission; the same preservation extends to known optional fields
Set-semantics array elements are sorted lexicographically by JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order) before signing
subject_key_ids[] and delegates_to.scope[] are set-semantics arrays and are sorted
transport_destination.aspects[], key_grant.rotation_chain and evidence_refs[] are sequence-semantics and keep authored order
A field's definition declares set or sequence kind; absent a declaration the array is set-semantics (sorted)
A substrate refuses an out-of-order set array with federation_set_semantics_unsorted naming the member and never re-sorts it
A set-kind array is sorted and unique; a duplicate element is refused federation_set_semantics_unsorted
An optional member is unset by absence never null; explicit JSON null is refused federation_malformed_row reason envelope_member_null
The key plane revocation_envelope binds its absent optionals as explicit null (the one exception to the no-null rule)
Where this document writes a default as null it means absent
Every byte field's string encoding is pinned; hashes and raw key material (public keys, destination_hash, root_hash, digests, fingerprints) are lowercase hex, never base64 in canonical bytes
note: tension with 725: pubkey_ed25519_base64 carries a public key as base64 (452 allows documented base64 fields)

gist: Fields explicitly documented as base64 use base64; the default for any key, hash or id byte field is lowercase hex
A subject_key_ids element naming a registered key carries the key_id string verbatim (label-fingerprint form or an older 64-hex id); the hex rule does not re-encode it
A canonical-hash subject element is the tagged canonical:{hashalg}:{hex} string; the untagged bare-hex spelling is refused at the gate
The canonical: prefix is a tagged-union discriminator exempt from the no-separators hex rule; only the {hex} segment is governed by 2.6.3
Every base64 field uses the RFC 4648 section 4 standard alphabet, with padding, no whitespace or newlines
The vector set includes a base64-variant round-trip case across two independent encoders
Every datetime field is the 2.6.2 canonical string: UTC literal Z, exactly three fractional digits
The cross-implementation JCS vector set covers a set-vs-sequence array case, a hex-vs-base64 byte case and a timestamp case
The omit-vs-materialize rule applies uniformly to every optional CC 2.1 envelope field
row.subject_key_ids is always present in the mirror ([] when no subject); the column beside the row is absent when empty
session_id and claimed_at are required on session:* rows
custody_state is required on a custody report; admission refuses one without it
group_kind and expires_at are required on a membership proposal; admission refuses one without them
proposal_hash is required on a membership answer; admission refuses one without it
attached_head_digest is required on a new trust:accepts:v1 edge; one without it is refused; an edge admitted before the requirement stays valid
attach_window_secs absent means no attach window; attach by out-of-band anchor only
witness_cadence_secs, witness_quorum and witnesses are required on a witnessed lineage's charter; absent, the lineage is unwitnessed for T6
halt_fuse_secs defaults to the constant 86400 when absent; an explicit value overrides
recovery_commitments is required on the accord's charter; absent, no holder can self-rotate and recovery is a roster change
family_id is required iff cohort_scope is family; admission rejects a family-scoped row without it
community_id is required iff cohort_scope is community or affiliations; admission rejects such a row without it
delivery_mode defaults to pull and history_on_join to from_join when absent
family_id and community_id are conditional-required, not optional-with-default; the substrate rejects a mis-shaped row
Envelope signing bytes are computed by JCS (RFC 8785): sorted members, no whitespace, UTF-8, RFC 8259 escaping, ES6 number rule
A conforming producer computes signing bytes as JCS over attestation_envelope
A conforming consumer recomputes signing bytes by the same JCS rule to verify a signature
A conforming substrate preserves the as-received envelope object for relay; it may store a parsed form alongside
The canonical-bytes contract is the as-received object's member set and values; insignificant whitespace and member order are outside the contract
A signed redaction marker that distinguishes authorized redaction from tampering is excluded as a design
A future redaction scheme lives on the envelope plane, declares its own redactability in the signed object, sits above whole-row hashing, or is a different object kind
The integrity gate is original_content_hash at ingest; persist_row_hash is never re-verified on read
A producer coerces every number to its finite IEEE-754 double before JCS and rejects with a hard error any number with no finite double
The JCS vector set includes a non-representable-number case asserted to reject under default and arbitrary-precision parsers
An envelope's JCS bytes never exceed 1 MiB; a producer does not emit above it; a substrate rejects at every write path with ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE (413)
Above the cap the payload moves to the blob plane as encrypted chunks replicated to the owner's chosen holder count, and the envelope names it by content hash in evidence_refs
A content hash resolves via custody:ack here rows plus ContentFetch in Commons scope; in a bounded cohort the holding claim never leaves the cohort and resolves only to admitted members
The blob-plane relocation adds no envelope field and no primitive; the 1+4 surface is untouched
The freeze-gate vector set includes an at-cap envelope that admits and a cap-plus-one envelope that rejects ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE
The contract bound |JCS(envelope)| <= 1 MiB is decided after parse; producer never emits above, substrate rejects above with ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE
Every write path enforces a finite intake ceiling on buffered octets from an untrusted source and refuses at it without completing the parse, with ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE / 413
The intake ceiling is a deployment parameter never set below 1 MiB; a deployment should publish it
A party transmitting an inflated non-canonical serialization may have it refused by a receiver's intake ceiling; that refusal is conformant
A signature is verified over JCS(envelope) by the hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 path
Defaults are applied to absent members only after verification; the object and signature are stored and forwarded as received
A relay preserves member presence and absence exactly and forwards as-received bytes; defaults are applied after signature verification
JCS is the only encoding; no new encoding format is introduced
Defaults still apply at interpretation time
Prior emissions that omitted or explicitly emitted defaults remain valid; only relay-time mutation of presence or absence is prohibited
The signed-object table, CDDL and JSON are rendered from one data file and never disagree; the data is the source
The signed object of an attestation row is the one JSON object attestation_envelope; the signing input is JCS(attestation_envelope) and nothing else
The row's signature members, every cosignature and every column beside the row are outside the signed bytes; a cosignature is never inside the bytes it signs
Seven columns are mirrored inside the bytes under row, a closed set; no mirror is refused envelope_member_missing; a column disagreeing with its mirror is refused typed_diverges_from_envelope
asserted_at and expires_at ride inside the signed bytes; the columns beside the row are read back out of them
The classical half verifies against attesting_key_id's Ed25519 key over the signing input; the PQ half over signing input plus raw Ed25519 signature; at federation tier both verify or refused
original_content_hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the signing input and is recomputed at ingest
A second signer over the same bytes is an additional_scrubs[] entry beside the row, verified against its own key
A JCS image above 1 MiB is refused ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE

A shape refusal is federation_malformed_row with one reason from the closed set: envelope_member_missing, envelope_member_invalid, envelope_member_null, typed_diverges_from_envelope, envelope_row_member_unknown, content_hash_mismatch, subject_key_id_malformed
A withdraws meeting no rule of 2.4.1.1 is refused federation_withdraws_not_admitted

A set out of order or with a duplicate is refused federation_set_semantics_unsorted; a type outside the five is attestation_type_unregistered; a failed signature half is SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILED; over the cap is ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE
An array's kind is set (sorted by JCS string before signing) or sequence (as authored)
row.attestation_id is required: a UUID minted by the stamper before the bytes exist; composers reference it
row.attesting_key_id is required and is the signer; the row's signature verifies against this key's pinned Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 keys; no separate signer slot
row.attestation_type is required, one of the five byte-compared; anything else refused attestation_type_unregistered
row.attested_key_id is required and defaults to the attester at the mint (a self-claim)
row.subject_key_ids is required, may be empty, always present in the mirror; elements are a key_id verbatim or tagged canonical form; uppercase, whitespace, disorder or duplicates refused
row.cohort_scope is required, a closed set of seven, no wire default; the authoring default is the smallest scope
cohort_scope is the one mirror member a placement-touching re-sign may narrow; it may never be re-authored
row.weight is optional, absent in the mirror iff the column is NULL; a non-finite value is refused at the stamp rather than serialised as null
row is required and closed; an eighth member is refused; no mirror refused envelope_member_missing; disagreement refused typed_diverges_from_envelope
asserted_at is required, stamped at the mint to the millisecond; the column is read back from this member, never a second clock; receiver-clock judged only where 2.6.7 says
expires_at is present in the bytes iff the column is set; any other pairing is refused
expires_at is required on census:share and census:member:share rows as the period's end; census_return_expired after it
dimension is required on every row type and is resolved through the namespace registry on all five
references_attestation_id is required on supersedes, withdraws and recants, naming the prior row; read only with the row type as discriminator (three readings); a fourth reading is a separate member
scope is required on consent:state:granted and on delegates_to; the emitter writes an array; a bare token is admitted as the one-element array; admission normalises nothing in the bytes
note: table; 480 catalogs scope as optional with default absent

gist: pre_rotation_commitment is optional on a charter
recovers and successor_keys are required on a charter recovery (predecessor root and the pre-committed successor set)
withdrawal_reason is optional on withdraws
consent_supersedes on consent:state:* names the prior consent statement replaced; it is separate from references_attestation_id
delivery_mode is optional, default pull; the recipient-receive axis
deletion_window is the deadline by which a consented payload must be deleted
media is optional, kept as JSON and validated at the door
widened_at is required on a widening supersedes and absent otherwise; asserted_at on a widening is the claim's own instant carried verbatim
accord_root is required on accord:* rows; a foreign row carrying junk fails closed at the fold
attach_window_secs is optional on trust:charter:v1 (absent = anchor only)
witness_cadence_secs is required on a witnessed lineage's charter
witness_quorum is required on a witnessed charter: floor(|witnesses|/2)+1 and at least 2, or 0 (witnessed mode off)
attached_head_digest is required on trust:accepts:v1: the lineage head the acceptance attaches on
recovery_commitments is required on the accord's charter: holder key id to commitment
for_key_id is required on census share rows; held only by author's and recipient's nodes; served to that key only, no widening; others refuse federation_addressed_not_recipient
period is required on census share, partial, composite, tally and expected_active rows: the period index on the global cadence
return_token is required on census share rows: H(node_secret || period), never a node id
share_index is required on share and partial rows, 0 or 1; any other value is census_share_index_invalid
share_count is required on partials; both partials of a period must agree
source_count is required on composite and tally; below 10 the cell is refused census_composite_below_k
n_eff is required on composite and tally; aggregation_meta_dominated when below half of source_count
max_source_multiplicity is required on composite and tally; aggregation_meta_multiplicity above the floor
mass_commitment_hex is required on composite and tally: Merkle root over per-member masses
member_commitment_hex is required on partial, composite, tally and expected_active; both partials of a period carry the same root
mass_total is required on partial, composite and tally; on a composite it equals source_count and the sum of the partials, else census_composite_mass_total_mismatch / partials_mismatch
aggregation_algorithm_id is required on partial, composite and tally; noise_floor_descriptor optional on composite and tally
version is required on composite and tally and equals 3; a lower value is refused
partial_a and partial_b are required on composite and tally, naming the two partials; references_attestation_id stays unset on a composite
window_periods is required on census:expected_active and equals 4: a member is expected-active when active in one of the last four periods
active_count and floor_applied are required on census:expected_active; every member recomputes active_count, else census_expected_active_mismatch
score is required on scores, in [-1,1]; the family's polarity class is an admission rule
confidence is required on scores, in [0,1]
context is optional free form, not parsed by the substrate
evidence_refs is optional (some families require it), a sequence in producer order; above the cap the payload is named here by content hash
valid_until is optional consumer-policy staleness, independent of expires_at
epistemic_mode is optional, read as direct when absent; an explicit default is signed as written
witness_relation is optional, read as external; oversight_mode optional (per-cell default); explicit null refused
occurrence_id, occurrence_count (at least 1) and occurrence_role are optional, read as occurrence-0, 1 and primary; occurrence_id self-asserted
stake is optional, read as reputational
community_id is required iff cohort_scope is community or affiliations and is the community whose roster gates visibility; refused when missing
family_id is required iff cohort_scope is family
session_id (verbatim, case-preserved) and claimed_at are required on session:*
custody_state is required on custody:ack, here or none; refused custody_ack_malformed otherwise
group_kind is required on membership:proposal; role optional on proposal and restated on acceptance
proposal_hash is required on membership:acceptance and decline: the answered proposal's original_content_hash
subject_sha256_ed25519_raw is optional on moderation:*; refused moderation_subject_digest_malformed when malformed
halt_fuse_secs is optional on the accord's charter; the halt latch reads the constant 86400 when absent
witnesses is required on a witnessed lineage's charter, a set sorted by JCS string
history_on_join is optional, default from_join
supersession_reason and differs_in are optional on supersedes; differs_in lists differing member names and a widening lists cohort_scope; differs_in is a sorted set
recantation_reason and what_was_false are optional on recants
delegation_purpose is optional on delegates_to; owner_binding is the one single-valued purpose
delegation_valid_from is optional on delegates_to, defaulting to the edge's asserted_at
delegation_valid_until is required on a termed delegates_to, at most 365 days after delegation_valid_from, else refused delegation_term_required
trust_classes on a delegates_to bearing trust:accepts is optional, non-empty when present; [] refused trust_accepts_classes_malformed; absent means every class the charter declares
trust_depth on a trust:accepts delegation is 0..5 (absent = 0); out of range refused trust_accepts_depth_out_of_range
Every other member, including subject_kind and per-family payloads, rides the envelope untyped by the substrate, is preserved on relay, and is validated by its family at the gate
consent_basis is an optional sequence on capacity:* and observation:access_assumption:v1 naming the grants a witness relied on
n_eff_pr, n_eff_h, sample_size, feature_dim, sample_size_gate, target_n_eff, min_feature_dim, n_eff_floor and window are optional on capacity:* and validated at the capacity gate
trace_level, occurrence_key_ids, window_from, window_to and channel_classes are required on observation:access_assumption:v1
amendment_digest and authorized_by are required on identity_amendment:v1; authorized_by names the deferral:response:approved row and admission checks it

Each beside column (attestation_id, attesting_key_id, attested_key_id, attestation_type, weight, asserted_at, expires_at, subject_key_ids, cohort_scope) equals its signed mirror or the row is refused typed_diverges_from_envelope
Beside expires_at is present iff the signed member is; beside subject_key_ids and weight are absent when empty or NULL
attestation_envelope is required beside the row, stored and relayed as received; the signing input is JCS of it and nothing else
original_content_hash is required: lowercase hex SHA-256 of JCS(attestation_envelope), recomputed at federation-tier ingest and refused on mismatch
additional_scrubs holds second and later signers over the same JCS bytes, each verified against its own key; it is the carrier of quorum on a row
persist_row_hash is store-computed over the row's own serialisation, informational on the wire, never re-verified on read, not a conformance target
withdraws_admission_rule is persist-internal audit metadata recording which rule (0-4) admitted a withdraws
tier and promoted_at are persist-internal, absent on the wire for a federation row and outside the signed bytes, so a promoted row is byte-identical to a native one
scrub_signature_classical is required: Ed25519 over JCS(attestation_envelope), base64 standard alphabet padded
scrub_signature_pqc is required at the federation tier: ML-DSA-65 over JCS bytes followed by the raw Ed25519 signature; verified under strict hybrid, never classical-only
scrub_key_id on an attestation row names the same key as attesting_key_id; on a key record it may name an anchor
scrub_timestamp is required and is asserted_at, or widened_at on a widening; outside the bytes; pqc_completed_at optional, outside the bytes
A cosign entry carries scrub_key_id resolving to a registered key, Ed25519 over the same JCS bytes, and at federation tier ML-DSA-65 over those bytes plus its Ed25519 signature
cosigned_at is optional on a cosign entry and outside every preimage, so stamping it moves no signed byte
key_id is required: label-fingerprint, the fingerprint the first ten lowercase base32 characters of sha256(ed25519 public key)
pubkey_ed25519_base64 (raw 32 bytes) is required on a key record; pubkey_ml_dsa_65_base64 (raw 1952 bytes) required for algorithm hybrid
The substrate takes key record writes only at algorithm hybrid; algorithm is hybrid on every admitted record
identity_type (a set rendered as one string), identity_ref and valid_from are required on a key record
valid_until is optional on a key record; its signed twin is inside registration_envelope
registration_envelope is the key record's signed object; JCS(registration_envelope) is the signing input for the base scrub and every additional scrub; its member table is the key plane's
A key record's original_content_hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of JCS(registration_envelope)
A key record's scrub_signature_classical is Ed25519 over JCS(registration_envelope); scrub_signature_pqc is ML-DSA-65 over that followed by the Ed25519 bytes, required once hybrid-complete
note: 735 'once hybrid-complete' vs 726/727 writes taken only at hybrid: is a classical-only record ever admitted?

gist: A key record's scrub_signature_classical is Ed25519 over JCS(registration_envelope); scrub_signature_pqc is ML-DSA-65 over that plus the Ed25519 bytes, required once hybrid-complete
scrub_timestamp is required on a key record; pqc_completed_at optional
A key record's persist_row_hash is required, store-computed, excludes itself and consent_role, informational
roles is an optional set beside the key record and is also carried inside the signed registration_envelope
attestation_evidence (hardware attestation blob) is optional on a key record
consent_role is a mutable persist-local marker excluded from persist_row_hash and from the signed bytes
additional_scrubs on a key record are second and later scrubs over the same JCS(registration_envelope), letting a replicated record prove its own m-of-n
A set-kind array is sorted and unique, refused federation_set_semantics_unsorted with the member named; a relay never re-sorts it
The emitter's form for scope is the array; a bare token is admitted as the one-element array; nothing is normalised in signed bytes
An explicit JSON null on an optional member is refused as malformed
The quorum carrier is additional_scrubs[] beside the row; witnesses[] is a set
The signed-object vectors' JCS bytes, hashes and Ed25519 half are recomputed on every change to this document; the signatures verify under the identities the file carries
A second implementation that reproduces the vector bytes and signatures has met the byte-identity target for the signed object
The v62 signed object is a CBOR object signed with COSE (signed_object_v2.cddl); the JSON object stays the signed object of earlier candidates and verifies as itself for ever
A row is one COSE_Sign1 with one signer; type, family, author key id, issuer and subject ride the protected header; nothing is written beside and again inside
A quorum is one statement per signer over the same payload, found by the quorum key (payload digest); additional_scrubs ends; a fold counts statements by person
Canonical bytes are CBOR deterministic encoding; a verifier verifies the bytes it received, never a re-encoding of typed fields
The statement id is the hash-agile digest of a labelled structure of protected header and payload with the signature excluded; one statement has one id whatever its signature
A low-entropy statement (a ballot, a census cell) carries a random salt as a payload member bound by every signer, so neither its id nor quorum key confirms a guess
The hybrid is the IETF composite ML-DSA-65 with Ed25519 construction signing a domain-separated representative binding both halves, under a private-use algorithm identifier until one is assigned
Each key is one composite COSE key; its id is its RFC 9679 thumbprint, rotating with the key; a person's stable reference is the genesis key thumbprint as issuer
Instants are integer POSIX milliseconds in the envelope and standard seconds claims in the header, derived by a fixed rule, never floats
Free text leaves the envelope: context becomes a bounded body note, every envelope member is bounded, and a reason code from a closed registry may stand in the envelope
Erasability is minted, never retrofitted: a blinded member is absent from the payload and is a salted disclosure; the payload carries every disclosure digest; erasure drops a disclosure
A disclosure set is bytes, not a row member: statements replicate with commitment and without disclosures; the set is fetched under the audience's consent edge; erasure is the bytes-plane tombstone
Which members are blind is a family-model column checked at vendoring; a row sealing a member its family blinds is refused; no fold or admission reads a blindable member
A family whose erasure route is subject request or purge mints every free-text or other-authored member as blinded, body.note first; identifiers, instants, references and digests stay sealed
A family whose erasure route is none or legal hold seals its members; its body.note is bounded and carries nothing a subject request could reach
Receipts over the provenance log and stream logs are COSE receipts over the RFC 9162 tree; published roots stay valid; each witness issues its own receipt; stream receipts cover batches
The view and queue of 4.5.13 are unchanged; the per-chunk media trailer stays a raw signature over fixed big-endian fields and its preimage never parses as COSE
One hybrid KEM, X-Wing, serves every key wrap and onion hop, under HPKE where a wrap is single-shot; the transit handshake is KEM-authenticated with X-Wing inside
Every attestation-plane preimage moves; every other signed thing except the chunk trailer becomes a COSE object with its own typ; no hand-laid or little-endian layout remains
There is no transparency service and no registrar; a trust decides what a node serves and no party stands in the middle
