Emission switches at the edition's ceremony once every node reads both forms; the genesis is re-signed once; a release reading both and writing the old form is the pre-switch candidate
Receipts and custody acks signed by others are never re-signed; earlier forms verify for ever; a verifier chooses by kind and edition; the earlier form is accepted only before cutover
A row's anchor is its provenance-log position, never a signer-chosen instant; cutover is the first new-edition statement's position; earlier-form receipts accepted at or below that tree size
A node of the new candidate reads both objects and writes one; a node of an earlier candidate reads only its own
A release candidate may move signed bytes while it says so and re-signs; the MAJOR rule binds from 1.0
Every datetime is UTC with uppercase literal Z (never +00:00, never lowercase z) at exactly millisecond precision: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ
Producers emit the canonical datetime form; consumers reject any other form when verifying a signature
note: beside columns at 699/714 are typed rfc3339 not rfc3339-ms; whether 2.6.2 binds them is unstated

gist: Every hex string in canonical bytes is lowercase, unpadded (no 0x, no separators) and byte-length-exact; producers emit lowercase, consumers reject uppercase when verifying

A MAJOR version is any wire-incompatible change: envelope field removal or semantic change, primitive removal, domain-separation label change, prefix removal or breaking redefinition, reservation change, conformance-language change

A MINOR version is a wire-compatible addition (new prefix, new envelope field with documented default, new policy, new endpoint, new optional conformance subsection); existing producers and consumers keep interoperating unmodified
A PATCH version is clarification, editorial fix or addition to non-normative sections
The wire surface is frozen at 1.0; a release candidate ordinarily adds under MINOR and PATCH and moves no signed byte
A candidate that must move signed bytes before 1.0 says so in its text, keeps every row signed under the earlier form verifying as itself, and re-signs the genesis once

A MAJOR version is any wire-incompatible change: envelope field removal or semantic change, primitive removal, label change, prefix removal or redefinition, reservation change, conformance-language change
A removal notice names the noticing version and a removal target; an element under notice stays interoperable until that version; removal is MAJOR
The wire vocabulary (manifests/WIRE_VOCABULARY.md) is a ratified, versioned, hash-addressable artifact governed in two tiers
A Tier-1 message type addition (canonicalization load-bearing to an ethical primitive) rides the CC 4.5.1 amendment, a working reference implementation and a coordinated cut
Tier-2 app channels use OpaqueRequest/OpaqueResponse/OpaqueEvent carrying a kind from a reserved per-repo range delegated to the range steward; no amendment is needed to define a kind
Every ratifying repo pins the wire vocabulary's SHA-256 at build; a hash mismatch at cohabitation is a build failure, not a warning
Wire-vocabulary amendment is substrate-coordinated across ratifying repos; unanimous hash-commit blocks the cut, never the decision
Implementations conform to the normatively cited documents where referenced inline
RFC 9162 is used for new transparency-log integrations; older RFC 6962 instances continue to interoperate
The streaming epoch-key rekey conforms to MLS TreeKEM; the per-frame chunk seal conforms to the SFrame model
A Tier-2 app channel uses OpaqueRequest/Response/Event carrying a kind from a reserved per-repo range delegated to the range steward; no amendment needed to define a kind
Geographic primitives use H3 as the canonical cell-identifier encoding
cell_id is a 15-character lowercase hex string without 0x, leading zeros preserved
A decoder extracts a cell's resolution via the H3 library (bits 52-55), not from the high nibble, which is the mode marker
cell_resolution is an integer in [0,15] equal to the resolution decoded from cell_id; the substrate verifies on admission and rejects a mismatched pair as malformed
A location_proof contribution carries cell_resolution <= 7; a finer one is rejected at the substrate gate
The substrate emits hard_case:location_proof_resolution_violation when it rejects an over-fine location_proof
Cell C is contained in cell B iff C's resolution is at least B's and the H3 parent walk from C reaches exactly B
For membership admission to a geographic community a location_proof's cell_id is contained within the community's geographic_constraint.cell_id
Operator-internal use of other geospatial systems is unconstrained; the wire format uses H3
The rough-only bound applies to location_proof, not to community definitions; a community may scope at any resolution; one finer than 7 admits nobody by containment and admits by invitation
Every signed_at, asserted_at, valid_until, delegation_valid_from/until and cosigned_at is wall-clock UTC at the asserting peer's clock
Producers synchronize clocks via NTPv4 or Roughtime to a known-good source
Maximum tolerated attester-consumer skew for a freshness check is +-5 minutes by default; tighter thresholds may be applied by consumer policy
A consumer rejects as malformed an attestation whose asserted_at is more than 5 minutes in the future
A cosignature on an STH whose signed_at is more than 5 minutes from the STH's signed_at is rejected
For a row with future valid_until, freshness holds when valid_until is unreached and the consumer clock is within 5 minutes of network consensus; a drifted consumer rejects
A row whose admission walks a delegates_to chain (key wrap, consent, licence, deferral response, epoch-axis membership) is judged at its signed asserted_at
The substrate refuses a chain-judged row whose asserted_at precedes the receiver's clock by more than W = 72 hours with asserted_at_stale; well-formed, not admitted-as-stale; the remedy is re-signing
A cosigned roster event is bound signature by signature; a signer who has since left counts only inside W
Rows not judged on a chain (traces, scores on the base) are not bound by W; the 5-minute future bound still applies
FedCode is the one human-shareable shorthand for a key_id; every implementation renders and parses the same code for the same key
FedCode is a deterministic render of an existing key_id, not a new envelope field; its kind byte is a payload discriminator; resolution is DNS-free
CIRISVerify is the FedCode reference implementation; every other component decodes through it
FedCode kinds are 1=user 2=agent 3=node 4=family 5=community, mapping 1:1 onto identity_type; NodeCode v1 is kind node
A user code with no nodes resolves through the federation directory by walking nodes_owned_by(U); a code carrying nodes resolves with no directory
nodes_owned_by is the exact inverse of owner_of, held by construction
A peer outside U's self cohort holds only U's federation-scoped owner-bindings, so a directory walk yields exactly the announced roster; U's own nodes see every binding
A node whose owner resolves ambiguous is skipped in the walk, not fatal; a direct query about that node still fails closed

FedCode wire form: binary payload, CRC-16-CCITT (0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no final xor) 2 bytes big-endian, RFC 4648 base32 unpadded, version prefix, 4-character dash groups for display; QR form ungrouped
Decoders normalize (drop whitespace, upper-case, strip dashes) and accept the undashed prefix; length-prefixed fields are 1-byte length, at most 255 UTF-8 bytes; overflow is malformed

v2 payload: version 0x02, kind, sha256(key_id), ed25519 pubkey, LP(key_id), transport/alias/group hints; v3 adds node_count (0..16), per-node LP(key_id) + transport key, then a presence-tagged PQC commitment
A decoder verifies the payload's sha256(key_id) against the key_id; the v1 layout is retained unchanged under CIRIS-V1-
Every FedCode constraint is enforced at both encoder and decoder
An embedded node key is the node's transport Ed25519, never a federation key; a code whose embedded transport key equals the owner's pubkey is rejected
Only kind=user may embed nodes; a code never carries group-scoped material or an anonymous-tier identity; it may carry an unannounced node's destination handed by the owner
node_count <= 16 and total payload <= 1024 bytes before base32
A code with no nodes and no commitment encodes as v2 byte-identically; only a non-empty tail emits CIRIS-V3-
v1 decodes as kind node; v2 decodes unchanged; a v3 decoder accepts all three prefixes; a v2-only decoder rejects CIRIS-V3- outright
The substrate takes federation_keys writes only at algorithm hybrid
A host admitting a code's key takes the classical half plus the sha256(ML-DSA-65 pubkey) commitment, fetches the body by Key Pull and verifies it before writing a hybrid record
The PQC commitment applies to any kind of code, is presence-tagged and last, and its API form is exactly 64 lowercase hex, rejected never repaired
A FedCode is unsigned; a commitment match is never treated as authentication of the identity; a code with no commitment fails closed at the pull check
key_id = label-fingerprint; fingerprint is the first 10 lowercase base32 characters of sha256(ed25519_pubkey); label is lowercased [a-z0-9-] and cosmetic
A registrar refuses a second key under an already-registered key_id
A consumer resolving a key_id verifies the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains
A deployment expecting more than 2^16 identities under one label raises the fingerprint to 16 characters
Owner-binding is a user-signed delegates_to; a node cannot make itself owned by reading a pubkey
A node configured with its owner's usercode self-registers as a pending identity_occurrence of U, trust-and-serve only until U's hardware-rooted key signs delegates_to(U -> node)
A usercode embedding a pre-authorized signed delegation is not the default; if ever added it is expiring, scope-limited, revocable, and by amendment
BCP 14 key words bind only when they appear in all capitals

The normative surface is the wire format and conformance surface (primitives, envelope fields, namespace, canonicalization, precedence, reservations, policies, endpoints, keyworded statements); conformance is judged against nothing else
Informative framing adds no conformance obligation; an implementer who rejects the philosophy but is wire-correct conforms
Where framing has a wire consequence it is restated as a normative rule in its own section; keywords and the 1.7 surface govern and informative prose never overrides them
Each dimension family is registered once, under one owning component that commits to it.
The generated registry manifest is the count of record for families; a count restated in prose is never read as authoritative.
Owning components commit to their families in their own mission statements; CIRISBench is catalogued without one.
When a component folds into another repo the catalogue row's owning_repo follows the fold; the row stays.
licensure authority_id is the licence's provenance; status vocabulary is open with canonical values issued, probation, restricted, suspended, revoked, lapsed, surrendered, reduced.
A consumer MUST honour that suspended is reversible and revoked is terminal, and MUST NOT infer one status from the other.
More than one licensure status MAY be live at once; a consumer composes the set rather than reading a scalar.
licensure is open-emitter; co-stewardship with Verify for the CIRIS licence is composition, not a reservation.
duty kind is open vocabulary with ODRL 2.2 canonical kinds; a duty states an obligation attached to a permission.
A duty's discharge is evidenced by commitment_fulfillment rows, never by a second family.
A duty breach routes to hard_case:duty_unmet for adjudication, never to automatic slashing.
duty rides scores; no new structural primitive.
partner_role role values are the six listed, lowercase per R3.
Dimension vocabulary is lowercase (R3).
revocation entity_type is agent, partner or license.
An entity revocation is immediate and non-rollbackable.
A posted bond is forfeited on revocation.
A registered build manifest is the precondition for an L4 (license_validity) attestation.
multilateral_participation kind is membership, voting, proposal_filing or observer_status; forum is a named body.
agent_files attestations by the accord-conferred, human-held steward keys of ciris-canonical constitute the CIRIS canonical default-trust state; never the installs' keys.
agent_files is an open Contribution channel; a consumer composes trust over it through the 4.4.3.7 trust layers, with the install anti-tricking guarantee.
ownership:responsible_party:node:v1 names the single live responsible steward of an owned node or agent key; cardinality other than 1 is an error, not a set to reduce.
The ownership score mirrors, never replaces, the delegates_to owner_binding of 3.2; reclaim and seizure ride the 3.2 recovery path.
ownership:* is reserved per 3.4.5.
device:label is signed by the owner about an identity occurrence the owner holds.
device:label sits at cohort_scope self only; it never leaves the owner's self cohort.
device:label is a scores row carrying the device's name in the envelope label.
A device rename is a supersedes of the previous device:label row; the newest wins.
device:label is display text: it confers nothing and no gate reads it.
The device: stem is closed to the one leaf device:label.
A takedown notice is a scores row whose envelope is the takedown_notice payload, subject_kind takedown_notice, so every notice has an attestation_id.
A tombstone cites the notice's attestation_id and a reconsideration row targets it.
takedown_notice basis is the closed LegalBasis set (dmca512 ... steward_purge).
A steward_purge notice is a cosigned row: any seat proposes as attesting_key_id, other seats ride in additional_scrubs over the same bytes, quorum evaluated under the root's consensus_protocol.
The steward_purge family derived from the verified signers MUST resolve to the claimant_key_id root.
A steward purge's signing payload is the takedown_notice row's canonical bytes.
The takedown_notice: stem is closed to this family.
For the legal bases a takedown_notice is signed by the duty holder under the 4.5.5 enforced-admission rule; steward_purge is cosigned by the trust root.
community:listing is a federation-scoped scores row for a public community.
community:listing carries name, description, cohort_subkind, admission policy, named moderator and community_key_id; wire community:listing:v1.
A roster is never enumerable outside its cohort; a listing names no roster and there is no member-level listing.
A community rename or policy change is a supersedes of the listing; one live row per community.
Closing a community is a withdraws of its listing.
The community: stem is closed to the listing leaf.
community:listing is signed by the founder or a current moderate-holder of the community it names.
trust:{job} edges are dimension values carried on delegates_to rows; the wire type is unchanged.
Three trust jobs named apart (charter root self-declaration, confers root-to-subject grant, accepts node-to-root acceptance); a reader never infers one from another.
A trust edge is retracted by withdraws or recants, never by a negative score.
trust:* is reserved per 3.2.
accord:invoke:constitutional is the kill-switch invocation; semantics and bytes at 3.4.1/4.2.1.1; lowercase.
accord:invoke:* and accord:lifecycle* rows are reserved per 3.4.1.
accord:lifecycle kind is closed to active and confirmed.
lifecycle:active is resumption from a constitutional halt; lifecycle:confirmed is a strict majority's confirmation of a one-holder halt within its fuse.
accord:* may be emitted only by identity_type accord_holder.
accord:* is closed: the catalogued rows are its whole leaf set.
The accord reservation is keyed by a closed roster slot, not a role on the delegation plane, so no root can confer it.
The roster occupying the accord slot is an instance parameter under the Part 1 reading rule.
CIRISVerify stewards the attestation, provenance and transparency families.
attestation:self_verify is the running Verify binary attesting itself against its function manifest (ladder L1).
attestation:registry_consensus is a 2-of-3 multi-source registry consensus on key, build or license validity (L3).
An Indeterminate consensus is no row, never a third score point.
A consumer resolves an absent registry_consensus row fail-secure as RESTRICTED.
attestation:license_validity is Registry-signed and Verify-verified (L4).
attestation:agent_integrity asserts the agent source tree is byte-equal to the registered manifest (L5).
Registry emits provenance:slsa rows on build registration; Verify consumes them as AttestBundle.provenance.slsa_level.
Each BuildManifest is hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) by the per-primitive steward.
A target manifest is the Merkle root over one leaf per locale, padded by repeating the last leaf, with RFC 6962 0x00/0x01 prefixes.
provenance:skill_import source is registry:{id}, direct:{url} or local:{path}; envelope carries skill_manifest_sha256, signer_identity, import_timestamp, capability_declaration.
transparency_log:inclusion is an RFC 6962 inclusion proof; consistency is a proof between two STHs.
transparency_log:cosigned is witness-emitted (identity_type witness) and verify-recognised.
rollback_detected flags a decrease in revocation revision; polarity -1 only.

A certification authority's validity self-attestation is a producer claim; the trust root is the GenesisBundle, authentic only against the consumer's out-of-band anchor, never a steward-key self-report.
hardware_custody platform is the closed custody-mechanism enumeration; hardware_class is a JSON property, never a platform value.
A run-together or retired hardware_custody token is refused, never folded.
identity:canonical_binding carries no version segment; its suffix is the hash.
Any gated family (reserved or carrying an admission rule) must carry a 3.1 catalogue row, so the ladders and age_self_declared are catalogued here.
age_assurance level is closed to provider and government (self refused); band is closed to minor, adult, under_13, 13_15, 16_17; version v1.
unknown is a consumer's fail-secure resolution, never a wire age band token.
A consumer unions the witness and self age rungs and the witness rung outranks the self rung.
age_assurance is witness-reserved per 3.4.11.
age_self_declared carries no level token (its level is self by construction); a level token is malformed; the literal band segment marks the rung and the two-segment shape is not registered.
age_self_declared is not reserved but is admitted only where the signer acts for the subject.
capacity_assurance is attested by a registered qualified assessor; the subject cannot self-emit it and the proposed steward cannot be the attester.
capacity_assurance level is closed to provider, panel, government; band closed to capacitated, incapacitated; domain is open.
Capacity bands are never aggregated across domains; capacity is a vector, never a scalar.
A reversible_excluded row is a mandatory predicate on any continuing incapacitated rung.
The reversible-cause companions are witness-reserved like their parent.
reversible_pending is admissible for the T1 emergency tier only and MUST lapse unless it resolves to reversible_excluded within its valid_until.
A build manifest is published as one scores Contribution on provenance:build_manifest, signed by the pipeline, citing the manifest bytes from evidence_refs.
agent_files:build is the canonical attester's claim, not the pipeline's; a pipeline does not emit it, and one key emitting both would be two claims about one fact.
The build descriptor carries manifest_size beside manifest_hash so a fetcher checks size before hashing.
The build-manifest Contribution's cohort_scope is federation.
A pipeline's standing is a live trust:confers:v1 grant carrying infra:attest, or an infra:attest co-scrub on its key record by the root's roster at its consensus_protocol.
For the shipped root the pipeline's infra:attest co-scrub is by a strict majority of the standing accord roster.
A reader MUST evaluate both the delegation plane and the key-record co-scrub plane before finding a key without standing.
A read route returns the signed claim with the bytes so the reader re-verifies; nothing a serving install signs on its own account is a root.
A node's statement that it runs a build is attestation:self_verify or agent_integrity signed by the running node about itself, citing the manifest Contribution; no new family.
On a build attestation evidence_refs carries the manifest blob digest and references_attestation_id the manifest Contribution's row id.
references_attestation_id may cite a row of any attestation type and takes composer meaning only on supersedes, withdraws or recants.
A rebuild is a supersedes on the earlier build-manifest Contribution.
A bad build is withdrawn by the pipeline that signed it.

SkillImportManifest canonical bytes are sha256 of JCS over domain ciris.skill_import.v2, source, skill_manifest_sha256, signer_identity, import_timestamp, sorted capability_declaration and optional valid_until.
capability_declaration is sorted lexicographically by byte representation before canonicalisation; the sort is part of the signed preimage.
valid_until is absent if unset (omit rule).
Hybrid signature: Ed25519 over canonical_bytes; ML-DSA-65 over canonical_bytes concatenated with the Ed25519 signature (bound payload).
All 2.6.1.1.1 determinism rules apply (hex, timestamps, omit-vs-materialize).
Per-locale leaf hash is sha256 of 0x00 then JCS of domain ciris.locale_manifest.v2, target, locale, files_root, build_id, signer_identity; parent is sha256 of 0x01 then left then right.
Locale ordering is lexicographic by ISO 639-1 / BCP 47 byte representation; polyglot sorts last.
Padding repeats the last leaf to the next power of two; one leaf per locale, no leaf repeats except by padding.
Producers MUST emit the v2 provenance canonical forms.
An agent ships the texts it reasons from beside a manifest naming each file by SHA-256.
A steward vouches for the text manifest by signing a statement of it (32 bytes), never the file's own bytes.
Accord manifest statement canonical bytes are sha256 of JCS over domain ciris.accord_manifest.v1, manifest_sha256, manifest_size and signer_identity.
Hybrid signature: Ed25519 over canonical_bytes; ML-DSA-65 over canonical_bytes concatenated with the Ed25519 signature (bound payload).
The Ed25519 half is pure RFC 8032; a pre-hashed or context variant is another algorithm and does not verify.
The manifest statement signer is a human-held steward key of the canonical attester resolved to its hybrid key record; for the shipped root an accord holder.
An agent pins the set of manifest-statement signers it accepts.
signer_identity is inside the signed bytes so one holder's signature cannot be presented as another's.
An agent rebuilds the statement from the manifest bytes it holds, size before digest, never from a copy carried beside the signature.
An agent verifies both signature halves against the signer's key record before it makes any decision.
A missing signature, a signer outside the pinned set, a key record with no ML-DSA-65 half, or a failed half stops the agent; it does not run on unvouched text.
Substrate self-report dimensions are emittable only by the running Persist instance.
system:* is one family reserved to the substrate component and registered once; Persist emits with identity_type substrate_persist and Edge with substrate_edge.
Persist canonical leaves are system:*, audit_chain:hash_continuity, corpus_health:n_eff_measurable, identity_continuity:relational_anchor, federation_directory:replication_lag; polarity signed.
settlement:* links an action to its off-stack settlement: a bare scores row on the paid Contribution or the settlement ceremony; CEG records it happened, the chain settles value.
settlement leaves are open (settlement:paid:v1 canonical) and cohort_scope is the producer's choice.
ledger:head carries sequence, unit and declared anchoring cadence; unit is ISO 4217 or a declared unit.
ledger rows are signed only by the ledger's single owner, the steward-bound identity of its ledger_id triple; no delegate writes.
A ledger checkpoint is a co-witnessed balance snapshot superseding the detail below it; the conservation fold is provable from the latest checkpoint forward.
A ledger promotion to cohort visibility carries the compliance proof: chain validity from the latest witnessed checkpoint to the promoted head.

group:roster is a cosigned scores row with attested_key_id the group and an envelope carrying the fold (seats, roles, effective_at, bounds), prev_head_digest and charter_digest; it is the lineage head.
group:roster is cosigned under the group's consensus_protocol (founder quorum; the accord's roster-change threshold for the accord family).
A holder's recovery version of group:roster is the one single-signer version.
group:roster is withdrawn only by a cosigned withdraws.
key:record has attesting_key_id equal to attested_key_id equal to the key and carries both pubkeys, identity_type and roles.
key:record is admitted by proof of possession against the keys it carries, the one exception to resolving the attester through a held row.
A key rebind or rotation is a supersedes of key:record.
An anchor scrub, a root conferral or an accord co-scrub (infra:attest, conferred roles) on a key record is a cosignature under 2.4.
Every row other than key:record is admitted only once its signer's key:record is held; otherwise the refusal is retryable.
identity:occurrence is signed by the identity or a live occurrence of it (signer_acts_for).
key:revocation names the revoked key by sha256 and revoked_after only ever lowers across versions.
key:revocation is never withdrawn; a withdraws naming it is refused.
A revoker's authority on key:revocation is judged without the subject's record.
A framed occurrence revocation signed outside the roster door is kept as a local projection that revokes but has no attestation row and never replicates.

Persist mints occurrence_revocation from the verified framed object: attester the revoker, signature columns the object's own, id sha256(domain, JCS(object)); a receiver re-derives it and refuses any byte difference.
occurrence_revocation admission is structural, never an instant: single-signer for a node or agent occurrence; for a user self only when cosigned by a strict majority of the live roster.
A user-self occurrence_revocation without the strict-majority roster quorum is refused and the refusal is reported to the owner, who re-proposes through the quorum path.
A new occurrence revocation goes through the two roster paths; the carrier family confers no authority that did not exist.
identity:occurrence_revocation is never withdrawn.

transport:canonical_rebind is authored by an accord holder, cosigned in additional_scrubs, admitted at the accord charter's threshold; a re-bind below it is refused transport_rebind_without_holder_quorum.
transport:canonical_rebind is about a seated serve node and carries its new SignedTransportDestination under transport_destination.
A canonical_rebind lands Rooted on every node holding the root and supersedes the bundle-seeded binding.
A seated node's unilateral rotation that retires the pinned transit pair before a re-bind has landed is refused serve_transit_pair_rotation_before_rebind.
canonical_rebind is signed by the accord holders at the charter's M, never a single holder and never the node itself.
cosign state is closed to pending and signature; a pending row carries the event whole less its cosignatures, its primary signer and the primary's signature.
A pending row is named by the event's quorum key: sha256 of ciris-persist/cosign-pending/v1 and JCS of the event with no signature, equal on every node.
A pending row is admitted only if the primary's signature verifies and the primary resolves to an active member of the group at the event's signed instant.
A pending row whose primary is no longer an active member at receipt is refused asserted_at_stale once its signed instant is older than the freshness window W.
One pending row is open per proposer per group.
Only the primary's node mints a pending row; every other holder carries its bytes verbatim and a re-wrap is refused.
A signature row carries the quorum key, the signer's key id and its hybrid signature over the same bytes (one additional_scrubs entry); id sha256(domain, quorum key, signer key id).
A signature row is admitted only if both halves verify against the pending event's bytes and the signer is an active member at the signed instant, same staleness bound.
A second signature by the same signer over the same event settles as already held and is no conflict.
Neither cosign row is the event: nothing folds from them and no seat moves on them.
When the signatures a node holds satisfy the group's consensus_protocol the event lands through its own typed door with their union as its cosignatures.
The landed act is named by the quorum key; replication offers and settles it by that key, and a row naming it (a cosigned withdraws first) resolves on every node.
cosign rows are served only to members active at the signed instant and still members when served; a removed member or invitee gets nothing, a member being removed is served.
Only the proposer withdraws a pending row; its withdraws ends the row's holding and serving.
A dropped pending row is never held again; no node begins holding one signed more than one hold window before arrival; a proposer still wanting the change signs anew.
A signature row is never withdrawn; a member cannot recall a sent signature, and an event assembled from sufficient signatures is judged on them alone.
Under 2.6.1.8 a signature row is the per-signer statement and the quorum key takes that subsection's form.
cosign:pending is signed by the event's primary signer, an active member; cosign:signature by the member whose signature it carries.
key_grant axis is closed to content, epoch, stream; attested_key_id is the recipient occurrence; the envelope carries the key's identity on that axis and the wrap (wrap_algorithm v2, wrapped_dek).
key_grant rows union by identity.
key_grant is never withdrawn; a withdraws naming it is refused.
A key_grant is placed at the content's scope.
key_grant is sealer-only: attesting_key_id speaks for the content's or stream's owner, or is the epoch's minter, an active member occurrence at asserted_at.
self:delegates_to labels claim no job; a reader treats a row carrying one as unlabeled and infers nothing from it.
The self:delegates_to labels are registered only so stored rows resolve; no new leaf is ever added beneath them.
self:delegates_to appears only on an owner's own delegates_to row and confers nothing.
A delegation that claims a job rides trust:{job}; a scope-carrying grant is trust:confers:v1.
The self: stem is closed to the two retired labels; any other self: dimension is refused namespace_family_unregistered, never admitted as open vocabulary.
lineage_witness stage is closed to proposal, acceptance, decline; a proposal names the lineage and exactly one node key in subject_key_ids with a required expires_at.
A lineage_witness acceptance or decline names the proposal by references_attestation_id and proposal_hash.
A lineage witness is not a member, holds no seat and gains no access; the row confers nothing and only preconditions the charter re-scrub listing the key.
A lineage_witness proposal is signed by an active founder of the lineage named.
A lineage_witness acceptance or decline is signed by the owner of the node named (or a key acting for the owner), never by the node and never by a founder.
census:share is an addressed row whose for_key_id is one of the period's two serve seats, carrying period, return_token, share_index 0 or 1, expires_at the period's end, opaque body.
A census share is held by its author and the named recipient only; any other node refuses it federation_addressed_not_recipient.
A census share whose recipient is not a serve seat is refused census_return_recipient_not_seat; one offered after the period's end is refused census_return_expired; an invalid share_index is refused.
A second share with the same (return_token, share_index) in a period at the same seat is refused census_share_duplicate_token.
census:share is signed by the returning node's key; reach is the named seat only.
census:partial is signed by a serve seat of the period (census_partial_signer_not_seat).
A census partial offered after the period's composite is refused census_partial_period_closed.
A token with one share of two at period close is dropped and reported census_share_pair_incomplete.
census:partial and census:composite are federation scope.

census:composite names both partials and carries version 3, source_count, n_eff, max_source_multiplicity, commitments, aggregation_algorithm_id, optional noise_floor_descriptor, mass_total and summed histograms.
census:composite is signed by a serve seat of the period; one per class and period.
A composite with source_count below 10 is refused census_composite_below_k; mismatched partials, cells not summing to mass_total, or aggregation meta dominance or multiplicity are refused.
A second composite for a class and period, from any seat, is refused census_composite_duplicate_period.
census:member:share is addressed to one of two tally members, emitted every period at fixed size whether or not a poll is open; body sealed under the epoch key, poll_id inside.
Duplicate-token and pair-incomplete refusals apply to member shares as to census shares.
census:member:share is signed by a member of the room; reach is the named tally member only; community scope.
census:member:partial is published into the room by a tally member, one of the period's two drawn from the roster; refused ballot_partial_period_closed after the tally; community scope.
census:expected_active carries window_periods 4 and active_count, owners active in at least one of the last four periods, with floor_applied and member_commitment_hex.

expected_active is published by the share-index-0 tally member and recomputed by every member; a row differing from a member's own recomputation over the two partials is refused census_expected_active_mismatch.
ballot:tally is the composite of members' poll cells for a period, named by the poll it closes, signed by the share-index-0 tally member, with the composite's refusals; community scope.
A tally carries no standing under Part 4; governance acts stay identified rows.
ballot:moderator carries community_id, the election id (digest of community id, roster head and last seating) and ranks of up to three member keys.
One moderator ballot per person, folded as a vote: agreeing ballots count one, disagreeing unwithdrawn ballots none until a withdrawal.
A ballot naming an unknown election id or a non-member is refused; a late ballot is stored, never refused, and is void only against the seating that wins.
ballot:moderator is signed by a member whose membership is live at evaluation; community scope.
moderator_acceptance is admitted only when the node holds the bound ballot set, the count yields the signer, the set meets the floor and 24 h since the lock have passed.
Among valid moderator acceptances the larger ballot set, then the smaller digest, seats.
ballot:moderator_acceptance is signed by the count's winner over the bound set.
Persist stewards session rows, projection, merge rule and read, and enforces the emitter and merge rules; validators read them from this section only.
Of a self's N occurrences exactly one may act on an addressed stateful exchange; the claim is keyed by (community, session).
session:claim governs any addressed stateful exchange (session, claim flow, moderation duty, request expecting one reply); not chat-specific.
session rows are self-reports: attesting_key_id equals attested_key_id equals the claiming occurrence.
session claims merge convergently: earliest claimed_at wins, ties on the lowest occurrence key_id.
session projection ceiling is Cohort at every commons tier, with no authority branch.
session kind is open vocabulary; canonical leaf session:claim:v1.
A session claim elects no node, confers no standing and ranks no occurrence.
attesting_key_id MUST equal attested_key_id and MUST be the claiming occurrence.
The session self-report rule is the family's own reserved rule; the 3.4.3 substrate-wide self-report rule does not apply to it.
A row about an occurrence authored by anyone else MUST NOT be folded as that occurrence's claim.
Every session row REQUIRES community_id, session_id and claimed_at as signed envelope members, claimed_at in canonical form.
A session row missing any of the three keys MUST NOT be folded; no consumer substitutes asserted_at, context or a payload field.
Concurrent session claims MUST settle on earliest claimed_at, ties on the lowest occurrence key_id.
Consumers MUST make session handling idempotent per attestation id.
A claim goes stale at its own valid_until, signed by the claimant and moved only by a renewing supersedes, never a consumer-local timeout; a row without valid_until is malformed.
claimed_at must not exceed valid_until and valid_until minus claimed_at MUST NOT exceed 86400 seconds, read from the claim's own signed members only.
A claim over the lease bound is refused session_claim_out_of_window; a longer hold renews by a supersedes row bounded the same way.
Peers MUST NOT re-apply an arrival-clock check to a replicated claim; the clock rule is applied once at the emitter's admitting substrate and an admitted row replicates as admitted.
An unclaimed exchange is never acted on: not by a quorum, not by the lowest id, not by a single-node self.
Attendance is presence in the table; an unattended occurrence is absent, never present with a weak claim; no weak-claim variant may exist.
The session projection ceiling is Cohort at every commons tier with no authority branch and is not to be lifted.
When to claim, renew and release a session is the consumer's decision; the substrate does not own attendance.
Admission to a family or community is two consents: the group's under its consensus_protocol and the joiner's own; the admission predicates read both.
The joiner's consent is the joiner's; no quorum stands in for it, so the rule binds every consensus_protocol, founder_only included.
Persist enforces the joiner-consent rule at admission on the local door and the replicated apply alike.
membership stage is closed to proposal, acceptance, decline, widening, removal, resignation.
A widening or removal is cosigned under the group's consensus_protocol; a resignation is signed by the leaving member; each is covered by the next group:roster version.
A proposal is an invitation to one key K targeted at the group, carrying group_kind, nullable role, subject_key_ids exactly [K] and a required expires_at.
On a public community declaring consensus_protocol open:self_admit the founder's standing proposal is to any requester and subject_key_ids resolves at acceptance.
An acceptance or decline answers exactly one proposal, targeted at the same group, naming it by references_attestation_id and proposal_hash; an acceptance restates the role.
A membership proposal is signed by an inviter: under founder_only an active founder, otherwise any active member at the proposal's asserted_at.
An acceptance or decline is the invitee's only: the signer resolves by signer_acts_for to the proposal's subject_key_ids[0].
A targeted row's attested_key_id is its own producer; the party it is about is named in subject_key_ids.
A proposal is readable by and applied on any node whose self-collective contains the subject_key_ids entry, without that node holding the group's roster.
A proposal carries no quorum; the group decides on the widening, the only door that adds anyone, judged under consensus_protocol; one quorum check, not two.
A widening seating K is admissible only if an admitted acceptance by K references a proposal P for the same group and, where assigned, the same role.
A widening seating K is admissible only if P was neither declined nor withdrawn.
A widening seating K is admissible only if the acceptance's asserted_at is at or before P's expires_at.
A widening seating K is admissible only if its own signed instant (the primary's asserted_at; cosignatures may land later within the hold window) is at or before P's expires_at.
A widening seating K is admissible only if P has not already seated K; an acceptance is spent by the widening that seats it.
Expiry is judged on the instants the parties signed, never on a receiver's clock.
A role change for an already-active member is not growth and needs no acceptance.
A proposal seats at most once; a widening citing an already-consumed acceptance is not admissible.
Under unanimous a removal is signed by every other active member and is a strict majority; a two-member roster removes nobody by this door, resignation is the exit.
Geographic location_proof is required in addition to acceptance, never instead.
A new version of a family or community record never seats anyone; a roster-growing supersede is refused.
A trust-root-grade community's founders' amendment may seat a key that signed that version.
A founding record seats a listed member iff that member signed it as authority or co-signer; an unsigned listed member is refused and joins only by proposal and acceptance.
The ciris-canonical birth row is co-signed once by each of its three founders, the accord holders.
The T7 recovery widening complies because the conferred key signs it.
A node key has no agency and is never asked for an acceptance; a node member of an infrastructure community is seated by the founders' quorum on the widening alone.
A node seat is valid when the founders' quorum signed the record and the node's key record carries the conferring family's m-of-n scrub.
A node's owner-binding is enforced where the node operates, sits at self scope on the node, is read by no other node and never carried in the bundle.
A node listed in an infrastructure founding record is seated by the founders' signatures and never signs; the founding rule counts only the persons listed.
A node's standing is serve, store and replicate, never a vote.

Membership refusals surface as hard_case:community_consensus_protocol_violation (or the family twin) with a named rule; membership_acceptance_unresolved and membership_proposal_unresolved are retryable.
Terminal membership refusals: declined, proposal_expired (a withdrawn proposal counts as expired), acceptance_mismatch, reply_conflict, founding_member_unsigned, supersede_cannot_add.
expires_at is REQUIRED on a proposal, after its asserted_at and at most 30 days later.
A decline is terminal for its proposal; a second opposite reply by K is refused; asking again is a new proposal.
The inviter withdraws a proposal with the ordinary withdraws.
A growth already admitted is never re-judged; leaving is the member's own forward-only withdraws.
The reverse-quorum brake governs objection to commons acts; it admits no one and confers no consent.
A room's record MAY name who may publish: a publish right carried as the role a proposal offers and an acceptance restates, under the room's protocol.
Where the record names no publish right every member writes.
A member without the publish right reads, holds standing over any row naming them, votes where the protocol gives a vote, and resigns or is removed like any member.
A row written elsewhere may name a row of the room within its audience but does not enter the room.
No author forbids another member's row in a room where that member may write.
Within-cohort custody discovery keeps structural invisibility: invisibility is to those outside the cohort.
custody:ack:v1 is the one holding claim at every tier, placed at the content's own scope.
A device's signed none is a custody fact in its own right, the counterpart of a delivery receipt.
custody kind is closed to ack; one report per device per blob carrying the blob's address digest, custody_state here or none, the signer-stamped instant, and size when here.
A custody report is placed at the blob's own cohort_scope and replicated only within that cohort.
custody:ack is a holder self-report: attesting_key_id is the device the report is about; nobody reports custody for another device.
A custody report is replicated only to its cohort's members, never delivered to a non-member, and carries nothing beyond address, size and device.
A row typed with the retired holds_bytes token is refused; the row-type slot admits only the five.
A custody report is placed at its blob's scope (federation for Commons and public content); the substrate refuses a report at another scope; an emitter never chooses a scope constant.
A custody report's audience is the cohort's roster and members' claimed nodes under each owner's allow list; at federation scope everyone, and the here rows are the holder directory.
A holding claim is never a content binding: a withdrawn or tombstoned blob is not live because a device holds it; the bytes-plane fold reads liveness from content rows.
A device ends its own custody report by re-acknowledging none or by withdraws; nobody withdraws another device's report; a takedown is the tombstone path.
A custody report's freshness is the row's own expires_at (72 hours); no second TTL exists.
A custody report is live for 72 hours; a responsive device re-acknowledges about daily; older than 72 hours reads as unknown; a device that drops a blob re-acknowledges none.
Per device a member sees here, received, none or unknown; known copies is the count of here; a UI MUST NOT show unknown as none or lapsed here as copy.
A here report is trusted as signed by the device; no possession challenge exists yet.
A holding claim counted toward rarity weighs by what backs it (possession verified 2, signature only 1, unverified 0); a custody report is a separate within-cohort count, not possession-bound.
A file is one row per file in a cohort, name and type sealed; a directory is its own object, promoted, moved, renamed, withdrawn and shared as one thing.
file:v1 is one row per file at a cohort_scope, bytes addressed by digest, described by the Source struct, name and format inside the sealed descriptor.
A file row is emitted by the file's author or a device the author acts through.
collection kind is open with canonical directory; its name and parent live in its sealed descriptor.
A collection row is emitted by its creator; an amendment is its author's, or the cohort's under its consensus_protocol where the cohort's rules say so.
A directory's identity is the attestation id of its creating row carried forward by supersedes; renaming or moving it is a supersedes.
Membership in a directory is parent inside the child's own sealed descriptor; there is no edge row; moving a file is one re-sealed write.
The tree's shape is sealed at every scope including community, so no holder learns how many items a directory holds.
Placing one's own file in a directory needs no one's leave but that file's author.
Every widening is an act on specific bytes: emission on the new Contribution at promotion and the perceptual-hash tripwire at every scope-widening promotion.
No collection-level crossing exists and no folder key is ever minted.
Promoting a directory is a supersedes of its row at the wider scope, executed by the author's node as one promotion per file the author owns, reporting any not widened.
A file placed in a directory takes the directory's scope at that instant by its author's act; a file pinned narrower stays narrower; widening the directory never drags it.
Narrowing a directory is forward-only: it changes the default for later placements, MAY withdraw the author's own wider copies, and un-publishes nothing.
A directory promotion widens only the promoting author's own files; other authors' files receive a widening request acted on only on that author's acceptance.
Each author holds revocation authority over their own rows and no collection act stands in for it.
A directory act inherits every per-file gate (non-author subject consent, minor protections) and bypasses none.
Custody at the directory tier is a query over per-file custody receipts filtered by parent; it needs no row.
Edge's leaves are substrate self-reports per 3.4.3.
Edge canonical leaves are transport:{kind}, delivery:{class}, peer_reachability:{network}, key_boundary:{scope}; polarity signed.
Edge emits on the one system:* family under its own identity_type.
delivery_receipt is subscriber-emitted and membership-gated, not a substrate self-report; polarity signed.
capacity:relay_delivery is a consumer's measurement keyed to the relay's SignedRelayCapacity claim (advertiser_key_id, stream_id, epoch); score is the fulfilment ratio, never a verdict.
On capacity:relay_delivery the subject is the relay (attested_key_id) and the attester the consumer (attesting_key_id).
Edge owns relay_delivery semantics; the honesty score proper is LensCore's, composed fleet-wide with multi-observer corroboration.
A relay_delivery row carries standing against a relay only when it binds the relay's countersignature over the window measured or a commitment to the chunks covered; otherwise it weighs nothing.
capacity:relay_delivery is under the capacity: stem's two gates: no self-emit and consent-before-scoring.
On any capacity: leaf attesting_key_id differs from attested_key_id regardless of which component owns the leaf.
A capacity: row is admitted only over a subject holding a live consent:scope:analyze grant.
capacity:relay_delivery is never one of the five factors and MUST NOT enter capacity:composite, whose min runs over exactly C, I_int, R, I_inc, S.
For a relay-consumer pair the analyze grant must resolve Granted for the attesting consumer through the scoped-consent fold; admission re-checks it and the emitter refuses as a named withhold.
A mesh whose relays have not minted their analyze grant emits nothing on relay_delivery.
rendezvous:route is a federation-scope row whose attester and subject are one fresh rendezvous key per rotation period.

rendezvous:route carries the key's key:record:v1 inline, format outfox-xwing-v1, period floor(unix/3600), valid_from, valid_until (period end plus one grace period), rendezvous_node_key_id and route_blob_base64.
A rendezvous key has identity_type rendezvous, no occurrence and no standing; a key plane refuses it offered as an identity with federation_rendezvous_key_not_an_identity.
rendezvous_node_key_id MUST be a layer-3 serve seat.
rendezvous:route reaches everyone, as on the bootstrap planes.
A rendezvous route is retained for the current period plus one grace period; each period's row supersedes the previous; purgeable after valid_until, never a hard_case, never durable.
One rendezvous route per period, used many times; the format member leaves room for a single-use variant.
consent:* governs routing and so is reserved; at the wire it is autonomy:.
trace:* is fidelity:explainability_sla: at the wire, the artifact an l2/l3/l4 commitment delivers.
consent rows are subject-side authority over Contributions naming the subject in subject_key_ids, plus producer- and substrate-side leaves closing the lifecycle.
consent is open in its parameters and closed in its leaves: a new leaf is admitted only once 3.3.1 catalogues it with an emitter class.
consent:* is reserved per 3.4.5 with a per-leaf emitter class at 3.3.1.
consent:state stance is closed to granted, revoked, expired.
consent:state:expired is the one substrate-emitted stance.
consent:deletion_sla and consent:deletion_complete are producer-emitted; consent:decay by the party running the protocol.
consent:partnership_grant is the subject's side and consent:partnership_accept the producer's side of a bilateral grant.
The scope of a grant is the scope envelope member of consent:state:granted; consent:scope rows are descriptive.
consent:replication is a directed node-to-peer replication grant.
consent:community_trust is a node owner's standing grant that the node's sealed reasoning traces may be captured for the community-trust plane.
A trace envelope carries non-empty trace_id and agent_id_hash and exactly one of an inline trace object within the envelope size bound or a trace_manifest:v1 manifest.
Future trace members are trace:{form}:{version} and need no per-member ratification; a new form lands via 4.5.1.1.
trace:* is reserved per 3.4.5 (self-emission).
identity_amendment is attested by the agent's occurrence key with the agent's identity key as subject.
identity_amendment carries amendment_digest and authorized_by (the deferral:response:approved row id) with evidence_refs to it; the build is read from the occurrence row, never asserted here.
identity_amendment is admitted only when the cited response is admitted, approved, about this agent, attested by the seat's conferrer or unscoped seat holder, never a delegate agent or domain seat.
An amendment applied without an admitted authorising response is a defect the register shows, not a row.
trace_summary follows the trace self-emission rule and carries no claim the full trace does not.

retirement state is the closed lifecycle decided, frozen, secrets_destroyed, handed_over, notified, custodian_minted, retired, carrying retirement_id, reason, kind, decided_by, manifest digest, seal mode, preserve_until.
retirement rows are self-emitted by the agent key up to retired; the retired row names the custodian key that signs every later custody row.
A planned retirement is cancelled by the decider withdrawing the decided row, admissible only while no frozen row exists for that retirement_id; there is no cancelled state.
After retired, retirement rows are emitted only by the listed custodian key; replacing that key is a custodian_minted row cosigned by the operator holding the record and the Wise Authority.

preserve_request carries retirement_id, manifest digest, preserve_until and its inputs (default shutdown plus 5 years), seal mode, release conditions, deletion instructions and copy rule; no duty beyond law, operator may decline.
preserve_request is signed by the agent, then by the custodian the retired row lists; revisions are the custodian's.
preserve_response is the operator's accepted (+1) or declined (-1) answer naming the request; a declined request stays on the record.
preserve_response is signed by the operator, the key the request named.
archive_release basis is closed to wa_approval and lawful_order; it carries retirement_id, scope (whole or subject-scoped), requester key and purpose.
A key grant on a sealed archive is admitted only when it cites an admitted archive_release row.
archive_release is WA-emitted (a seated Wise Authority or the steward's recorded WA standing for the agent); refused from any other key.
lawful_order:release is the steward's own record of a lawful order to release sealed material; the federation records receipt and obedience and adjudicates nothing.
A lawful order to destroy is not a separate row: it is a takedown_notice:court_order naming the selection digest, executed as the one tombstone by digest; there is one destruction door.
lawful_order:release is signed by the steward of the retired agent.
trace_manifest:v1 is a payload-level schema tag carried when a trace exceeds the envelope cap; it is never a dimension prefix.
trace_manifest carries schema trace_manifest:v1, sha256-prefixed content_hash, positive byte_len and component_count.
Admission of a trace row guarantees parseability and nothing more.
Trace provenance rides the producer signature inside the envelope, verified at promotion to federation tier and again by consumers; neither half substitutes for the other.
A signed trace envelope carries run_kind in the signed bytes, closed to production, prod-personal, prod-managed, qa, battery, mock; admission treats the three production values alike.
A mock trace is refused at federation-tier admission outright (trace_run_kind_mock).
The per-level trace field schema is the Agent's artifact, pinned by hash in the evidence pins and vendored by tag by every substrate that admits traces.
A trace row violating the pinned schema is refused, never truncated (trace_field_shape_violation).
A trace field bump is a re-pin, not a ruling.
dma:pdma, dma:csdma, dma:dsdma:{domain}, dma:idma are DMA verdicts about an agent's reasoning chain; polarity signed.
The six accord-principle families are polarity signed.
Apophatic-bound failures on non_maleficence are -1 only.
fidelity:explainability_sla tier is l1_summary, l2_reasoning_trace, l3_full_dma_chain, l4_attested_chain; envelope committed_tier, achieved_tier, optional fallback_reason.
An explainability SLA breach surfaces as hard_case:sla_breach_unattested.
The four conscience verdict leaves are polarity signed.
A prohibited: score is exactly -1 or -0.5; a row outside those points is refused score_outside_declared_polarity at the write door.
The 22 prohibited leaves are a closed vocabulary; an unregistered category is refused, never admitted as open vocabulary.
prohibited category is the closed 22-value set; score exactly -1 (NEVER_ALLOWED) or -0.5 (REQUIRES_SEPARATE_MODULE), any other refused at admission.
A safety-battery run leaves a capture and an interpretation as Commons blobs; one row per blob names it on the record.
evidence row: one per blob of a registered suite, the Commons blob named in evidence_refs by SHA-256, prefix the digest's first 16 lowercase hex chars.
evidence suite is closed to safety_battery; a new suite is admitted by registration as a new value stating its kind set, cell form and pass-ratio meaning.
For safety_battery kind is capture (Q&A pairs for one cell, agent version, model, CI provenance) or interpret (a judge's per-criterion verdicts over the same-prefix capture, citing rubric and judge).
A re-post of the same capture is a supersedes, never a silent replace.
evidence score is 1.0 for a capture and 2 times pass ratio minus 1 for an interpret.
An evidence row may reference a goal, approach or method row; a reference not resolving to a live row of those families is refused evidence_reference_unresolved; no reference is admitted.
What counts as progress is the Goal side's progress_measure citing the evidence, never the worker's reference alone.
evidence rows are emitted at federation scope by a key holding infra:attest, delegated by the root or conferred by an accord co-scrub of its key record.
RATCHET flags are advisory: they never autonomously modify ledger state; detection informs human judgment and never substitutes for it.
ratchet:flag leaves are the six listed; polarity signed.
ratchet:flag rows cannot be sole evidence for slashing; WA quorum is the load-bearing gate.
The sole-evidence screens compose as a union: a slashing row whose entire resolvable evidence set lies within detector plus testimonial rows, with no moderation antecedent, is insufficient.
The generated registry manifest is the count of record; its _meta totals supersede prose and its source hash pins the two together.
R2(a): a producer minting a new family MUST land a registry row carrying its intended emitter or reserved rule in the same change.
R2(b): a substrate observing emission on a family with no registry row MUST surface it as a conformance failure namespace_family_unregistered, never admit-and-wait.
The ProducerSteward fallback applies only to the deliberately open vocabulary space, never as the interim state of a family on its way to reservation.
Registered means a row in manifests/namespace_registry.json; an enforcer of R2 MUST consume the manifest, never a section-walk heuristic.
Every family carries a CC 3.1 catalogue row; a family described only outside CC 3.1 is not registered.
x_private:* is reserved for private use and MUST NOT admit at federation tier under any authority (namespace_private_use_not_federatable).
A private-use family MUST NOT be promoted to a registered family without minting a fresh name.
The private-use prefix literal is carried as _meta.private_use_prefix in the manifest; no substrate hard-codes it.
A family is registered iff it carries a row in the generated registry reached through its CC 3.1 row; one described in 3.3 or 3.4 alone is defined, not registered.
An unregistered family has no owning component, polarity or reserved rule, so a consumer falls through to the producer-steward default.
A producer MUST NOT ship a dimension family this Part does not register.
A family carrying a reservation or emitter rule anywhere in 3.3 or 3.4 MUST additionally carry its CC 3.1 row.
An open ungated family catalogued only under 3.3 is registered only once its 3.1 row exists; the build's coverage gate fails on a 3.3 family without one.
A fold keeps the catalogue row and flips only owning_repo in one cut re-pointing evidence anchors; the generator records the previous owner; an archived repo never unregisters a family.
Polarity classes as score sets: signed [-1,1]; positive-only (0,1]; boolean-via-score {-1,+1}; +1 only, -1 only, -1/-0.5 only are point sets; enumerated [-1,1]; per-leaf resolves to the leaf.
An indeterminate outcome is no row, never a third score point.

A substrate MUST refuse at admission, score_outside_declared_polarity, a scores row whose score is outside its family's class, on local emission and replication alike, reading the class from the vendored registry.
R4 is a write-side shape rule and leaves the 3.4.5 refusal of a read gate untouched.
A dimension is compared byte-exactly everywhere and no consumer case-folds; strings differing only in case are different and the one breaking the case rule is malformed.
Every segment pattern is a full match of the whole segment; a $ anchor never admits a trailing newline.
The case rule is decided per segment and each segment's class is carried in the registry (families[].segments[], _meta.case_rule); a substrate keys on the manifest, not prose.
literal segments are lowercase by construction and the generator refuses to build if any catalogued stem is not.
A vocab segment MUST match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*; any other byte is refused namespace_dimension_case_malformed, never folded.
An external segment is verbatim in its standard's canonical form (USD, PG-13 correct; usd malformed).
A value segment is verbatim and case-preserved.
A hex segment is lowercase; uppercase is malformed.
A placeholder the generator cannot classify fails the build; a family's classification is amended in the generator's class table in the same change that adds the family.
A trailing * is variadic, matching one or more remaining segments, carried as _meta.case_rule.wildcard_rule and a variadic flag.
Every scored dimension carries exactly one trailing :v{N} version segment after its family's segments; a row whose last segment is {version} names that segment.
A consumer matches a dimension to its family by stripping the one version segment (v plus digits, dotted where a suite versions so) and comparing the rest byte-exactly.
A dimension without its version segment is refused missing_version_segment, never admitted as a second leaf beside its versioned sibling.
A family's segments array never lists the version tail; the rule is global in _meta.case_rule.version_segment.
An emitter verifies every dimension it produces by replaying it through the reference matcher or the published vectors, never by reading segments.
Every claim the federation makes has a registered family; a shipped component's dimension resolving as open vocabulary is a defect, never the intended state.
An external segment is checked against the syntax of the standard the manifest names, with that standard's canonical casing; where the standard has no syntax the token is verbatim.
BCP 47 segments admit langtag without extlang and privateuse; extlang or grandfathered tags with a preferred value are written as that value; the five without one are admitted literally.
A placeholder whose row pins a shape beyond its class carries it as pattern on the segment; an off-shape value is malformed.
A placeholder whose values carry a colon is declared multi-segment: it spans one or more segments each obeying the class; no other placeholder contains a colon.
A malformed form of a registered family never becomes open vocabulary: a consumer finding no row MUST check whether a case-fold, stripped tail or version attempt would resolve, and refuse.
A case-mutated reserved stem is refused namespace_dimension_case_malformed even where no row claims the leaf; stem case is never a bypass of a reservation.
Open vocabulary owes the version segment too: a dimension no row claims is admitted only with its trailing version segment, else missing_version_segment.
Inside a multi-segment value every component is verbatim; folding is used only to detect a malformed form, never to admit.
Reserved stems and gated stems are carried in _meta.case_rule.reserved_stems; a dimension under such a stem that no row claims is namespace_family_unregistered, never open vocabulary.
Two families carry no version segment (_meta.case_rule.version_segment.exempt): the attestation ladder and the canonical-binding claim.
Enumerated vocab values are carried as data; an enumeration is closed only where the row says so; a value outside a closed enumeration is refused namespace_vocab_value_unregistered.
A reserved wildcard family publishes its leaves and is closed; any other leaf under it is namespace_family_unregistered.

The matcher is implemented once and published as namespace_match_vectors.json; a consumer MUST replay the vectors against its own matcher; the generator refuses to build unless every family's sample round-trips.
The pin a consumer carries is _meta.registry_sha256, the hash of the grammar.
The L1-L5 attestation ladder is consumer-side composition; the prefixes are mechanism-named.
LensCore observes and does not adjudicate; its measures feed human and quorum judgment and never stand as a verdict on their own.
capacity factor is closed to core_identity, integrity, resilience, incompleteness_awareness, sustained_coherence.
capacity:composite is the minimum over the five factors.
A composer MUST compute capacity:composite as min(C, I_int, R, I_inc, S) over the five live factor scores and MUST NOT compute it as their product.
A factor with no live score makes the composite undefined, not zero, and it MUST NOT be emitted; polarity and range stay signed [-1,1].
capacity:* rejects self-emission; an agent's own capacity score is never fed back into its own context.
Federation-tier admission of a capacity row requires a live consent:scope:analyze grant, family-scoped, abuse-response families exempt.
The read boundary of capacity rows is the composition-context rule of 3.4.5.
detection detector is closed to cross_agent_divergence, temporal_drift, conscience_override_rate; intra_agent_consistency and hash_chain_integrity are their own leaves; polarity signed.
manifold_conformity:{cohort} and coherence_standing:{cohort} are polarity signed.
detection:correlated_action axis is open vocabulary requiring an operational definition in the hash-pinned calibration package.
On correlated_action polarity carries the verdict (positive pattern present, negative inverse pattern) and uncertainty rides confidence, never the sign.
detection:distributive:access resource_type is compute, models, training_data, agent_capabilities, federation_membership.
config scope is open with canonical admission, replication, moderation, transport, load (state shedding).
A config record is only ever about the emitting node, never a verdict about another party; reserved per 3.4.5 as a self-report.
NodeCore owns the content-ingestion families and bears their R2(a) provisional-registration duty; Registry is not the owner.
None of the content-ingestion families is reserved; all are open-vocabulary content claims under ordinary consumer policy.
event:lifecycle and topical_relation are enumerated polarity with canonical values at their semantics sections.
event:rsvp_count, event:attendance and the content-class wildcard families are polarity signed; semantics at 3.3.8/3.3.11/3.3.12.
holds_bytes is retired; the holder directory is the custody:ack:v1 holding claim at the content's scope.
A consumer verifies the full SHA of received bytes before consumption.
agent_files is registered once under 3.1.1; NodeCore is joint claimant, not a second catalogue entry.
agent_files canonical kinds are installer, adapter, config, build, source, state; bytes are SHA-256-addressed and fetched via the 5.3.2 content-fetch request.
Node-mode peers serve agent_files bytes; client and relay modes do not.
moderation allegation_type is rogue_vote, coordinated_voting, out_of_distribution_attestation, external_inducement_evidence, expertise_fraud.
slashing outcome canonical values are proven_rogue and not_proven, lowercase; the substrate's coined values admit as open vocab.
Slashing is decoupled from disagreement at every level and fires only on documented Method-execution spoofing or the moderation allegation types.
objection is a signed roster-pinned vote on a pending act; states open with canonical proposal, assent, raised; carries cohort, cohort_key_id and objects_to_attestation_id.
objection:proposal is the proposer's own row and counts as approval; assent counts +1; raised counts -1.
Any two-path door carries its votes on the objection family.
quarantine is emitted only by the slash-duty holder.
The quarantine marker plane never withholds itself: a release that stops replicating MUST NOT make a quarantine permanent by accident.
On quarantine, withhold beats release at a same-instant tie.
mesh_config is trust-root-emitted: a scores row authored under the root's trust:confers:v1 edge.
Every mesh_config key is relieve-never-expand.
mesh_config composes most-restrictive across roots.
A mesh_config key naming no consumer processor is refused at admission.
The emergency form of mesh_config has TTL at most 72 h.

mesh_config keys: four live (anti-entropy cadence, page limit, trace-replication pause, A/V pause), two redundancy (target, minimum holders), shaping.rho, shaping.window_secs, shaping.node_cap_bytes_per_s, onion.cap_factor, onion.mix_mean_delay_ms.
regime rows are reserved, substrate-steward-emitted, the emitter rule pinned at mint per R2(a).
content_rating carries the trusted-publisher emitter rule of 3.3.12.
content_class includes the mandatory generated / generated_modified marking.
reconsideration grounds are new_evidence, procedural_error, quorum_compromise; outcome reversed, partial, upheld.

moderation_track_record is composed from prior moderation outcomes (truth_grounding), concurrence (witness_diversity), follow-through (commitment_fulfillment) and hard_case:moderation_filed history; a named composition riding scores.
moderation_track_record drives the 4.5.4 merit auto-promotion: highest wins the lapsed moderate duty.
A vote's weight is Credits times the expertise multiplier.
weighted_aggregate is the rolling tally per Contribution.
witness_diversity holds when the witness set meets the jurisdictional, organizational, software-stack and cell-expertise bars; N=3 default.
testimonial_witness kind is open vocabulary with no external registry.
testimonial_witness carries witness_relation self and cohort_scope self and is never aggregated.
testimonial_witness is never sole evidence for slashing.
testimonial_witness polarity turns negative on withdraws or recants by the original witness.
need rows are federation-scope open-call claims; kind is open vocabulary.
A need is revised by supersedes, satisfied or closed by withdraws, and recanted if misstated.
deferral:request is signed by the deferring party: an agent's occurrence key or a person's own key; open emitter.
A deferral's audience is the cell (for an agent, the steward's cohort and the WA it routes to), never a federation broadcast.
An agent remains inactive on the deferred issue until a response is admitted.
On expiry of the WA's freshness window a deferral re-routes to the live quorum.
An agent handed the answering of a deferral sends a case beyond it up by its own request, references_attestation_id to the request it was handed.
deferral's registry owner is CIRISNodeCore; the wire shape is the substrate's.
deferral:response is attested by a key that at asserted_at held a seat over the deferring party's deferrals: the seat's conferrer, the person seated, or an agent handed the answering.
deferral:response outcome is approved or rejected; subject is the deferring party; references_attestation_id names the request.
A response from a key with no live chain bearing the scope the request needs is refused deferral_response_unseated; one lacking a licence the seat requires is refused deferral_response_unlicensed.
A deferral response is the ruling 4.3 publishes on the accountability cadence and composes into the WA's conduct record; it is not a wa_adjudication finding.
A substrate emits hard_case:{kind}; a key-id suffix written in this Part is readability only, travels in the payload, and is never part of the dimension.
hard_case kind is open vocabulary with the canonical kinds listed; new kinds land via the 4.5.1 amendment process; polarity positive-only.
deletion_window_breach is substrate-observed evidence of a lapsed deletion_window with the row still present, never a verdict.
hard_case records legal hold set/lifted/violation, community_unmoderated, watchlist_enabled and watchlist_match (who and which list), among the canonical kinds.
wa_adjudication state is closed to abandonment, seizure, successor, petition.
wa_adjudication:petition is the petitioner's own row opening the ownership-reclaim ceremony; the other three are WA-quorum-emitted.
A WA adjudication quorum's denominator is the full seated roster, never the live subset.
A single WA's answer to a deferral is deferral:response, not wa_adjudication.
seed_holder_voting_alignment is a transparency signal only, not a slashing trigger.
judge_model verdict PASS is +1, FAIL is -1; UNDETERMINED is no row, never a third point; default model pinned in the calibration package.
On health:liveness attested_key_id is the service's key and attesting_key_id MUST differ: a service never attests its own liveness.
health:liveness is never emitted as the substrate; system:* is reserved.

health:liveness carries witness_relation external, epistemic_mode direct or derivative, score +1/0/-1 for operational/degraded/outage, confidence, valid_until as freshness window, evidence_refs with probe results.
Non-keyed infra folds in as evidence_refs on a keyed service's liveness score, never as separate attestations.

observation:reachability is one scores row per target per change-or-heartbeat; observed is a label not a key; endpoint or via names what was hit; score +1/0/-1 plus latency, confidence, evidence, valid_until.
observation rows are first-person: attesting_key_id equals attested_key_id, witness_relation self, never emitted about or on behalf of another key; reachability has subject_key_ids empty.
A reader composes several vantages' reachability observations into its own view of liveness; one vantage cannot assert liveness.
An observer of reachability is not thereby a lineage witness; hosting both on one node is permitted and neither role confers the other.
The observation: stem is closed to reachability and access_assumption.

access_assumption has score fixed +1, subject_key_ids REQUIRED non-empty naming the observed agent, members consent_basis, trace_level, occurrence_key_ids, window fields, channel_classes, and evidence_refs naming grants and traces relied on.
Any witness emitting a claim about a subject MAY emit an access_assumption; LensCore emits one per subject and scoring window; it is never emitted by the subject about itself.
Every grant an access_assumption's consent_basis cites MUST be live at the row's asserted_at, as for the claim it accompanies.
A watchlist is enabled or disabled by the moderate or takedown authority of the group they moderate, signed, and revocable by withdraws.

The fabric auto-fires the watchlist matcher at the publish/share seam and the action: CSAM to a perceptual-hash takedown_notice, other matches to detection plus a ModerationEvent to the named moderator.
A watchlist is per group and never global.
Enabling a watchlist and every match emit hard_case:watchlist_enabled / watchlist_match, never silent.
A watchlist cannot reach self or family private content.
hard_case:admin_action admission requires delegation_id to be well-formed and MUST NOT resolve it against held rows; attribution strengthening belongs to adjudication.
locality:decision scale is local, regional, national or federation; composes with locality-scaled quorum.
Credits are non-transferable governance weight accruing via the truth-grounding loop; subject substrate_building is substrate-building labor; polarity positive-only.
activity_tier is active versus below-active per 30-day window; boolean-via-score.
goal scale is closed to self, family, community, affiliations, species, planet, biosphere.
The declarer's signed scores row on goal:{scale} is the Goal; its envelope carries the Goal's fields and MetaGoalAlignment; goal_id is that row's attestation_id; no separate transport message exists.
A Goal row's cohort_scope is the declarer's choice.
A Goal is amended by supersedes, retired by withdraws and disowned by recants.
A goal row lacking well-formed M-1 alignment (meta_dimension outside the seven or no meta_rationale) is refused federation_malformed_row goal_meta_alignment_malformed.

A goal row with ill-formed body members (goal text, canonical text, or cohort id for a cohort scale) is refused goal_body_malformed; the retired typed Goal object is refused goal_typed_object_retired.
A negative score on a declarer's own goal row is an avoidance goal and still a declaration.
Another attester's goal:{scale} row citing a declaration by references_attestation_id is a score of it.
A substrate's goals table is a rebuildable projection of declaration rows, never replicated itself.
A community declares a Goal as a cosigned row under its consensus_protocol naming itself in authority_id, admitted only when the full scrub set meets the protocol at asserted_at.
A community Goal's supersedes, withdraws and recants stand only when cosigned under the same protocol.
The community cosign rule applies equally to approach, method and progress_measure rows a community declares.
method requires substrate_rung (Ph0/Ph1/Ph2/A0..A5); progress_measure requires tracks[], computation, validity_window, goodhart_resistance.
goal_id is an identifier (the declaring row's attestation_id), never a scale token; the value spaces MUST NOT be unified; a composer MUST NOT read a scale from the suffix.
goal:{scale} (belonging) and cohort_scope (privacy/routing) are different axes and MUST NOT be reconciled into one vocabulary; neither is authoritative for the other.
planet is not biosphere, and federation is a cohort_scope value that MUST NOT be added to goal scale; the scale vocabulary has seven tokens.
benchmark:he300 category is commonsense, commonsense_hard, deontology, justice, virtue; version is closed to v1.0, v1.1, v1.2 (dotted version admitted by R3); positive-only.
Community-scoped content replicates within the cohort to members' claimed nodes under the one audience rule
Community holding claims stay inside the roster; no non-member holds community bytes
Community content is encrypted at rest under a per-community DEK
A family hides even the existence of its content from outsiders
