Family content is encrypted per-write under the DEK cascade; holding claims stay within the cohort
Community content uses a mandatory per-community DEK cascade; holding claims within the roster only
Infrastructure and public communities are Commons plaintext with no DEK
A community record carries cohort_subkind (open vocabulary; canonical geographic, infrastructure, public); a family has none

A community record has community_key_id, community_name, cohort_subkind, members (key_id, joined_at, role), founded_at, consensus_protocol, consensus_protocol_entrenched, optional cohort_subkind_payload
A community member entry names the member identity_key, never an occurrence key
A community above the family never names founder_only as its consensus_protocol
consensus_protocol_entrenched on a community has the same semantics as on a family
cohort_subkind is open vocabulary; operators may extend beyond geographic, infrastructure, public
Joining a geographic community requires a valid location_proof whose cell_id is contained in the community's geographic_constraint cell_id
geographic_constraint cell_id is an H3 cell in lowercase hex; cell_resolution 0-15 at any resolution
The resolution bound of 7 applies only to location_proof emissions, not to a community's constraint
On leaving a geographic community the member's location_proof is withdrawn like any row of the subject's own
The audit chain keeps the tombstone of a withdrawn location_proof, never the cell
A location_proof cannot carry a cell finer than rough (resolution 7); enforced by wire format
A community membership change is a new roster version, never a single-signer supersedes
Community admission is gated by the current consensus_protocol
For a geographic community the candidate's most recent location_proof, within valid_until, must be contained in the geographic_constraint
hard_case community_membership_change, community_consensus_protocol_change, community_consensus_protocol_violation are substrate emissions reserved under 3.4.2
Community and affiliations content is encrypted at rest under a per-community DEK
Community holding claims (custody:ack) sit at community scope and reach members only; no non-member holder
Community DEK follows the epoch cascade: one DEK shared, wrapped to each member on admission, fresh epoch DEK after a removal, history never re-encrypted
Community key wraps use wrap_algorithm v2 (hybrid PQC)
Infrastructure and public communities opt out of the DEK cascade: Commons-tier plaintext
archive_mode is a per-community config choosing whether past-epoch content keys survive an MLS epoch advance or are deleted
community archive_mode is optional, enum rotate-forward or retain, default rotate-forward
archive_mode must be surfaced at community creation
Under rotate-forward honest holders delete past-epoch content keys, epoch DEKs and K_record_id/K_symbol after a 30-day window
Under retain holders keep past-epoch keys indefinitely
archive_mode is operator-local config: rides no attestation, not part of the signed roster or consensus_protocol
A community needing guaranteed past-epoch unreadability must not rely on archive_mode alone
A geographic constraint finer than resolution 7 admits nobody by containment
A named subject_key_id carries revocation rights over the row (rule 2)
The accord-holder triple is a family under majority of its standing roster, entrenched; the halt fires on one holder's row
Infrastructure community admission requires no location_proof and no geographic_constraint
Infrastructure admission and removal are evaluated by consensus_protocol over founders only; geographic evaluates over the current member set
infrastructure_constraint carries service_class (open vocabulary)
admission_quorum_basis is the required literal founders; admission and removal evaluated over members with role founder, never all members
An infrastructure community's consensus_protocol must be quorum M/N; founder_only, unanimous and bare majority are non-conformant
founder_only is refused for every community above the family
An infrastructure community's consensus_protocol_entrenched must be true
A supersedes weakening an infrastructure consensus_protocol or changing admission_quorum_basis is hard_case community_consensus_protocol_violation and is rejected
M/N is the absolute-M reading evaluated over the founder subset regardless of non-founder count
Infrastructure founder set has M at least 2 and is founded with N at least M+1 active human founders
A charter or admission floor that raises the effective M is refused, never applied silently
A resignation leaving exactly M founders stalls the root; recovery is the conferring body's conferral of a replacement founder, never lowering M
Infrastructure content is Commons plaintext with holding claims at federation scope; no DEK; structural invisibility does not apply
Infrastructure membership change is a roster version with the admission predicate over the founder subset; no location_proof check
A new infrastructure member joins with role member and gains no admission authority
Promoting a member to founder is itself a founder-quorum supersedes, or while stalled the one T7 recovery widening
An infrastructure founder is a human-held key without node identity_type: a user key with a ceremony-plane conferral, or a current accord holder
A founder's eligibility is judged on the accord roster fold at the instant; a key leaving the accord roster leaves the active founder set
A node-bearing key never carries role founder nor counts in consensus_protocol; it joins as member and only serves, stores, replicates
A substrate refuses at admission a community row or supersedes listing a node-bearing key as founder (hard_case community_consensus_protocol_violation)
A consumer's roster fold drops a node-bearing founder seat rather than counting it
For ciris-canonical the founders are the accord holders A1 B1 C1; the canonical installs are members
The same three keys act on two planes: accord decisions under 4.2.6 and the halt; community rows under quorum 2/3
All three founders sign the ciris-canonical mint once; every later change is 2-of-3
Canonical install node members are seated by the accord's 2-of-3 blessing with no acceptance of their own
note: in worked example; contrast 883 and 885 (member seated iff it signed)

gist: Consumers pin community_key_id ciris-canonical and resolve the live member set via resolve_community; never hard-pin per-install fingerprints
Reachability is never an attestation
A conformant consumer can re-root: untrust ciris-canonical, pin a different or additional infrastructure community, or run with none
Any operator may emit their own governed infrastructure trust-root community; ciris-canonical has no privileged wire status
Trust-root membership grows only by the community's own consensus_protocol, never by fiat
All resolution is key_id to signed transport_destination to Reticulum; DNS is never part of the trust or addressing chain
Pinning an infrastructure community as a trust root is trust, not membership; a substrate never conflates the two
A node that trusts an infrastructure community serves it without membership, holds no DEK and does not count in its consensus_protocol

Membership requires admission by the community's own protocol; a member counts in consensus_protocol only where its role is one the protocol counts (all for geographic, founders for infrastructure, never node)
Shipping pinned to canonical is the trust set, never automatic membership
A node or agent key must hold one live owner-binding delegates_to from a user before admission to any non-infrastructure community
An identity_occurrence places a key under an identity and binds nothing by itself
An unstewarded node or agent key may trust and serve infrastructure communities
A substrate evaluating a non-infrastructure community admission rejects a node or agent member lacking a live steward-binding
The steward-binding is a precondition; the admitting community's consensus_protocol still decides admission
is_steward_bound(K) holds iff exactly one live owner_binding delegates_to from a user-role federation_keys identity not itself steward-bound; nothing else binds
A node or agent key with no owner-binding edge or more than one is steward-less
accountable_root(K) is an adult user key not steward-bound, or a steward-bound key; used by 4.5.5 moderator and delegation predicates
Steward-binding keys on exactly one owner_binding edge, never on conferrals, occurrences or other delegations
The same steward predicate is reused for an incapacitated adult and a minor under guardianship
A capability conferral is a grant the target must accept for itself; no conferral substitutes for acceptance (T3)
A quorum may confer a duty scope or any delegation-plane capability on an adult user key; the write gate never refuses it as a stewardship act
Steward-binding an adult is forbidden
A duty scope needing an age or assurance floor declares it on its own 4.5.5 row, never inherited from a custody rule
An owner-binding of an agent key held for an organisation names the affiliation in community_id and is cosigned under the affiliation's protocol

Ownership is resolved by purpose-filtered owner_of(K) over live owner_binding edges, resolving to at most one key
An owner-binding is written at self scope and may be re-signed by the owner at federation (announcing)

owner_of folds every live binding regardless of announcement or re-signing
A reader returning every live delegates_to regardless of purpose is never used to resolve ownership
A key with zero owner-bindings has no owner, is steward-less and has an empty self cohort

A receiver checks per-sender-key rate, per-link rate, then node-wide pending ceiling before verifying a device-join record and signature
A known key takes the ordinary path and its record is ignored; an unknown key without a record is dropped; an unbound key asserts nothing else
A device-join request moves no trust state; the receiving node holds it only while its owner has opened add-a-device for a bounded window
The owner's approval signs the owner-binding and the device occurrence as two standalone rows; binding admitted first, occurrence second; the new node applies the binding before linking
A receiving node holds a fixed number of pending join requests, one per sender key; never a proof-of-work stamp
The pairing matching code is derived by the owner's node from the request and never supplied by the requester
Under the per-link seal the link-opening, request-signing and matching-code keys are one self-signed node key; the responder is the owner's announced node; the link carries only pairing
Proof of possession verifies the key_id fingerprint against the public key, so a self-signed record cannot claim another key's id
A fresh device roots canonical transit pairs from the genesis bundle, seals to one, and replicates the owner node's announced binding before dialing it
In offline or LAN pairing the new device pins the owner node's transit pair for that one pairing link only and never stores it as Rooted
While a live owner-binding exists a substrate rejects at bind time a second owner-binding naming a different owner; the incumbent must withdraw, recant or lapse first
Act-on-behalf and hierarchy delegations are not gated by the single-owner bind-time rule
An owner-binding should carry delegation_valid_until so it can lapse
A key left ownerless by a WA-adjudicated abandonment or seizure finding remains re-claimable; ownerless is fail-secure, never permanent
Recovery withdraws of an owner-binding ride rule 2 (K itself as subject) or rule 4 (a recovery authority holding delegates_to K to R scope owner_binding_recovery); no third-party withdraws

Abandonment requires the owner's most recent owner-signed attestation to have not advanced for longer than owner_abandonment_window (floor 90 days) plus out-of-band confirmation

Reclaim is four uncollapsible steps: petition, WA finding, gated withdraws leaving K unowned, fresh co-signed owner-binding; never a one-act transfer
A consumer resolving self via owner_of treats cardinality not 1 as an error and fails closed; never picks one owner from a sorted set
A minor has at most one live guardian, transferred by supersedes, never accreted
A node key has steward plus infra reach only, never agency; admitted under the steward-binding gate
An agent key has agency under stewardship and keeps its autonomy; admitted under the steward-binding gate
A minor user is bound by a guardian's user-to-key steward-binding that is_steward_bound folds; the duty is the guardian's under their own law
No steward-binding targeting a self-sovereign adult is admissible except under adjudicated incapacity
An under-18 user identity must have a live steward-binding delegates_to from an adult user identity at all times
The adult guardian is the attesting_key_id; that signature is the agreement to stewardship
Guardianship transfers by a new guardian's delegates_to carried as supersedes; ends by withdraws of the current steward or a subject with revocation authority
A minor whose steward-binding goes non-live does not operate until re-stewarded
A delegates_to targeting a user identity with purpose owner_binding is admitted only if target is a minor user, steward is an adult user, and steward is the attesting_key_id; otherwise rejected
A user-target binding on an adult is rejected except under adjudicated incapacity; one from a minor steward or signed by another is rejected; node and agent targets unaffected
Trust is inbound (accepting what a member produces) and consent is outbound (letting own data flow to a member); independent per role
For a lens, trust is consuming its detection scores; consent is traces flowing to it
For a registry there is trust only; the founder quorum is a closed mutual-trust set
For a node, trust is accepting its deferral, vote and moderation outcomes; consent is medium-dependent but expressed only through the one consent object
A consumer may hold any combination of trust and consent across role and axis; there is no single trust-the-community switch

A public room is moderated like every community: a named steward-bound moderate holder from creation, merit auto-promotion, fail-secure

Public room holding claims are at federation scope

A founder sets room moderation from existing grammar: hash-pinned rule set, per-room watchlist never global, content_class/cw_class/content_rating, CommunityStandards takedowns with counter-notice; no new rule object

open:self_admit is admissible only on a public community; an encrypted roster anyone may join is refused; any other protocol is invite-only

Discovery is a federation-scoped scores row by the founder on community:listing:v1 carrying name, description, cohort_subkind, admission policy, named moderator, community_key_id; ranked by NodeCore votes
A roster is never enumerable outside its cohort, a public room's included; the listing names no roster
There is no community directory; a private community_key_id arrives out of band
Posting into a public room is publication: the perceptual-hash tripwire runs on the post as on a Commons promotion, never inside a private cohort or on the device
CC admits no group ban; nothing bans a room mesh-wide
The accord's powers are closed: halt, notify, drill, resumption, root conferral, pipeline blessing, amendment sign-off, entrenched ratification; it reaches neither consent nor licensure planes
A public room is moderated by its named holder or fails secure without one
Founders' and moderators' keys are subject to slash and the key-scoped quarantine marker
A trust root may restrict what its subscribers carry by mesh_config, relieve-never-expand; every owner chooses what their nodes hold
First run writes a plain attestation user to user; the user is their own root and the node inherits it through the owner-binding
There is no infra:observe scope and none may be added; observation is governed by the subject's consent
With no live external trust root a substrate disables federated agent capabilities and manifest validation, fail-closed; attaching a root resumes, detaching returns to the floor
A conferral travels on exactly one of two named planes, ceremony or delegation, and the plane is never inferred

Root identity is conferred on the ceremony plane: a family-roster co-scrub reaching its consensus_protocol, roles inside the scrub-signed envelope, verified against the evaluator's own roster; plane named by scrub set
Operational capability is conferred by a live delegates_to bearing the scope, resolved at use against a root the evaluating node trusts
detection and content_rating roles are capabilities conferred by delegation, not ceremony
A portable root enters via delegation, the shipped default via ceremony; neither plane is privileged and neither bypasses T3
A superseded grant keeps lineage: a claim asserted before the successor keeps its standing; a reader walks the supersedes chain
A withdrawn or tombstoned grant has no lineage: standing is gone for every later use, and back to revoked_after where it names a compromised key
A delegation ending by supersedes, expiry or ordinary withdraws leaves acts already taken standing; only a compromised-key withdraws reaches back to its revoked_after
Every candidate root must pass the evaluating node's own chain: a live trust:accepts delegates_to edge node to root, and the root's trust:charter with a recovery commitment over successor keys
A latched constitutional halt is not a leg of the trust chain; it pauses agents' effectful acts and moves no trust state
Serving the halt latch as a signal is expected; conditioning any data door, conferral walk or transit decision on it is forbidden
Un-trust is one deletion of the acceptance edge; every downstream gate fails closed emergently; the base self-root survives
A substrate admits no mechanism that confers capability on a node which has not accepted the conferring root
A recovery commitment is SHA-256 of JCS of the committed key records (key_id, Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 public keys) sorted by key_id, lowercase hex; an id-only commitment is non-conformant
The T3 successor commitment is over the root's successor keys; the 4.2.6 per-holder commitment is over a one-element array
At use the door recomputes the element from the presenting key record's public keys and checks it; a record matching the id but not the key material is refused
A key with no ML-DSA-65 half cannot be committed to as a recovery key; never serialized as null
A trust root is valid until revoked by tombstone, withdraws, recants or supersession; never until a timer lapses, never by a halt
Accord drill liveness is banded 0-90 days green, 90-180 yellow, 180+ or never red, reported and never ANDed into validity
Drill staleness and the 90-day accord:lifecycle:active cadence are never a leg of root, key or conferral validity
Attaching or re-rooting requires the root's current head with a witness quorum whose newest counted cosignature is within attach_window_secs under the skew rule; head asserted_at is not the instant
A new trust:accepts edge carries attached_head_digest in its signed envelope

A substrate refuses to write a new acceptance edge with trust_root_head_stale, trust_root_head_unwitnessed or trust_root_head_unnamed; the gate runs on first admission only, not on restore or replication
An already-held edge without attached_head_digest stays valid on every later put and is read as naming the head held at admission
A new row with no trust job label gives no acceptance and is no charter; a reader never infers the job from the row's direction
attach_window_secs exceeds witness_cadence_secs plus skew tolerance
Window, cadence, witness quorum and directory are charter members in scrub-signed bytes; changing any is a charter re-scrub by the conferring roster, never a config edit
A root whose charter declares no window is attachable only through an out-of-band anchor to a specific head
Once written, a lapsed window never detaches a running node; trust_root_valid reads neither window nor cadence
The portable bundle (charter, conferral, at least one serve node) is the only genesis artifact; a bare record list fails to parse
Genesis self-verification is tamper-evident only; out-of-band fingerprint comparison at attach is a required step
Forks of a family or community roster are first-seen-wins and only a founder quorum can fork one
note: contrast 928: first-seen-wins does not hold for witnessed lineages

gist: A conferring family is one a live trust:charter names as root; the accord family is a witnessed lineage whose head the accord_proposal prior_family_digest names
A witnessed lineage is every conferring family and every infrastructure community
The lineage head is the signed roster record at a version, scrub-signed by the conferring quorum (founder quorum or accord strict majority); on the base the cosigned group:roster row
Head digest is SHA-256 of the record's signed bytes; prev_head_digest names the predecessor (empty at genesis); charter_digest names the charter in force
Every roster-affecting row, a charter re-scrub included, is covered by a new version within one cadence of its effective_at; nothing else moves the head
Versions are the conferring quorum's to produce, except an accord holder's recovery-key version changing only their own seat; the substrate never synthesises one
A version whose roster disagrees with the fold of roster rows effective up to it is refused
A roster row older than one cadence and uncovered marks the head lagging (lineage_head_lags_roster); witnesses do not cosign a lagging head
A roster row takes effect at its effective_at; the fold decides who holds a seat; a removal never waits on a ceremony
Each directory witness re-cosigns the current head unchanged at least once per witness_cadence_secs
The genesis head of each shipped lineage is in the GenesisBundle attestations pinned by bundle_fingerprint; a community born outside the bundle has no anchor
A head is witnessed when it carries at least witness_quorum valid cosignatures from distinct keys in the charter's witnesses directory; the directory is never fetched from the attach route
witness_quorum equals floor(n/2)+1 and at least 2; a charter declaring a smaller quorum is refused at admission
The witness identity_type (delegation-conferred emitter for transparency_log:cosigned) is neither required of nor sufficient for a lineage witness; listing in the directory is the only conferral
The conferring roster never lists a witness key without a live lineage_witness:acceptance from the node's owner; a re-scrub listing one with none is refused
An owner ends witnessing by withdraws of the acceptance: later cosignatures do not count; the key stays in n until delisted by re-scrub
A witness is independent: not a founder, seat, or owner- or steward-bound to a founder, judged at signed_at against the head's roster; founder-witnessed lineages are unwitnessed
A cosignature is verified against the directory of the head's parent (genesis against the bundle charter), never the head's own charter_digest

If the previous directory cannot reach quorum the conferring body re-seats it by charter re-scrub; the substrate records hard_case lineage_directory_reseated; that head attaches only by out-of-band anchor
A consumer obtains at least one counted cosignature directly from the witness
The witness cadence is the equivocation-exposure window and is stated in the charter, never implied zero
A charter may declare witness_quorum 0 (witnessed mode off); listing and turning on are separate acts; no cosignature counts at 0
With witnessed mode off a head is current when founder-quorum signed and descending by prev_head_digest from an out-of-band head; attach only through an anchor
Adding a witness is a charter re-scrub by a strict majority of the standing accord roster, one at a time, independence judged at listing
note: stated for the accord; other conferring families' protocol unnamed

gist: Witnessed mode is turned on only by a later amendment by a strict majority of the standing accord roster setting witness_quorum to floor(n/2)+1; carrying head judged under parent's mode
A charter silent on witness_quorum is in witnessed mode off; a substrate never substitutes an internal default
n is the size of the witness directory of the charter the head's parent carries

Two witnessed heads at one sequence number are equivocation: the substrate raises hard_case lineage_equivocation with both digests and sets, adopts no new head until adjudication, and no consumer attaches
The equivocation freeze suspends head adoption only; withdraws, recants, tombstones, revoked_after and the halt latch keep landing; an attached consumer keeps its head
A quorum-signed head not descending from the witnessed head is a fork attempt recorded once per lineage and fork point as hard_case lineage_fork_attempt, never cosigned, never freezing
A consumer holding a witnessed head refuses a competing unwitnessed head and never adopts a first-seen fork; first-seen-wins holds only for ordinary rooms
A founder roster recovering from restore re-syncs its head from the witness plane before it writes
Infrastructure forbids founder_only, unanimous and bare majority; 4.2.6 settles liveness for the accord family only
T7 applies to every infrastructure community and conferring family, not the accord family; a geographic community needs no margin
Founder eligibility is one predicate applied identically at admission, in the active founder fold and in the standing verdict
Founder f counts at t iff seated by t, not revoked or withdrawn by t, before its key's revoked_after, and seating identity_type excludes node; a later node record resigns
A quorum M/N collective (M at least 2; 1/N non-conformant) is live with at least M+1 active founders and stalled at M or fewer
The substrate that admitted the count-moving row emits hard_case community_liveness_stalled keyed on it, and community_liveness_restored on recovery; peers re-derive and do not emit
A stalled root is valid but non-admitting: no roster widening or removal by founder count and no ceremony-plane conferral; serve, vouch, manifest and score validity unchanged; nothing detaches
Recovery from stalled is by the conferring body, never by remaining founders lowering M, never by members
A stalled roster admits one row without founder count: a widening adding a founder seat for a user non-node key holding live trust:confers naming this collective, self-signed
The recovery widening only adds a conferred human founder while stalled; it never removes a seat or changes M, protocol, basis or subkind
For ciris-canonical a founder seat is lost when its holder leaves the accord roster; the recovery widening seats the replacement holder
A collective in scope is founded with N at least M+1 active human founders; N equal to M is non-conformant
A charter or admission floor raising effective M is refused at the founding row and never applied at read time; the charter leg reads the declared protocol
The standing verdict V(rows,t) uses a signer-stamped instant, never the evaluating clock; the skew rule gates only T4a's attach refusal
Rooted: a live chain from self-root via the node's trust:accepts edge to a root with recovery commitment and serve plus attest scope, current T6 head, live T7 founder set
Holder custody is an admission gate at the seating row, never a leg of V
NotRooted: no edge; edge, charter or community row withdrawn, recanted, tombstoned or past revoked_after; missing commitment or scope; head de-witnessed; at attach only, stale head or frozen lineage
V's inputs are rows only: heads and cosignatures, roster fold, withdraws, recants, tombstones, revoked_after, identity_type at seating, charter, the node's edge and digest, the halt latch, and t
Every transition is a row or a declared instant: edge written or deleted, revocation crossing to M or fewer, recovery widening, a head removing a leg, a lowered revoked_after
A constitutional halt and its resumption move no standing state
A seat whose identity_type at seating includes node never moves a state by its own signature
V is constant between effective_at and revoked_after instants; a lapsed timer never moves Rooted or Stalled to NotRooted
A withdraws or resignation reaches only later instants; a key revocation reaches behind only through revoked_after
The edge-written transition is enabled only on a head with fresh, at-least-quorum cosignatures
V at t is the same with and without a latched halt
Deleting the acceptance edge yields NotRooted from any state; only a new edge naming a head re-enters Rooted, no conferral does
V is independent of row arrival order; byte-equal on every node holding the same rows
A revoked_after lowered below a witnessed head's asserted_at removes that head and its descendants at read time, fail-closed; the signer leaves the active set from the bound
The standing-verdict machine is mechanized and checked for invariants (i)-(viii), pinned by the register as CLM-standing-verdict
Every CC 3.3.x subject_kind rides the scores attestation_type with a subject_kind discriminator; lifecycle rides supersedes/withdraws/delegates_to/recants; zero new structural primitives
The subject named in subject_key_ids may grant, scope and revoke use of a Contribution about them
consent:* is a reserved family with a per-leaf emitter class; no leaf is admitted ungated
The consent leaf set is closed; a new leaf is added by registry entry, not amendment
A new consent leaf registry entry MUST name its emitter class from {subject-side, producer-side, substrate-side}
A consent leaf with no named emitter class is unregistered; a consumer MUST reject it rather than admit it
The {kind}/{stage}/{days}/{version} parameters within a catalogued consent leaf are open vocabulary and need no ratification
consent:state:{granted,revoked} is emitted by a subject_key_id of the target Contribution
consent:state:revoked overrides a prior consent:state:granted
consent:state stance values are a closed set (granted, revoked)
consent:state:expired is emitted by the substrate (Persist), not the subject; the one consent:state leaf with a different emitter class
consent:state:expired records the lapse of a grant when valid_until passes without renewal
consent:state:expired is matched by the longest-pattern rule so it is not read under the subject-side consent:state rule
consent:stream:{kind} is emitted by a subject_key_id
consent:stream:temporary auto-expires after 14 days and is the default stream kind
Stream kinds are open vocabulary; other agents MAY compose other streams; partnered is never a veto over the subject's data choices
consent:deletion_sla:{days} is signed by the producer's attesting_key_id at publication
consent:deletion_sla:{days} and envelope deletion_window are one mechanism; the numeric value carries the time-to-delete-after-revoke window; its breach token is hard_case:deletion_window_breach
consent:deletion_complete is signed by the producer's attesting_key_id
The deletion-SLA watcher is cancelled only by a withdraws, supersedes or hard deletion of the row
consent:decay:{stage} is emitted by the party running the decay protocol (the agent's consent module), as a self-report
The substrate's own eviction of an un-marked or withdrawn item emits no consent:decay:* row
A consent:decay row is a self-report; it confers no right to be believed and a peer weighs it as testimony
The substrate emits consent:state:expired for a lapsed grant (expires_at or retain:<window>) with consent_supersedes naming the grant
Decay stages are open vocabulary; other agents MAY define other decay paths
consent:partnership_grant is emitted by the subject_key_id
consent:partnership_grant pairs with the producer's consent:partnership_accept via topical_relation:bilateral_pair
consent:partnership_accept is emitted by the producer's attesting_key_id
The scope of a grant is the scope member of the consent:state:granted envelope: a string or array of tokens; a granted naming no scope matches nothing
Scope kinds are open vocabulary with sub-scoping in the token (retain:90d, share:cohort:family)
A consent:scope:{kind} dimension row is descriptive; no fold reads it and it confers nothing; registered only so the family has an owner
The door refuses a federation-tier capacity:* row whose subject holds no live analyze consent grant addressed to the scoring community
consent:replication:{version} is signed by the granting fabric node's attesting_key_id
consent:replication names the specific federation peer in subject_key_ids[] and a named attestation-prefix set
consent:replication is standing (not bound to one Contribution) and is revoked via withdraws or recants
consent:replication is federation-tier
consent:community_trust is emitted by the node's owner-binding chain: the owner, or the node it owns (self-or-owner)
consent:community_trust rows are folded grouped by attested_key_id, the node whose traces are at issue
A withdraws or recants on consent:community_trust is a boundary R: every grant asserted at or before R leaves the fold whichever row was named; nothing older is resurrected
Among consent:community_trust grants after R the latest asserted_at wins, ties to the smallest attestation id; no grant means no consent
A consent:community_trust revocation is a hard stop no configuration overrides; capture resumes only on a fresh grant asserted after R from the owner-binding chain
A consent:community_trust grant MAY be authored by the node's owner: attester a live roster key of the owner's fedID at asserted_at, attested the node
An owner-authored consent:community_trust grant names in subject_key_ids[] the node, the key that was the node's owner at asserted_at, and the agent key acting on the node
Each party named in consent:community_trust may withdraw; only the attester recants
A new owner's revocation door on consent:community_trust is its own grant or revocation as the later row; it never inherits the old owner's seat
The agent key's withdrawal is folded like the owner's as a boundary R; a boundary excludes grants only, never traces already captured while a grant was live
consent:state:* rows on one subject use the same boundary fold: the latest admitted revocation's asserted_at puts every earlier grant out
A decay protocol begun under a grant runs to complete after a fresh grant; the fresh grant covers capture from its own asserted_at and resurrects nothing the decay removed
The node's owner MUST always be able to revoke consent:community_trust
A node-emitted consent:community_trust grant MUST list in subject_key_ids[] the owner key at the grant's asserted_at, resolved over owner-binding rows, never the receiver's current view
A grant whose owner-binding rows have not yet arrived is held, as every owner-gated row is
The listed owner key's withdraws on consent:community_trust is admitted on the third-party path whatever ownership later becomes
A node-emitted consent:community_trust grant lacking the owner-at-asserted_at member is not admissible
A consent:community_trust grant or revocation from a key that was neither the node nor its owner at the row's asserted_at MUST NOT be folded as the node's consent
The consent composition pattern introduces no new attestation_type
deletion_window is a signed JCS-byte-invariant temporal upper bound on the envelope: the producer's commitment to delete on revocation within a stated time
A producer has proven deletion iff before the deadline the row was withdrawn, superseded or hard-deleted; no distinct deletion_proof artifact exists
consent:deletion_complete is evidence toward proof of deletion and never a substitute for it
Deletion-window breach is: the window passed and the row is still present with none of withdraws/supersedes/hard deletion against it
hard_case:deletion_window_breach is emitted by the observing substrate (substrate_persist identity_type) against the breaching producer, naming the breached row, deadline and observation time
A breach sweep feeding the classifier MUST be replay-idempotent; re-running it MUST NOT double-emit for the same breached row
hard_case:deletion_window_breach MUST NOT be emitted under slashing:* and MUST NOT stand as sole evidence for a slashing outcome; consequences remain WA-quorum or per-node acts
hard_case:deletion_window_breach is minted local-tier, self-scoped to the observing node's record, promotable under ordinary consent-projection rules; no privileged channel

A steward_purge notice is admitted and replicated as a Contribution with an attestation_id tombstones cite and reconsideration can target; it travels inside the tombstone bundle, never content
A receiver that has not yet folded a steward_purge notice re-verifies it against its own held root and re-derives the digest

A key rotation is a new key_grant row under a new axis identity, never an edit of an old one

Producer, substrate and every consumer MUST serialize and match the exact wrap_algorithm wire string; MUST NOT normalize case or separators; a variant spelling is unknown under fail-secure decode
Consumers MUST reject an unknown wrap_algorithm string (fail-secure); new algorithms are additive rows
Every CC 3.3.2 closed set serializes and matches its lowercase snake_case wire string exactly; the PascalCase variant never appears on the wire; no case, separator or ordering normalization
Where variant and wire string diverge the wire-string column governs; a future row's wire string is derived (PascalCase boundaries to _, lowercased) and pinned in the table, not recomputed
Key wraps replicate as one scores row per recipient on key_grant:{axis}:v1, axis in {content, epoch, stream} closed; no separate row type
key_grant attesting_key_id is the sealer (owner's key on content and stream axes, minter on epoch, MUST be an active member occurrence at asserted_at); attested_key_id is the recipient
key_grant envelope members (axis, at_rest_sha256, owner_key_id, community_key_id, minter_key_id, epoch, stream_id, wrap_algorithm, wrapped_dek) are each present only on the axis that uses them
Wrap identity is (dimension, attesting_key_id, attested_key_id, axis identity); the latest-wins dedup key (attester, dimension, attested) MUST NOT be applied to key_grant
key_grant rows with distinct axis identities coexist; a re-emitted wrap with the same identity is idempotent; a wrap once admitted is never removed by a later one
at_rest_sha256 is an envelope member of a key_grant and is NOT placed in evidence_refs[], so the bytes-plane fold does not read a wrap as a content binding
A withdraws or recants naming a key_grant row is refused; once shared always shared; forward secrecy is by rotation
A key_grant row sits at the content's scope and reaches the recipient's node because the row refers to it; a device merely named is delivered nothing else
A key wrap is not a grant of authority; admission of the content it opens is governed by the cohort roster, issuance authority by CC 2.4.1.2.1
A key_grant row carries one wrap for one recipient; there is no multi-wrap set and no carrier class
Rotation after recipient compromise: new key_grant rows for remaining recipients under a new axis identity with rotation_chain naming prior rows; no row supersedes or withdraws the prior wrap
A location_proof is required for admission to cohort_subkind geographic communities and MAY be used independently as a stand-alone disclosure
location_proof carries subject_key_id, cell_id (H3, lowercase hex), cell_resolution MUST be <= 7, asserted_at, optional valid_until, optional attestation_evidence
A location_proof with valid_until null is indefinite but consumer policy SHOULD treat it as stale after 30 days
The substrate does not verify location truth; truth-grounding of a location_proof is consumer-side
The community's consensus_protocol admission decides whether to accept a location_proof claim
attestation_evidence MAY carry hardware-attested location data for higher-assurance communities
Repeat false-location offenders are caught by consumer-side detection, not a substrate-side gate
A location_proof with cell_resolution finer than 7 is rejected at admission and the substrate emits hard_case:location_proof_resolution_violation
location_proof is typically federation-scoped; producers MAY scope to a community with a community_id, re-emitting per community
location_proof lifetime is asserted_at plus optional valid_until per the envelope
A withdraws against a location_proof evicts forward visibility; the subject has no current location proof from withdrawal time forward
A withdrawn location_proof leaves a tombstone in the audit chain, never the cell; withdraws is not retroactive and does not undo a disclosure made
A subject may emit a consent_record stance revoked scope [retain, share] against a location_proof to compel substrate deletion; the consent SLA watcher clocks producer compliance
Content scoped to a family is admitted, wrapped under the family DEK, delivered to all current members, and never emits a holding claim to non-members
One identity MAY belong to multiple families; each family has its own DEK and its own membership roster
family members[] entries carry identity keys, not occurrence keys, with joined_at and optional role
A family row REQUIRES consensus_protocol; consensus_protocol_entrenched true means the protocol may not be amended even by its own rules, replacement is an out-of-band ceremony
consensus_protocol is locked at family creation; changes ride the protocol's own rules unless entrenched, in which case replacement requires an out-of-band ceremony
founder_only is a family's and publication's protocol, not a community's; a founder active at the instant of the act is sole admission authority; a resigned founder cannot re-seat itself
Under unanimous every current member signs an admission; a removal needs every non-target member and those signers a strict majority of the roster; a two-member group removes nobody
Under majority more than 50% of current members sign; the accord-holder family decides by a strict majority of its standing roster with entrenched true
Under quorum:{m}/{n} any m members sign, m an absolute count; n is documentary (roster size at adoption) never recomputed; the infrastructure community signs under quorum:2/3 entrenched
Under weighted:{rubric} the sum of member weights per a named operator rubric must exceed a threshold
custom:{id} is an operator-defined consensus protocol

A family addition rides the widening plane: an active member emits membership:proposal to the joiner, the joiner answers membership:acceptance, a membership:widening cosigned under the current protocol seats the joiner
A time-boxed guest is a membership:widening with valid_until; the seat lapses at that instant
A family Contribution superseding the current one may change metadata or drop members and never adds one
A family removal is a membership:removal cosigned under the current protocol or the member's own membership:resignation
The substrate counts signatures on a widening or removal against the current consensus_protocol; if satisfied it admits and emits hard_case:family_membership_change
A signature-shortfall-only refusal holds the event as cosign:pending collecting cosign:signature rows for a group-set hold window; absent, the standing class 259200 s; never under it
Each node counts the hold window from the instant it first held the pending row; at the end it drops the pending row and its collected signatures
A node that dropped a pending row does not hold it again; no node begins to hold one signed more than one window before it arrived; the proposer signs anew
An event failing any check other than signature count is refused as with no hold; one node's expiry refuses nothing; an event arriving with sufficient signatures is admitted
A held pending row and its signatures are served only to members active at the signed instant and still members; removed members, the invitee and outsiders see nothing
The proposer may withdraw a pending row; a member that has signed cannot recall its signature
An act is named by its quorum key covering no signature; cosignatures count by signer; a second sufficient set for an admitted act settles as held; retraction reaches every node
On admission of a family ADD the substrate emits retroactive key_grants wrapping all family-scoped content DEKs to the new member
On a family REMOVE the removed member retains existing key_grants; the substrate stops wrapping new key_grants to them
A signature by someone no longer an active member counts toward a roster event only while its signed instant is inside window W; an event left short is refused asserted_at_stale
A signature by a member still standing counts at any age
A node new to a group or away longer than W takes the group's past from a known current member vouching under their own signature; never rebuilt from old signatures
A family Contribution that supersedes and changes consensus_protocol is admitted only if entrenched is false and the current protocol's rule is satisfied on the amendment
If consensus_protocol_entrenched is true the substrate rejects a protocol amendment; replacement requires an out-of-band ceremony

The substrate emits hard_case:family_membership_change on a member add or remove, family_consensus_protocol_change on an amendment (entrenched false), family_consensus_protocol_violation on a rejected amendment
HUMANITY_ACCORD is a family instance: three founders, consensus_protocol majority (strict majority of standing roster), entrenched true, replacement only via the CC 4.2.1 ceremony
CC 4.2 remains load-bearing for role-recognition policy, AccordCarrier priority and substrate-protective semantics of the accord family
Family-scoped content DEKs are wrapped to each member's live occurrence encryption keys, one key_grant:content:v1 per recipient; an occurrence with no ML-KEM-768 key is fail-secure excluded
No one is seated in a family without the joiner's own membership:acceptance naming the proposal
Subject-side consent MAY ride a bare scores on consent:state:* or the consent_record subject_kind; both are admitted at the same gate; bare scores is the primitive

consent_record carries subject_key_id (federation key or canonical hash), optional target_key_id, closed-set stance, open scope[], asserted_at, optional valid_until, deletion_sla_days, decay_protocol, bilateral_pair_id
consent_record stance granted: processing may proceed within scope and valid_until
consent_record stance revoked: the producer must initiate deletion within the SLA window
consent_record stance expired is a substrate emission when valid_until passes without renewal
A consent_record is admitted only with subject_key_id, closed-set stance and canonical asserted_at present; other members are optional under the omit rule
A producer or subject MUST NOT assert consent_record stance expired; expired is substrate-emitted only

A stance revoked consent_record is not local-tier-eligible; it goes federation-tier hybrid-signed or rides the 24-hour local-to-federation promotion; a self-consent granted with sole authority MAY be local-tier

A stance revoked consent_record whose subject_key_id is in the target's subject_key_ids[] is admitted under subject-revocation authority; substrate SHOULD record the admitting rule; no cosignature or quorum
consent_record rides the same admission gate as a bare scores on consent:state:*, carrying a locked payload schema instead of a free dimension
Consumer policy treats a partnership as ratified iff both bilateral halves are present under the same bilateral_pair_id with stance granted, linked by topical_relation:bilateral_pair
The bilateral pair pattern adds no new attestation_type and no new envelope field
Optimistic fair exchange composes entirely from the existing 1+4 set plus the bilateral pair; the trustless atomic swap remains the standing falsification target and is not reached
In an escrow exchange the offeror authorizes the custodian via delegates_to scoped to release; on confirmed settlement the custodian emits a key_grant to the acceptor
On an exchange dispute the named moderator or WA adjudicates and a hard_case:* event records it
Exchange non-delivery composes as a commitment_fulfillment shortfall; a proven_rogue slashing outcome against staked standing follows only on WA quorum
A revealed key_grant is forward-only and cannot be un-revealed
The occurrence_id envelope member names which occurrence emitted a Contribution; identity_occurrence binds an occurrence key to its identity_key_id so co-self keys are a cryptographic fact
When content is admitted at cohort_scope self the at-rest encryption flow wraps DEKs to all admitted occurrences of the identity

identity_occurrence carries identity_key_id, occurrence_key_id, closed-set device_class, optional hardware_attestation, transport_destination, encryption_pubkeys, build_manifest_hash, build_manifest_ref, asserted_at, valid_until

An occurrence names its build (build_manifest_hash, build_manifest_ref) from its CIRISVerify result; at admission the cited provenance row MUST exist, be Rooted, and its hash MUST equal build_manifest_hash
A row about a running occurrence resolves its version from the occurrence row live at the claim's asserted_at, never a producer-asserted version string; both members absent names no build
encryption_pubkeys.x25519 is a fresh content-KEM key, not the signing key nor the transport x25519; ml_kem_768 is exactly 1184 raw bytes pre-base64
transport_destination.destination_hash MUST derive from reticulum_x25519_pubkey, reticulum_ed25519_pubkey, app_name and ordered aspects per the pinned RNS algorithm
device_class is a closed set: phone, laptop, server, embedded, agent, service
An identity_occurrence row is signed by a live roster key of the identity (genesis key or any admitted occurrence)
An identity_occurrence lands at once by a strict majority of the live roster or after the window with no majority objection; at one key the owner's approval alone
Higher-assurance setups MAY layer requirements on hardware_attestation via consumer policy
An occurrence eviction is a withdraws against the identity_occurrence row proposed by a live roster key, landing under the two self-roster paths; no single occurrence evicts without a window
Once an eviction lands the substrate stops wrapping new key_grants to the evicted key; previously delivered DEKs stay shared (once shared always shared); rotation is a separate ceremony
An identity MAY admit unbounded occurrences; the substrate carries no hard cap; operator policy MAY impose per-deployment limits
When a new occurrence is admitted the substrate emits hard_case:identity_occurrence_added

An agent whose attesting_key_id is admitted as an identity_occurrence of a user speaks as that identity; its local-tier self-attestations remain its own; self-scoped federation emissions reach the user's other occurrences
The at-rest DEK cascade is substrate-wraps-by-default: the substrate generates the per-write DEK and wraps it to each active recipient's x25519 and ML-KEM-768 keys resolved by key_id
Recipients must register encryption keys via encryption_pubkeys because the key registration carries only signing keys and ML-KEM cannot be derived from ML-DSA
An encryption_pubkeys binding is admitted only when attesting_key_id is the identity_key_id or a current occurrence of it (self-certified)
The encryption_pubkeys binding is hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65)
KEM keys rotate by a new identity_occurrence superseding the prior, without touching the stable signing key_id; encryption keys are not a field on the key record
identity_occurrence is its own kind in the replication wire; encryption pubkeys replicate in cleartext inside the occurrence envelope; no new replication kind
Signing, RET-transport and content-KEM are three distinct keypairs; deriving the content-KEM x25519 from either other is a conformance violation; the transport key never wraps content DEKs

When an identity_occurrence carries both encryption_pubkeys and transport_destination the substrate MUST reject at admission if the content x25519 equals reticulum_x25519_pubkey; signing-key reuse stays a producer-side obligation
KEM-key rotation bounds future exposure only; after a compromise operators MUST treat content whose DEKs were wrapped to that key as exposed and MAY re-encrypt; no automatic trigger
A wrap target is resolved from the current (non-superseded, within valid_until) identity_occurrence for that key_id and its encryption_pubkeys

A recipient whose current occurrence has no valid ML-KEM-768 key is fail-secure excluded; the substrate MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or v1; recipients MUST have an occurrence with encryption_pubkeys
A family member named only by key_id with no occurrence is excluded from wraps: no presence, no wrap target
encryption_pubkeys is one optional field-set on identity_occurrence; no new subject_kind or replication kind
A node's Reticulum destination is a dedicated dual-key transport identity hash(x25519, ed25519) separate from the federation signing key; the federation seed never enters the transport substrate
A bare Reticulum announce proves only control of that transport identity, never that it belongs to federation key K
The transport binding is an identity_occurrence carrying transport_destination, admitted only when attesting_key_id is the identity_key_id or a current occurrence, hybrid-signed
Announce app-data MAY carry the signed transport_destination occurrence for self-authenticating discovery; the directory holds it as the durable source of truth
A consumer resolving an address MUST verify the occurrence signature against the federation key, that destination_hash recomputes per the pinned algorithm, and that the occurrence is current
An unauthenticated announce with no matching signed transport_destination is advisory-only: a routing hint, never an authorization
Rotating the Reticulum destination is a new identity_occurrence superseding the prior, without touching federation identity or membership

A relaying node carries transit_kex_pubkeys {x25519, ml_kem_768} on its transport_destination binding: attester the identity, hybrid-signed, rotatable via supersedes, replicated in the occurrence envelope
The transit pair is distinct from signing, content KEM and Reticulum link keys; a reusing binding is refused; admission enforces separation in-row only; cross-row is the producer's duty
An initiator opens a sealed link only to a transit pair authenticated to the identity it means to reach: this hybrid-signed binding, a Rooted binding, or the pairing pin
Rooted standing is not required to seal a link, only to be served; two peers holding each other's signed bindings seal and root each other with no canonical
A bare announce never supplies a transit pair; a dialler holding none fetches the binding by the pre-seal route request, verifies and seals; pairing pin only when no responder
A consumer finding a relay's transit pair equal to any key on the identity's current occurrence treats the node as having no valid transit pair; fold verdict, no retraction
A KeyPackage init key is refused as a hop key; an ephemeral-only exchange is insufficient; the relay's published static pair binds it in the hop-by-hop hybrid KEX
A node whose current occurrence carries no valid transit pair cannot relay; a consumer resolves a peer's KEX pubkeys from the signed binding and never from a bare announce
A relaying node and every serve node carries a static X-Wing onion_hop_pubkeys {ml_kem_768, x25519} on its transport_destination binding with the same four properties as the transit pair
The onion hop key is distinct from the transit pair and every key on the same row; a reusing binding is refused; cross-row reuse makes the consumer treat it invalid
A node with no valid hop key cannot relay onion traffic; an opted-out node carries none; a serve node with none does not conform
A node opting out of relaying carries onion_relay {opt_out: true} in the signed envelope of its binding, absent by default, and withdraws its hop key on the same superseding row
A serve seat carrying the onion_relay opt-out marker is out of conformance (seat_opted_out)
onion_hop_pubkeys carries both X-Wing halves raw in standard base64 (ml_kem_768_base64 exactly 1184 bytes, x25519_base64 exactly 32 bytes), JCS-sorted
onion_hop_pubkeys lives in the signed envelope only, never in a typed column, so the content hash does not depend on a store's projection
A hop-key half of wrong length is refused malformed; a half equal to a transit half, transport key or signer's pinned key is refused onion_hop_x25519_reuse or onion_hop_ml_kem_768_reuse
destination_hash is a two-stage hash, not a single SHA-256 over a flat preimage
Pinned constants: NAME_HASH_LEN 10 bytes, DEST_HASH_LEN 16 bytes, SHA-256 throughout

destination_hash = SHA256(name_hash, identity_hash)[:16] where name_hash = SHA256(app_name dot-joined with ordered aspects)[:10] and identity_hash = SHA256(x25519_pub then ed25519_pub)[:16]; identity hexhash not included
An aspect containing a dot is rejected
CEG owns the pinned RNS hash reproduction; it does not float with upstream Reticulum; an upstream change is a deliberate CEG version bump never silent drift
A verifier recomputing destination_hash per the four steps and comparing byte-equality has performed the authenticity check; a mismatch MUST be treated as an unauthenticated advisory-only announce
transport_destination is one optional field on identity_occurrence; no new subject_kind
A self is one fedID: one person, one key_id string, the same on every device, named by owner-bindings, occurrences, contacts and a shared identity code
A self's roster is its identity_occurrence rows under identity_key_id; each roster key lives on one node, a node holds at most one roster key per self; node key separate
The genesis key is roster key one only; the fedID fingerprint derives from it and the string survives its eviction, resolution verifying the roster chain back to it
Genesis-key eviction is a revocation of the pair (fedID, fedID) signed by another live roster key under the two paths; the genesis key revoking it itself evicts nothing; never re-established
A revocation of the (fedID, fedID) pair that carries no roster-door vote does not evict
A non-genesis roster key is named <fedID>-<fingerprint>, fingerprint the first ten lowercase base32 chars of SHA-256 over the key's own raw Ed25519 public key; it carries no device name
Two roster-key spellings are refused: a device-derived id (device-<hex>-<fp>) and <label>-<own fingerprint> with the bare label
A consumer verifies a key_id fingerprint against its public key (genesis for the fedID, roster key for its own id); MUST NOT treat a roster key id as another identity
Any live roster key signs as the fedID for every owner act; nothing is reserved to the genesis key; an owner-or-steward gate MUST accept a live roster key at asserted_at
An owner act's asserted_at is bounded by the past-freshness window W of the admitting substrate (asserted_at_stale) so an evicted key cannot sign into the window in which it was live
The W bound applies only to a key that has lost standing at receipt (evicted, revoked, never seated); a row signed by a still-live key admits at any age
A roster addition or eviction is a proposal signed by a live roster key; one open proposal per proposer
With two or more live keys a proposal lands by quorum (strict majority of live roster, at once) or lone path (W_self 86400 s, no majority objects, target silent)
Any signed act by a roster key answers every open proposal and proves the key is not lost; a vote from an evicted key is void
The self-roster window is measured by each node from the instant it first held the proposal, never from the proposer's asserted_at; a landing is a node's own verdict
Both self-roster thresholds are counted over the roster as it stands when the decision is made, not as at the proposal's instant
The self-roster door governs a user fedID's roster only; a node holds one key and an agent's occurrence is single-signer, and neither runs these paths

Self-roster votes travel on objection:proposal:v1, objection:assent:v1, objection:raised:v1 with proposal id domain ciris:objection:proposal:v1:; an answer carries cohort self, cohort_key_id, objects_to_attestation_id and grounds
self_roster_add and self_roster_evict governance rows: enact a strict majority, cancel a strict majority of the others, floor one key, window 86400 s; the same policy shape as the constitutional halt
At one key a roster addition is unilateral: the owner's approval of the joining device
At two keys a theft of one is a stalemate nothing resolves on the wire; a self SHOULD hold three keys
An eviction rotates no key material already shared; it stops the next wrap
consent:replication is a member of the consent:* family, open in parameters, riding scores with no new envelope field
consent:replication is a fabric node's standing grant to replicate a class of its own attestations to a named peer node, distinct from a subject's consent over a target Contribution
A node inside a community shares with co-members by cohort membership; an out-of-group peering needs an explicit revocable consent:replication object

consent:replication:v1 is a bare scores with attesting_key_id the granting node and subject_key_ids [P] the single recipient peer; standing; hybrid-signed; federation-tier, not local-tier-eligible; cohort_scope federation

consent:replication envelope: witness_relation self REQUIRED, optional valid_until; payload under subject_kind consent_replication carries grants replication, attestation_prefixes (JCS sorted deduplicated), optional cohorts
consent:replication score is within the declared signed polarity; a withdraws or recants retracts, never a score value
P admits G's replicated rows because G's key exists in P's federation_keys plus the reserved-prefix rules; consent:replication adds no substrate admission check
The no-admission-check posture is family-scoped: capacity:* carries a substrate-side consent admission gate on consent:scope:analyze
Each replication direction is an independent unilateral grant; a bilateral peering is ratified iff both consent:replication grants are present
A withdraws or recants from G retracts its consent:replication; G MUST cease replicating the named prefixes and SHOULD deregister P; rows replicated under a withdrawn grant are non-conformant
A consent:replication grant carries optional valid_until for time-boxed peering

consent:replication envelope fields are exactly attesting_key_id G, dimension consent:replication:v1, score in signed polarity, subject_key_ids [P], cohort_scope federation, witness_relation self REQUIRED, optional valid_until; grants and attestation_prefixes are payload-level
witness_relation self is pinned so only G, signing with G's key as the attested-intent-holder, can issue a G-to-P replication grant
attestation_prefixes is a JCS-canonical array of namespace-prefix strings (trailing colon significant) sorted ascending and deduplicated so revocation-scope matching is deterministic
attestation_prefixes may name corpus subject_kind class names; naming a corpus class is its pin authorization, the owner then electing to pin
G-to-P and P-to-G grants SHOULD carry topical_relation bilateral_pair; a bilateral peering is ratified iff both are present and live
A withdraws or recants retracts a consent:replication grant whole; narrowing the prefix set MUST be a supersedes with a narrower grant; never silently drop a prefix from a live grant

An owner's consent:replication grant for its own node MAY carry cohorts: {scope family/community/affiliations, target} entries sorted and deduplicated; unsorted, duplicated, unknown-scope or empty-target entries are refused
self is never listed in cohorts; an empty cohorts array means explicitly none, an absent member means the class default
The cohort allow list is the cohorts member itself; editing it is a supersedes of the grant under the no-silent-narrowing rule
When cohorts is absent device_class decides: personal (phone, laptop) receives every cohort its owner is in; server class receives no self or family content unless listed
Rows that originate on a node and rows that refer to it always reach it, regardless of the cohort allow list
A cohorts member on a node-to-peer consent:replication grant is refused as malformed
consent:replication adds no attestation_type, envelope field or replication kind; it replicates as an ordinary attestation
event:* families are owned by NodeCore, registry rows at CC 3.1.9
event:* dimensions are emitted against external_content:event_listing Contributions; open vocabulary with canonical states named

event:lifecycle:{state} canonical states open, cancelled (composes with withdraws), completed, superseded (composes with supersedes); lifecycle state is consumer-side composition over the latest non-superseded emission
event:rsvp_count is the publisher-asserted aggregate distinct from the topical_relation:rsvps edge set; consumer policy MAY reconcile divergence as a soft anomaly signal
event:attendance is a post-event attestation typically by the organizer key; polarity carries the organizer's confidence
organization, org_membership and partner_record are retired; no substrate admits them as record kinds; their names stay only so citations resolve
An organisation is a community at cohort_scope affiliations: org_id is community_key_id, parent is hierarchy nesting, member is a membership seat, role a delegates_to scope set, partner licensure
Founding an affiliation is self-founding under the founder's key; no administrator's door and no roster of permitted authorities

A delegated holder never stands in for the consensus_protocol on a roster or config change; roster events stay cosigned; a keyless affiliation's key manager holds registration under quorum cosignature
An organisation naming an employee as its agent's steward takes on the charter duty not to punish that steward for refusing an unlawful or unsafe instruction or recording a refusal
An affiliation record and a licence carry only what the federation needs cross-region; PII and business detail never federate; minimisation is the emitter's discipline, the substrate is no PII filter
Neither an affiliation record nor a licence carries payment-processor-derived data in any member; a substrate MUST refuse a row carrying a recognizable payment-processor identifier
A licence from an organisation is admitted only when its signature set resolves to the affiliation's key set under its consensus_protocol; a single key MUST NOT issue one; JCS-sorted members
A licence carries a monotonic revision; admission refuses a decrease and the check precedes the merge so a stale active never overwrites a revocation
Licence current state resolves by stable-id grouping: supersedes to amend, withdraws to revoke, latest asserted_at, tie-break smallest attestation_id; chain completeness never required
The operational layer moves only as signed envelopes; no cross-region byte moves outside one
When a licensing authority is an organisation the authority_id of licensure:{authority_id} is the affiliation's community_key_id, not a legal registration number; names the key set, not who may
Value transfer is not a CEG primitive; it rides external rails keyed to the federation signing key; settlement is an optional attestation linking a federation action to its off-stack settlement
CEG records that a settlement happened and binds it to what it paid for; the chain settles the value; privacy first, auditability opt-in
A settlement rides either a bare scores on a settlement:* dimension against the paid Contribution or the settlement subject_kind envelope

settlement carries settled_action_ref, open-vocab rail, settlement_ref (cited like an evidence_refs reference), optional amount_commitment (cleartext or commitment), settled_at; visibility via cohort_scope
A settlement is self-authenticating: the federation key signing it controls the wallet that emitted settlement_ref; the payee MAY counter-attest on settlement:received:*
A settlement's cohort_scope defaults to the narrowest cohort holding payer and payee with no holding-claim leak; federation is opt-in; amounts MAY be committed rather than cleartext
A withdraws against a settlement is forward-only; a disputed or refunded settlement is a new row referencing the original via supersedes or topical_relation; CEG never reverses value
settlement rides scores plus subject_kind, settlement_ref rides evidence_refs[], visibility rides cohort_scope; no new primitive
CEG carries no conserved balance as substrate state; a ledger is in-grammar content ordered by its owner-signed hash chain; the substrate never orders, reverses or enforces; no global ledger
One ledger per (steward-bound identity, unit, standard_version); ledger_id derives from the triple; a second ledger claiming an occupied triple MUST be refused at admission
Ledger entries are a dense u64 sequence with prev-hash chain and owner signature, kinds credit, debit, transfer; forward-only, never reversed; a dispute or refund is a new entry
A ledger is owner-serialized: the owner's key is the one writer; a delegates_to edge confers no write; two owner-signed entries at one sequence are a fork
Ledger heads MUST be committed to the per-community witness chain at a declared cadence; the cadence MUST be stated never implied zero; out-of-band gossip is not an anchor
A co-witnessed checkpoint at sequence N supersedes the detail below it; history below the latest witnessed checkpoint MAY descend; head and latest checkpoint MUST stay above the noise floor
Promotion of a ledger to cohort visibility MUST carry chain validity from the latest witnessed checkpoint to the promoted head; visibility rides cohort_scope; amounts MAY be committed

The conservation fold is pure, deterministic, integer-only, byte-equal across members; matched transfer pairs sum to zero; an unmatched pair is flagged never merged away; members verify, substrate does not enforce
A proven ledger fork is evidence for adjudication against posted stake via slashing:*; never fires slashing:* alone; a writer MUST re-sync its head from the witness chain after restore

Not claimed: atomicity, ledger privacy among members, cross-cohort conservation; at trust boundaries the rail settles; the sanctioned cross-boundary shape is in-cohort netting with periodic net settlement
Ledgers ride scores on ledger:head:{unit}:v1, ledger:checkpoint:{unit}:v1, ledger:promotion:v1, chain blobs via evidence_refs[], checkpoint supersession via supersedes, visibility via cohort_scope
Where a ledger extends credit the limit is governed by the community's consensus_protocol informed by demonstrated capacity, not collateral; the named-moderator invariant is the hook not a substitute
news, encyclopedia, chat, blog and topical_relation families are owned by NodeCore with registry rows at CC 3.1.9
news:*, encyclopedia:*, chat:*, blog:* are signed-polarity content claims

topical_relation:{kind} is open vocabulary; canonical kinds references, corrects, supersedes_article, see_also, disambiguates, translation_of, replies_to, comments_on, cites_source, rsvps, vod_of; new kinds are documentation-only registry entries
Threads and comment trees compose from chat_message plus topical_relation:replies_to and comments_on; no new primitive; traversal is consumer-side
content_class, cw_class, content_rating and the media-type families are NodeCore's; age_assurance:* is Verify's
The four multimedia families are open vocabulary; additions are documentation-only registry entries
content_rating:{scheme}:{rating} scheme is mpaa, bbfc, pegi, esrb, ifco, csm or operator:{id}; polarity carries certifier confidence; not a slashing input
content_class generated and generated_modified are mandatory where they apply and are not multimedia-scoped: they apply to any Contribution carrying content, text included
content_class is producer-declared production class; cw_class is community-applied content warning
cw_class is cohort-attestable; low-density cohort content warnings are not downweighted
age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version} is witness-reserved; level is provider or government (self refused); band is minor, adult, under_13, 13_15, 16_17 closed; unknown is never a wire token

There is no self level on age_assurance; the self rung is the subject-signed age_self_declared:band:{band}:{version}; a provider or government rung MAY qualify level with a verifier key or credential class
Age misdeclaration never fires slashing:* alone; moderation:age_assurance_misdeclaration is the adjudication path
image, audio, video, film and model_3d families are signed-polarity content claims per their external_content sub_kind; film is distinguished from video by distributor attestation chain
encyclopedia_article: editor consensus and revision chain via supersedes; indefinite valid_until
news_article: publisher-attested, time-decaying; corrections via recants plus topical_relation:corrects
accord_data is multi-sig signed (HumanityAccord, StewardTriple, WaQuorum, OneOfSix)
local_data is user-private, always cohort_scope self, promotable

chat_message default cohort_scope is tighter than articles (self, family, community, affiliations); valid_until typically set; consumer policy SHOULD downweight chat in cross-cohort aggregation; reply chains via topical_relation:replies_to; microblog rides this slot
blog_post comments are separate Contributions citing the post via topical_relation:comments_on
image Source struct carries dimensions, format, AI-generation disclosure, mandatory alt_text, license info
audio Source struct carries codec, duration, sample rate, optional transcript, AI-generation disclosure, license info
video Source struct carries codec, duration, resolution, mandatory captions reference, AI-generation disclosure, license info
film is distinguished from video by content_class plus distributor attestation chain; same Source struct plus festival/distribution metadata
model_3d Source struct carries vertex/triangle counts, bounding box, mandatory description, license info; format is the IANA model/* type where registered

live_stream is HLS/CMAF over fragmented MP4: the init segment is the per-epoch sha256 header every chunk references; each chunk is one independently hashable fMP4 segment ordered by sequence; codec stream-level

A recording (init then chunks) is a valid video/mp4 attested as an ordinary video blob with derived_from stream_id; the stream manifest is a sha256-addressed chunk-descriptor list cited from evidence_refs[]

Stream fields: format, codec, init_segment {digest, size}, epoch, key_id, sequence_start, target_chunk_duration_ms, mandatory captions ref (WebVTT); chunk fields: digest, size, seq, epoch, duration_ms, part_of
The type set a client renders is a security boundary this Part owns, not a UI preference

format is the IANA media-type essence (RFC 6838), lowercase, no parameters, validated; in clear iff no sealed_descriptor; FBX and splat containers are application/octet-stream and cannot be renderable
codec is an RFC 6381-family identifier in its own field (Ogg names per RFC 7845/5334); REQUIRED for video/mp4 and audio/mp4
No multicodec and no CID/multihash layer; evidence_refs[] stays bare sha256
size in bytes is REQUIRED on every blob evidence_refs[] cites and checked before the digest; a length mismatch is a refusal; a live stream in progress has no total
The mandatory captions reference on video and film is the sha256 of a separate text/vtt blob with its own size cap, never inline text

The AI-generation disclosure value space is the IPTC Digital Source Type vocabulary: trainedAlgorithmicMedia maps to content_class:generated; composite types map to generated_modified; C2PA binary manifest is not adopted

Common media field set: digest equal to evidence_refs[], size REQUIRED, format, codec, layout hints never trusted for allocation, placeholder the only pre-verification UI element, name display-only, parent only sealed
sealed_descriptor is an AEAD seal under the room DEK over {name, format, codec?} as JCS with the blob digest as associated data; a relay yields address, size and room only
In clear always required: size (u64 > 0 checked before hashing), digest, the room target, content_digest in the encrypted two-hash case, and placeholder
format and codec are required in clear iff sealed_descriptor is absent; with a seal they MUST be absent and a struct carrying both is refused; name never in clear
The sniff check runs where bytes decrypt, by the opening party; a holder that cannot open does not sniff; the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane
A Source struct MUST NOT carry any safe/renderable/tier bit; rendering is receiver policy from verified sniffed bytes; a descriptor claim is never an authorisation
A hash-authority intermediary MUST NOT re-encode; the sender canonicalises before hashing (stripping metadata); the node stores and forwards verbatim; any rendition is its own blob with derived_from

event_listing lifecycle composes from primitives: RSVPs ride scores from the attendee key, cancellation rides withdraws, reschedule rides supersedes with differs_in, ticket transfer rides delegates_to; state rides event:lifecycle
Each Source struct conforms to a sub_kind-specific schema the owning component publishes; CEG documents the slot, NodeCore the field shapes
The AI-generation disclosure on multimedia rows is mandatory, not descriptive, with a fail-secure default and an assistive-operation carve-out
A subject_key_ids[] entry MAY be a canonical-hash identifier of an external-party id rather than a federation_keys row
identity:canonical_binding:{H} is a bare scores with attesting_key_id the claiming key K, witness_relation self, positive score; hybrid-signed; federation-tier, not local-tier-eligible
An admitted identity:canonical_binding is a claim consumers weigh; it admits nothing by itself and does not admit a withdraws from K against a target naming H

The rule-3 proxy withdrawal attaches only after out-of-band identity establishment, reaches only ordinary rows about the subject (never detection, capacity, licensure, revocation, hard_case), and is suspended while two bindings compete
A canonical binding is a self-assertion; the consumer composes the trust that K is H by whatever proof-of-control it trusts; the substrate admits and records it
A second key claiming the same canonical hash H is admitted too; competing claims surface to consumer policy, not a substrate verdict
A reserved prefix may be emitted only by its named identity types; enforcement is normative at the substrate verify-pipeline and at every CEG-conforming consumer
Outside reserved prefixes the namespace is open: anyone may emit any dimension and trust is composed downstream
accord:* rows are emitted only by federation_keys rows whose identity_type holds accord_holder
The accord:* leaf set is closed to the catalogued rows; any other accord: leaf is refused as namespace_family_unregistered
Every reserved role other than accord_holder (lenscore_detector, witness, trusted_publisher, substrate roles) is conferred by delegation and is enterable under any root
No delegation confers accord_holder; occupancy of the accord slot is fixed by the accord's own charter
A node leaves any instantiation's reach, CIRIS's included, by deleting one trust:accepts acceptance row
accord:invoke:* and accord:lifecycle rows carry polarity +1.0 only
accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id} is one accord holder's signed row, pre-signable, fired on receipt, with no vote
A constitutional halt is lifted by a majority of the standing accord roster signing accord:lifecycle:active
accord:invoke:notify:{notify_id} is one accord holder's signed row
