Accord-holder PQC halves are published as signed key records in federation_keys under their own identity_type, never in the GenesisBundle holders roster; absent publication hybrid resolution fails closed
The live-quorum section is entrenched; before the scale gate the steward's authority over entrenched surfaces applies; after it a change needs the entrenched accord ratification
WA appointment, rotation, recusal, appeals and wisdom-assessment criteria are set by the Governance Charter Annex B, external to the system
A WA quorum threshold over an entrenched, restrictive or roster-changing decision takes its denominator over the full seated roster, never the live subset; a shrinking live set never lowers it
A WA decision that unseats a roster member is tallied at the pre-change denominator
Liveness-critical WA decisions (deferral answering) are exempt from the full-roster denominator; presence is authority there because an absent WA freezes the agent
A WA who does not answer within the quorum's freshness window lapses out of the live set and the denominator for deferral-answering and other liveness-critical decisions
A deferral is never routed to a WA outside the live set nor left open indefinitely because its addressee is gone; on window expiry it re-routes to the live quorum
A WA who resurfaces rejoins going forward and does not reopen decisions taken by the then-live set
WA rulings are published on the accountability cadence and compose into a WA conduct record on scores, relative and positional, never a global score nor a substrate verdict
Last-deferral-answered and published-ruling history are readable by the parties who defer, at the same grain as accord-holder liveness and moderator standing
A seat over one party's deferrals is conferred by that party in a signed row and by nobody else; there is no roster of permitted Wise Authorities
A person confers the seat over their own deferrals under their own key; an agent's seat is conferred by its steward, holder of its live owner-binding, never the agent's key
The seat is a delegates_to from conferrer to a person's key with scope resolve_deferral
Anyone the seat row reaches can read who is seated over whom
resolve_deferral:{domain} seats a WA for one domain (open vocabulary); a domain seat answers only deferrals whose lowercase domain equals the seat's exactly; the unscoped seat answers any
A seated WA may delegate answering to an agent by a further delegates_to of the same or narrower scope, attenuated, depth-capped, revocable per link
An approval authorising an identity amendment is not handed on; it is signed by the conferrer or the person holding the unscoped seat
Where a seat requires a licence the seat row names the authority and a response is admitted only when its signer holds a live licence from it at asserted_at

A deferral:response is admitted only when at its asserted_at its attester is the conferrer or on a live chain from the conferrer bearing resolve_deferral or the request's domain; else deferral_response_unseated
A deferral:response whose attester lacks a licence the seat requires is refused deferral_response_unlicensed
The conferrer ends a seat by withdraws against its row; a WA ends its own delegation the same way; a chain is live only while every link is
A deferral response is judged at its signed asserted_at bounded by the freshness window W
A deferral left open by a withdrawn or lapsed seat re-routes to the party's other live seats and, with none, to the conferrer
Every deferral step is a signed row naming the row it answers: deferral, answer, act taken; seat and delegation rows show under whose authority each answer stood
An agent handed the answering defers a case beyond it to the WA who delegated it, by its own deferral:request referencing the one handed; its answer cites the ruling received
A conforming consumer implements at least Policy A (direct trust); the other reference policies are recommended
Consumers apply identity-prejudice-resistant weighting
Consumers do not downweight testimonial_witness rows from cohorts with low attestation density
Consumers do not downweight non_maleficence claims about a partner because of the partner's long partner_role track record
Consumers apply lexical-vulnerability priority in tie-breaks involving small cohorts
testimonial_witness is never sole evidence for slashing
The consumer weights witness_relation self claims against the attester's other-emission track record; the Frickerian rule applies after these structural safeguards
Default aggregation for signed polarity: mean of score times confidence across attesters
Default aggregation for boolean-via-score polarity: min, any negative trumps positive (fail-secure for hard constraints)
Default aggregation for positive-only polarity: max across attesters, any positive conclusive
Default aggregation for -1.0-only polarity: min across attesters, any negative conclusive
Default aggregation for enumerated polarity: most recent by signed_at from the attesters authorized to emit
Default aggregation for detector dimensions (detection:correlated_action, detection:distributive:access, ratchet:flag): median across attesters
Specific dimensions may override the default aggregation via consumer policy; the defaults are the conforming-consumer minimum

RECOMMENDED names the consumer's choice of composition; a subsection marked normative or MANDATORY inside a policy section binds the substrate whenever its subject exists, whichever policy is composed
WA quorum size is a function of decision locality: reference local 2, regional 3, national 4, federation 6 (policy-tunable); min_pool(S) is quorum_size(S) times 2
Recusal is feasible when cell_pool is at least min_pool(S); decision-scale matching is enforced and overreach surfaces as a named locality-mismatch failure
When cell_pool is below min_pool(S) the consumer takes one of the explicit sub-quorum paths; there is no implicit fallback
Sub-quorum scale-down: re-attest the decision at the next-lower locality scale and emit hard_case:locality_scale_down
Sub-quorum escalate: emit hard_case:locality_underpopulated and route the decision to the federation-scale cell
Sub-quorum liveness-defer: emit hard_case:locality_quorum_unreachable and defer until the pool grows; the deferred state is itself reviewable by reconsideration

The amendment process routes through locality:decision:federation by default; the federation pool is sized so min_pool(federation) holds at genesis; below it only the constitutional halt resolves the crisis
Community content is encrypted under a per-community DEK and its holding claims reach members only; byte-confidential and existence-invisible to non-members
Content with a bounded membership roster is encrypted; content without one is plaintext
Self and family scope: encrypted per-write DEK, no wire discovery outside the cohort, readers are the occurrences or family members
Community and affiliations scope: encrypted under the community DEK; no discovery outside the roster, custody:ack within the cohort; readers are members via the DEK cascade
Commons scopes (species, biosphere, federation): plaintext; custody:ack at federation scope forms the holder directory; anyone reads

A public room (cohort_subkind public) at community scope is plaintext with no DEK, custody:ack at federation scope and a community:listing row; anyone who joins reads; replicated to the roster's nodes
Within a self or family cohort a device's custody:ack for a blob is permitted at the blob's own scope and replicated only to members, never to a non-member
Community and affiliations content is encrypted at rest under one per-community epoch DEK wrapped to every current member occurrence at each sealed write; holding claims reach members only
A member admitted since the epoch DEK was minted is wrapped at the next sealed write; the epoch rotates before the next seal after a removal
wrap_algorithm v2 (hybrid PQC) is mandatory for community DEK wraps

The seal covers the content body only (inline body, chunk, stream segment); attestation rows, directory, holding claims, key_grant metadata, blob provenance and transparency logs are not encrypted at rest
The only plaintext bodies at community scope are an authorized infrastructure community's and a public room's, decided by the community record never the writer; Commons scopes are plaintext by tier
A node never holds bytes it cannot account for: it inspects plaintext Commons bytes or is a cohort member holding ciphertext its owner can open; no stranger holds opaque blobs
cohort_subkind infrastructure and public opt out of the DEK cascade and are Commons-tier: plaintext, holding claims at federation scope, no DEK
Node-to-canonical traces (conformance and registry_consensus emissions to a governance community) are cohort_scope federation, plaintext and world-readable
After a community member removal each minter rotates its epoch DEK before its next sealed write so the removed member receives no new content; what they already received stays
A community membership change is a new version of the roster record admitted under the group's quorum and chained by prev_head_digest, never a single-signer supersedes Contribution
The substrate evaluates the current community's consensus_protocol (the six canonical kinds as family) and any subkind-specific admission requirements
A community change whose signatures fail the current consensus_protocol is refused and hard_case:community_consensus_protocol_violation is emitted
A supersede never adds a member; each new member needs their own acceptance of an undeclined, unwithdrawn proposal for the community, grown before its expires_at, else the change is refused
A community change failing subkind admission (geographic: location_proof not contained or expired) is refused with the same hard_case prefix
An admitted community change emits hard_case:community_membership_change
On refusal the substrate emits the hard_case violation row and returns the token federation_community_consensus_protocol_violation to the submitter; the two are different objects
A geographic community admits a new member only with a latest valid location_proof on file whose cell_id is contained in the community's geographic_constraint and whose valid_until has not passed
A public room under open:self_admit admits a new member only with their own membership:acceptance naming the standing founder proposal; the widening still passes consensus_protocol
An unknown cohort_subkind admits on consensus_protocol alone
Operator vocabularies extending cohort_subkind provide their own subkind-admission predicates per the custom:{id} consensus_protocol hook
One held version per group id: a new version is admitted only if its signed prev_head_digest names the held head; a later instant not naming it is refused, not preferred
The community roster is the head (or witnessed head where the charter declares witness_quorum) folded with membership rows effective at now, each admitted per the current consensus_protocol
resolve_community has the same shape as resolve_family; each member key_id is an identity
Every implementation resolves community membership identically; member resolution is a chain of signed bindings replacing DNS and IP
Membership is evaluated as of the resolving consumer's own clock: a member is included iff joined at or before now and not removed at or before now; no global clock
The head is the one held version; a new version is admitted only if prev_head_digest names the held head, else refused; with witness_quorum the head is the witnessed head
The resolved member set is canonically ordered by key_id in lowercase-hex byte order
For cohort_subkind infrastructure, admission evaluates consensus_protocol over the founder members only, not all members

A member resolves to a transport address only through the current identity_occurrence with transport_destination present, valid at now and hybrid-signature verified; with none the member is skipped fail-secure
destination_hash must equal the pinned two-stage rns_destination_hash over the Reticulum x25519 and ed25519 keys, app_name and aspects, not a flat-concat SHA-256
Reachability is never trust: a path that answers is not an authorization; only the signed binding plus quorum are
Cold start needs the pinned community_key_id, at least one seed destination_hash, and a witnessed lineage head inside the charter's attach_window; freshness gates attaching, never staying attached
A bootstrapping node verifies founder quorum against the pinned community_key_id; a malicious seed cannot forge membership, only deny service
Joining a community is three rows (proposal, acceptance, cosigned widening), never a supersede; a supersede never adds a member
No one is seated in a community without the joiner's own membership:acceptance naming the proposal
At the next sealed write in the epoch the sealer wraps the epoch DEK to the new member's occurrences (key_grant:epoch, wrap v2); holding claims stay within the roster
The subscriber set for any push-delivery flow is a community row; subscribing is joining the community and inherits Policy M revocation, consensus and structural invisibility

For a push Contribution at community scope subscriber_set is resolve_community(community_id, now); producer_gated subscription is consensus_protocol founder_only with the publisher as sole founder; open is open:self_admit
An observer share (N=1) is a single key_grant with no epoch; revocation is withdraws against the grant
Multicast (N greater than 1) uses a flat per-epoch key_grant cascade, one grant per subscriber and epoch; the epoch rolls on member removal (mandatory) and on time or bytes (optional)

For delivery_mode pull subscribers discover via the holding-claim directory at the stream's scope; Policy M membership filters non-member peers from the discovery surface; no delivery_receipt is required
For push delivery the substrate fans out to entitled and reachable members; entitlement is Policy M membership; reachability is a node-local presence tracker never attested, replicated or logged
history_on_join carries and does not change what a joiner receives; what a joiner receives is fixed by the tier
At community and affiliations a new member gets the current epoch's key at the minter's next sealed write, no earlier epoch's; the epoch rotates on removal never admission
history_on_join full confers no grant on an earlier epoch; on a stream it is the producer's signal that the stream is kept
Removed members retain extant key_grants for content they were entitled to during membership; a new member receives what the tier delivers
Community content arriving at a member's identity key propagates to their occurrences via the Policy L cascade only if the local substrate re-emits it at self scope

A community member who is a subject of a community-scoped Contribution retains revocation authority; cohort_scope (visibility) and subject_key_ids (revocability) are orthogonal at community scope as at family
A geographic community overlapping a family's location does not cross-admit: families are not auto-admitted to communities nor communities to families; each membership is explicit and independent
Affiliations share the community DEK tier and all community machinery (cascade, forward secrecy, consensus_protocol admission) and add institutional governance through one declared config record
Everything in an affiliation's config record is declared at creation and visible to members on joining; there are no undeclared institutional powers
A community carries the pro-social floors: no single vote admits or removes, a named moderator, removal on a harm report by more than one voice

The data limbs of the affiliation record (classification, retention, legal hold, erasure, disclosure, custody, designated officials) bind an affiliation and no community, except a community issuing a legal-weight licence class
An affiliation may have one member and holds, processes and licenses under the record's limbs from creation; the limbs attach to the record, never to a head-count
A statement about an affiliation (review, rating, complaint) is not personal data: the affiliation never retracts it and contests by reconsideration; readers discount correlated sources
Affiliation members hold no governance vote unless the charter grants one; the deciding seats are its officers under its consensus_protocol
Appointment to an affiliation is the body's signature under its protocol plus the appointee's own membership:acceptance; a one-voice body may hire
Where an affiliation has one deciding seat, an act against a member (removal, quarantine, slash, takedown) is admitted only when countersigned by a key outside the seat
The named-moderator duty of an affiliation is discharged by the designated official; a body of two or more deciding seats decides under its own protocol as a community does
A community record declares its kind in one member declared_cohort (community or affiliations); one record is one kind; a key wanting both founds two records
An absent role_term means the 365-day ceiling applies to every role edge; a charter may lower it and never raise it
A licensure row in a class the charter does not declare is admitted as a row and honoured by no reader (licence_class_not_trusted)

An affiliation's existence, community_key_id, officers' roles and declared licence classes are Commons-visible; a non-public affiliation carries a federation-scope community:listing naming those four things only; public subkind is admissible
An affiliation's members' rows follow its tier's audience rule, a seat reaching members only; a licence keeps no public default, scoped per class in the charter
An affiliation's charter names succession (a successor seat or dissolves_at); when its last deciding seat lapses with neither it is dissolved at that instant
A community whose last founder leaves continues under its consensus_protocol over remaining members, who may seat a founder; T7 stall and recovery reach only trust-root-grade groups
Dissolution is the withdraws of the record: DEK rotates no more, no new seat or grant, seats lapse at effective_at, edges and grants end; custody rows and record stand
A licence issued by a dissolved authority stands and reads lapsed from the dissolution instant; the authority's trust:accepts edges end with its record so no reader's walk hops through it
There is no merge and no split of a community or affiliation: the new body founds a new record and members re-sign into it, community_id being in the signed bytes
Anyone may be a licensing authority under their own key, a community included
The licence classes an authority issues are declared on its signed community record as licence_classes beside declared_cohort, each with legal_weight true or false, absent meaning none
A community declaring a legal-weight licence class takes on the affiliation's data limbs for it
Readers decide whom to honour as a licensing authority
affiliations sits beside community, neither wider nor narrower; a re-sign between them is a new placement, never promotion or narrowing
membership_basis (voluntary-total, ascriptive, role-assigned, employment-contract) is an explicit field orthogonal to cohort_scope; a group needing no institutional governance is simply a community

disclosure_posture is privacy-seeking (default, cohort under the DEK) or transparency-seeking (per-class placement at federation scope decided by the record, never the writer); community-scope plaintext bodies stay the two named
compartments are need-to-know sub-cohorts within the roster each with its own DEK (the epoch cascade applied recursively) carrying explicit per-member exclusions
member_attributes gate compartment access: a member without the required clearance or with a lapsed credential must not decrypt the compartment; credential expiry auto-descopes
access_control_model is roster-wide (default), rbac, or minimum-necessary; under minimum-necessary a read reaches only records a declared relationship covers and every break-the-glass read is logged
A data_subject_access_grant lets a member node decrypt and serve a non-member subject's own records over a session and hand over an export without conferring membership
archive_custody is an escrow role holding per-epoch archive keys decoupled from the live roster so permanent records survive member turnover; rides the key-grant cascade
chain_of_custody is an append-only gap-marked provenance chain per accessioned object riding supersedes and holding claims
Every affiliation role, issuance or moderation edge carries delegation_valid_until at most 365 days after delegation_valid_from, the charter's role_term (1 to 365); renewal is a fresh conferral
A lapsed moderate edge is a moderator lapse: auto-promotion in the same step, read-only recovery where nobody can be promoted

Affiliation hierarchy supports multi-parent DAG roles, a depth cap above the default 5, per-compartment roles, roots in accountable humans or the consensus_protocol body, independent_branch oversight, nested sub-affiliations
designated_officials are named accountable-human roots gating specific operations; optional at every scale, named by the archetype preset where a regime requires one

lawful_access is declared, scoped to the declaring affiliation only, always logged as hard_case, transparency-reportable and never a covert backdoor; it does not touch anonymity-by-default or no-client-side-scanning elsewhere

Each lawful_access authority declares a type (interception, records_production, regulator_inspection, mandated_reporting), a statutory_basis, a transparency_mode (immediate, delayed, aggregate_banded, sealed_cleared_audit) and optional carve-out compartments; none/immune is a first-class posture; default off
transparency_obligations are proactive-disclosure duties decoupled from lawful_access: a duty to publish, not an access concession
disclosure_accounting is a per-data-subject disclosure ledger retrievable by that subject, distinct from the aggregate transparency report
breach_notification declares detection-to-notify SLA and notifier identity tied to DEK or unauthorized-access compromise

processor_chain and baa declare sub-processors and the affiliation-to-affiliation boundary; marking_binds_to_record makes classification, export marking and retention travel across the cohort boundary

Records bearing minor subject_key_ids require a live guardian consent chain delegates_to(parent to minor, scope consent_revocation or share) under the guardianship rule; minor-as-data-subject is distinct from minor-as-member

Where rights transfer to the adult student at postsecondary enrollment the institution is modelled as records custodian with the subject retaining rights (external_controller plus data_subject_access_grant), not as parent-to-minor stewardship
dissolves_at or sunset auto-winds-down an ephemeral affiliation riding supersedes and withdraws, leaving no zombie cohort or un-purged data; internal_normative_regime may reference bylaws

regulatory_profile and jurisdiction are open lists loading the Annex I sector overlay and Annex C cross-walk and supplying defaults; the SI at least 0.6 Controller rule selects the accountable authority
local_feed reads cohort_scope self only, steward-filtered, self-attested with no peer weighting
community_feed reads family, community and affiliations scopes, cohort-weighted; cross-cohort attestations are downweighted unless explicitly invited
global_feed reads species, biosphere and federation scopes with full federation expertise weighting, fact-checker weight, and Frickerian discipline applied
A local_data Contribution starts at cohort_scope self and should appear only in local_feed; promotion widens cohort_scope via supersedes

A Contribution's cohort_scope may be widened by a supersedes against the prior row: references_attestation_id names it, differs_in names cohort_scope and optionally sub_kind, content_sha256 is reused, the new scope is wider
Promotion reuses the supersedes primitive, never a promote primitive; the lineage is walkable via references_attestation_id
For any self or family Contribution the substrate computes the current member set from the latest identity_occurrence and family rows and resolves which keys must receive a key_grant
At every sealed write the substrate wraps the content DEK to every current recipient occurrence and emits one key_grant row per wrap
A self or family newcomer is caught up by a re-key walk: every per-write DEK of every at-rest blob the cohort holds grants on is wrapped to the newcomer's occurrences
A newcomer without usable content-KEM keys is excluded fail-secure with hard_case:recipient_excluded, never granted
The re-key walk is triggered by admission: at login for a new self occurrence (late devices caught by receive doors), by the admitting host for a family member
At community and affiliations there is no walk: a new member gets the current epoch's key at the minter's next sealed write only
Removal rotates the epoch, admission does not; removal is never retroactive at any scope: past grants stay and a removed member receives nothing new
A key_grant for a newcomer covers every still-admitted self or family Contribution of the scope target, names its recipient and axis content, and carries no scope

An ordinary row about a subject is erased by the subject's withdraws; an adverse row by its producer under rule 1 or refused with reason
A subject access export is the query of all attestations whose subject_key_ids contains the subject
consent:scope names the permitted use (retain, share, analyze, train, publish); cohort_scope names the permitted visibility
Parental authority over a minor's records composes as delegates_to from parent to student with scope consent_revocation; no new shape
AI-generated content is marked by content_class:generated or generated_modified with an identity_type agent attestation, re-expressed at egress
A subject withdraws training-set consent by consent:state:revoked against the training-datum Contribution; the producer's deletion SLA then fires
Consent requires revocability, and revocability requires a halt authority outside the system being halted
CEG prescribes no regulatory framework; operators in regulated verticals SHOULD pin compliance mappings as configuration, not as new wire shapes
A dimension pattern naming a subject implies subject_key_ids must name it
Ceremony grants take the bilateral-pair shape
Consent decay composes as protocol stages
The substrate emits hard_case rows; a detector library composes detection rows
Consent stream kinds are open vocabulary; temporary, partnered and anonymous are recommended canonical kinds, not a lockdown
SLA values are operator policy; the deletion SLA SHOULD be at most the one-month statutory deadline
A 90-day decay is the canonical example; other decay protocols MAY exist
The immediate-removal legal bases are TvecTerrorist, NcmecCsam, GifctCip, PerceptualHashCsam and CourtOrder
A takedown_notice is signed by a claimant who MUST hold the takedown duty over the content's community, as self or delegated from an accountable root
The fast path waives the quorum and the counter-notice, never the duty-holder gate; a notice from a key without the duty is refused
On an admitted takedown the substrate tombstones the content on the bytes plane; nobody withdraws another device's holding claim
Holders seeing a tombstone SHOULD cease serving the bytes and re-acknowledge none
Under an immediate-removal basis a reachable holder MUST destroy the bytes on receipt of the purge; a withheld copy is knowing possession
A duty-holder takedown and a trust-root steward_purge execute as one tombstone row: plane, target digest, authorising notice id, never content
The tombstone replicates, since only a tombstone tells a peer holding a replica to descend
A duty-holder's notice reaches the bytes plane only; a steward_purge is cosigned by the trust root and reaches any plane
A steward_purge hard-deletes W = 72 h after the tombstone, a substrate-stated dwell with no peer acknowledgement; purge_not_settled refuses an early finalize
The tombstone outlives the row
A retraction the door cannot admit aborts the whole purge (purge_retraction_inadmissible); a purge is whole or not at all
A tombstoned record is refused at every admission door and never served (purge_tombstoned)
Under TvecTerrorist or GifctCip the operator coordinates via the designated channel (regulator within 1 h) and the substrate logs notice and eviction to its audit chain
Under NcmecCsam or PerceptualHashCsam a US operator MUST file the CyberTipline report and an operator elsewhere MUST discharge its own law's equivalent duty
For CSAM bases the substrate retains hash and minimal metadata for the legal window only, never content; the operator preserves outside the substrate; descent terminates at zero
Under CourtOrder the operator follows the court's timeline; the substrate logs the order text and the eviction
Every fast-path takedown enters a hard_case:fast_path_takedown row; reviewers MAY file reconsideration:procedural_error if the basis was misclassified
Immediate-removal bases have no counter-notice; Dmca512, DsaArticle16, CommunityStandards and OsaIllegalContent take counter-notice as a reconsideration row decided by a review-duty holder
An expeditious basis withholds then hard-deletes: Dmca512 10 d, DsaArticle16 14 d, OsaIllegalContent 14 d, CommunityStandards 30 d, counted per holder from its own tombstone execution
A takedown is reversed by an admitted reconsideration with outcome reversed naming the notice, signed by a key holding the review duty over the community; the reversal replicates
Whether bytes are withheld is computed at read time, never stored as a flag: withheld while an admitted notice stands with no admitted reversal
A reversal inside the window resumes serving, the sweep skips the bytes and the holder re-acknowledges here
A reversal after the window voids the notice, lifts the tombstone and restores standing; any remaining holder or the republishing publisher may serve; no holder must have kept a copy
A reversal of an immediate-removal takedown lifts the tombstone and restores standing but cannot restore destroyed bytes; the publisher may re-publish
An ordinary row about a subject is erased by the subject's own withdraws: rule 2 with a federation key, rule 3 through a delegates_to proxy chain with scope consent_revocation
An adverse row is reached by no subject-authority path; the producer withdraws it under rule 1 or refuses with reason; the subject's contest path is reconsideration
Erasure's replicated fact is the ordinary tombstone by digest per plane; there is no node-local purge basis; a purge-ledger entry is informational, never a notice
A hard case recording an erasure MUST NOT name the subject
Fast-path takedowns happen via this protocol and nowhere else; a takedown_notice targets content under a community's duty-holders only
federation_keys is not a takedown target; a notice demanding removal of key records for categories of participants is refused at the enforced-admission gate
The halt is no escalation path for takedown; it pauses agents' acts and touches no data door
A community operates and federates only while it has at least one active holder of its moderate duty
A community is admitted and continues to federate only while one member holds the live moderate duty; the creator names one at creation; without one it is non-conformant
When a community has no live moderate holder (lapse, inactivity past freshness, authority set narrowed, holder left) it locks read-only and elects by a 24 h ranked-choice vote over its roster
The election ballot orders the roster by highest moderation_track_record, then earliest membership by roster-lineage admission order, then lexicographic key_id; the members' votes appoint
If no eligible member can be named (track record, consent, accountable root) the community fails secure and MUST NOT federate or operate at moderated capability

A named moderator is an appointment: delegates_to from an authority in the community's authority set (founder or protocol-authorised key, an accountable root) to K, scope including the duty, community_id C; no new shape
is_named_moderator(K, C, duty) holds when a live delegates_to chain from an authority-set accountable root reaches K with every edge scope including the duty and community_id C
An appointment by anyone but a founder carries the consensus_protocol's own signatures; belonging to the authority set holds no duty
In an Anonymous Tier room the appointed moderator MAY be an anonymous identity; this reaches the room's duties only, never the review of a licence, which stays with its issuer
The election emits the same appointment shape: ballots are the room's protocol signatures, the winner's acceptance is consent; no node signs; one code path
An ungoverned room is locked and the lock ends only by the members' own hands or a steward's
An anonymous identity passes accountable_root as its own root, steward-bound to its user key, with the age band declared at first run
A founder is in the authority set under every consensus_protocol and keeps the zero-hop duty through a protocol change with no row written; the change narrows who may appoint, never who holds

An auto-promoted moderator holds the moderate, takedown and review duties; every action is constrained by the operational-language gate and reconsideration appeals; the duty is revocable and re-promotes on lapse
moderation_track_record rides scores; the existence invariant and auto-promotion are composition rules over delegates_to; no new primitive
The substrate MUST evaluate is_named_moderator for a community at admission and re-check at every federation apply step; a moderator-less community locks, elects and fails secure
No governance or consumer-policy layer may admit or sustain a moderator-less community into federation; the gate is substrate where the write lands
The moderator election is a 24 h ranked-choice vote over the roster, the community read-only throughout, the ballot reopening while nobody votes
Moderation is a delegable duty, not a platform role; a participant exercises moderate, takedown or review as self or delegates it to an agent or any trusted party via delegates_to
Every media or chat surface runs under the moderation duty, enforced at admission, as a condition of carrying content
A warning said as peer speech (a scores row naming a person) is the named person's to retract under rule 2, the retraction visible and the speaker attributed
A harm report filed with the named moderator is a duty-holder's record: the named person cannot withdraw it, contests it by reconsideration, sees it exists, its kind and consequence; never purgeable
The moderator's process MAY shield the reporter of a harm report; action on it runs under the floor, no single vote excluding; filing changes the duty, never the audience
A false report is contested like any other and the reporter answers for it on the record via moderation_track_record
The speaker of a retracted warning keeps their own words at self scope, served to no one, and may still file them with the moderator
Anyone MAY file a scores row against anything they see; it is an opinion visible to any reader who chooses; consumers compose filters over the score graph as consumer policy
A member MAY mute another: a reader-side filter changing no row, roster or standing, untold to the muted, never hiding a row that names the muter
A statement about a person is always visible to that person
A filter MAY escalate to an auto-finding, such as a watchlist match auto-firing a takedown_notice under an enabling authority
Acting on a group's behalf (takedown, ModerationEvent, appeal ruling) requires the delegated moderate, takedown or review duty; hiding for yourself needs none
moderation_track_record composites a moderator's action outcomes into a relative positional reputation, never a single global score
CEG names moderate, takedown, review and slash as canonical scope kinds and enforces their admission, mirroring consent_revocation
The moderate scope emits moderation ModerationEvents, report-to-scores, and age_assurance and content_class gates on the delegator's behalf
The takedown scope emits takedown_notice including the immediate-removal fast path
The review scope emits reconsideration appeal and review rows
The slash scope emits slashing verdicts and the quarantine marker plane
The subject of the target attestation holds standing to file reconsideration; a licence subject contests by reconsideration, never by withdrawal
A licence subject can see every licence about them, a read over rows they are party to
Contestation is at zero disclosure: the subject files band-blind and a duty-holder who can see the composition performs the valence-sensitive step
The person named always sees that a record about them exists, its kind, consequence and who answers; peer speech and an authority's act are visible in full
A duty-holder's record MAY withhold the reporter's identity and report content from the person named where the process protects the reporter
The principal an action is taken on behalf of is found by walking delegates_to upward from attesting_key_id; there is no on_behalf_of envelope field
A moderation action is admitted as-self when attesting_key_id holds the duty over the target: the content's own subject or the community's moderate holder
A moderation action is admitted as delegated when a live delegates_to chain with every edge bearing the scope runs from an accountable root holding the duty, depth at most 5, no edge revoked
Otherwise reject; a verifier MUST NOT read an absent principal field as as-self
A substrate SHOULD record which rule and which root admitted a moderation action
A delegate may further delegate a duty only if the delegator granted sub_delegation in the scope
Every sub-delegation attenuates, never expands: child scope is a subset of parent scope and constraints may be added but never removed
A delegation chain is depth-capped at 5
A withdraws against any delegates_to invalidates everything downstream for acts not yet taken; authority is judged at the act's signed instant
A withdrawal reaches forward: acts already taken stand; only a withdraws for a compromised key reaches back, to its revoked_after bound
A scope token MAY be sub-scoped to a dimension family (infra:attest:licensure:{authority}) under the attenuation rule; it adds no member to the closed infra set
Sub-scope matching is directional: a parent satisfies a check for its child, a child MUST NOT satisfy its parent; no prefix test
A verifier MUST match the full scope token with parent/child semantics and MUST NOT widen an unrecognized sub-scope to its parent; unknown caveats fail closed
The duty-holders of a takedown_notice target are the content's signed subject set plus named takedown holders of the content's community
The duty-holders of a moderation action against a subject are the named moderate holders of the relevant community
The duty-holders of a reconsideration against a prior action are the target's subject plus named review holders of that community; the ruling stays with review holders
A reconsideration against a licensure row is decided by the issuing authority set plus any review-scoped chain from it
As-self holds iff attesting_key_id is in the target's duty-holders; delegated holds iff the chain root is and is an accountable root; all resolvable from existing rows
The subject claim of a takedown or moderation action MUST be verified against the content's establishing attestation, not the action payload
subject_of(content_sha256) is the signed subject_key_ids of the establishing scores attestation the hash binds; resolved by the usual content-hash lookup
Admit-(a) subject-self means attesting_key_id is in the signed subject set; the payload's subject_key_ids MAY route or queue but MUST NOT be the admit set
If the establishing attestation is not locally held, subject_of is undetermined and subject-self fails; only the named-moderator path remains; absent provenance never admits
Every moderation action is delegate-signed, traceable to an accountable root and revocable; a demand to remove federation_keys fails the gate; the halt is no escalation path
Every new prefix admitted to the namespace passes the four-test gate; failures are reframed or rejected
A moderate holder may enable a watchlist for a group they moderate; the fabric matches at the publish seam and auto-fires takedown_notice for CSAM, else detection plus a moderation event
A watchlist is enabled per group by its moderate or takedown authority; a global scan-everything configuration is non-conformant
note: ambiguity: 1565 says a moderate holder enables; here moderate or takedown authority

gist: Watchlist enable and disable are signed by the authority and revocable by withdraws
Separation of powers: the fabric holds the matcher only, the operator the licensed hash database and report duty, the authority the per-group opt-in; no party does all three
Enabling a watchlist emits hard_case:watchlist_enabled with who and which list; every match emits hard_case:watchlist_match
Disabling a CSAM watchlist MUST be an audited withdraws that emits hard_case:watchlist_enabled (disable variant); silent removal is barred; non-CSAM lists toggle freely
Detection runs only at the publish seam of enabled groups; it cannot reach self or family E2EE content; no client-side scanning is mandated
federation_keys.identity_type is a set of roles; reserved-prefix gates are evaluated by set membership
Set membership grants the wire-level right to emit per held role
Consumer policy SHOULD treat an accord_holder key that also holds other roles with elevated scrutiny; cohabitation is not forbidden on the wire; dedicated keys recommended
A system row is emitted only by the running substrate; a key cohabiting a substrate role with an application role is still held to that reservation
identity_type is a set of role strings; a scalar is read as a singleton set
Emitter rules are evaluated as role membership in identity_type
The dimension namespace is independent of the role set
The envelope, the 1+4 primitives and subject_kinds are independent of the role set
identity_type is a set of role strings and a scalar reads as a singleton set; one key may hold many roles without new wire surface
attesting_key_id must differ from attested_key_id for capacity regardless of roles held; a folded agent plus detector key MUST NOT score its own capacity
Reasoning-trace emission needs no reserved identity_type; it rides the agent role's open-vocabulary surface
A cohabiting key emits agent-intent rows under agent dimensions and detector verdicts under detection; cohabitation grants the right on each surface, never merges them
The identity_type set encodes as sorted-ascending, deduplicated, comma-joined canonical bytes; a single role encodes as its scalar form
identity_type members are an open vocabulary owned by the reservations and sibling-component extensions, not a closed set
No cohabitation is forbidden at the wire layer; the substrate enforces gates by membership and cohabitation discipline is operator policy
Joining a geographic community is a one-way disclosure enforced at the wire, not by policy
A location_proof is emitted only by its subject (attesting equals subject) or by a delegates_to chain with scope consent_revocation; the substrate cannot mint one
A community cannot require a location_proof from non-members; it may only gate admission on whether a member produced one
A location_proof without the subject's own signature is rejected by the substrate
A demand for location_proofs of non-consenting subjects is refused at the door; the halt touches no data door; content disputes route through takedown under the duty-holder gate
location_proof.cell_resolution is at most 7; finer resolution is rejected at the substrate gate
The substrate emits hard_case:location_proof_resolution_violation on rejection; observability, not a slashing trigger
When a location_proof is withdrawn, forward visibility evicts: consumer policy treats the subject as having no current proof from withdrawal time on
A withdrawn location_proof leaves serving like any own row; the audit chain keeps the tombstone that a proof existed and was withdrawn, never the cell
A copy a peer took before a withdrawal reached it is not recalled by the wire; the tombstone is what every holder converges on
A standing location claim is bounded to resolution at most 7
A location claim exists only because the subject signed and emitted it
The subject can prove what they did or did not claim and when; the tombstone is the receipt and carries no cell
location_proof resolution is at most 7
Withdrawal of a location_proof is not retroactive
A location_proof is signed by the subject only or a delegates_to proxy chain
Geographic community admission composes by Policy M evaluate_subkind_admission
The wire format uses H3 only; operators may use other geospatial systems internally
Only location_proof is bounded to resolution 7; a community MAY scope its geographic_constraint at any resolution
Perceptual-hash matchers are pluggable; operators choose which to enable; CEG governs the access-policy contract only
The default operator path is a self-hosted PDQ matcher against feeds the operator obtains; the operator carries index freshness; feed terms apply
PerceptualHashCsam is the only legal_basis that consumes hash-match output as an immediate-removal trigger
An operator running a PDQ matcher MUST register its source feeds and freshness cadence via a system:perceptual_hash_matcher:registered row
CEG prescribes no hash database; matcher selection is operator policy
After genesis a curated batch of proposal Contributions is admitted via the amendment flow; content-neutral; the prefix gate keeps source-tradition vocabulary out
On departure from a family or self the departed party keeps the key_grants it holds; nothing is re-encrypted; new DEKs are no longer wrapped to it; no rotation ceremony
One identity MAY belong to multiple families; each family has its own DEK and roster
A cohort_scope family Contribution MUST carry family_id naming which family's DEK and visibility apply; the substrate rejects family-scoped rows without it
A new identity_occurrence is admitted on a signature from the root identity_key_id (until the self evicts its genesis key) or any active occurrence of that identity
note: tension within line: single-vouch heading vs strict-majority self-roster door for user-role keys

gist: A node-role signer vouches for an occurrence only through its live owner binding

A user-role key joins the self's roster by the self-roster door: one key by the owner's signature; two or more by a strict majority of the live roster or the lone path after its window with no objection
Higher-assurance setups MAY layer hardware_attestation requirements on occurrence admission via consumer policy
The four membership-event hard_case prefixes (occurrence added, family membership change, protocol change, protocol violation) are reserved to substrate_persist emitters
Family membership changes are not single-vouch; the family's consensus_protocol governs admission: founder_only, unanimous, majority, quorum, weighted, custom; open:self_admit for a public group
founder_only is conformant for a family and a publisher-gated subscription, refused for a community, and admissible for an affiliation only under the one-voice countersign rule
note: tension with 1493, which speaks of a community moving from founder_only

gist: consensus_protocol is amended under the same protocol's rules unless the family is consensus_protocol_entrenched; entrenched families reject amendments at the gate and need the out-of-band ceremony
No holding claim leaves a self or family cohort
HUMANITY_ACCORD is the canonical entrenched family instance
The consensus_protocol vocabulary is open; canonical kinds are named for coordination
A removal never re-encrypts history; it is never retroactive
Reverse quorum never admits anyone to a family or community and confers no consent; joining is proposal and acceptance
A decision opens a bounded window; one present accountable actor may act alone; on absence a count carries over the policy's named set; the absent never block
In the accord one present holder fires, and a roster change counts its yes-votes against the standing roster
In community moderation a present moderator acts; on the moderators' absence the live community governs its own content
A community is required to have a named moderator, the moderate-duty holder; it is the only required role
A community may name one or more stewards, steward-bound, who appoint and oversee moderators; a steward may add further stewards
A contested party must not mint co-stewards to manufacture a quorum or dilute a pending protective veto
At creation the creator chooses steward plus moderator, or moderator only
No quorum is imposed on a moderator or steward; either resolves an action by a single signature; a community may impose one on itself
Anyone may propose a moderation action by the open-labeling path, a report-to-scores Contribution against the target
A moderation proposal opens a 48-hour participation window
A moderator or any steward resolves a moderation action by a single signature at any point in the window
A single signature resolves content and a member's standing to speak: a withhold, a takedown of a row, a warning, a block for the room
A single signature never removes a member from the roster; removal is a roster change under the floor in every protocol, open admission included
No single key, a moderator's or a founder's, removes a member alone; a moderator appointed by one founder cannot remove another
At two members nobody is removed: unanimous removal and strict majority coincide only if the removed consents
Either member may leave by their own forward-only act, the last founder included; the founding-core rule belongs to infrastructure communities and conferring families, not rooms
A founder hands the room on by promoting a member to founder under the protocol, with that member's own signature
A room left with no founder locks and elects
If no moderator or steward acts within 48 h the proposal is tallied by live-majority vote over the community's live members
Presence asserts by a fresh proof-of-presence plus vote over the proposal nonce; a silent member is not in the denominator
The community fallback fires only on genuine moderator and steward absence; it is never a check on them
The 48 h window governs only the fallback; a moderator rules at any time and a withhold is immediate
A report filed privately with the duty holder opens no window, is seen by nobody else, and becomes the duty holder's record, the reporter shielded
A moderation action raised in the room is public, names what is asked, and starts the 48 h window at once
The client offers both the private report and the public action and never folds one into the other
A community with no live moderate holder locks: read-only to everyone, nobody posts, admits or acts until a moderator is seated
A locked room elects a moderator in a 24-hour vote
The ballot is the roster, every member a candidate, presented in worthiness order: track record, then admission order, then key; confirming as presented votes that order
Each person ranks up to three; one ballot per person however many keys, folded as a vote is
The count is instant runoff, weakest eliminated in turn, a tie broken against the later in worthiness order; the floor of two voices applies
The winner accepts by their own row; declining or silent past the room's grace passes the duty to the next in runoff order; nobody holds a duty unsigned
The voters' ballots are the appointment's signatures; no node signs anything
A room where nobody votes stays locked and the ballot stays open
A steward, where one exists, may appoint a moderator directly at any point and end the vote
The election id is the digest of the community id and the last seating row, or the roster genesis for a room never seated; a ballot names that id
A member leaving while locked changes nothing about the election; a lock traps nobody; nothing is admitted or removed
The electorate is the live roster at the count; a ballot from a member no longer live counts for nothing; the ballot stays open until a seating lands
The winner's acceptance row carries the election id and the digest of the ballot set it was counted over
A node admits an acceptance only when it holds the ballot set, the count yields the signer, the set meets the floor, and its own 24 h have passed
Among valid acceptances held a node seats the one counted over the larger set, on equal size the smaller digest; the seat follows rows held, never arrival
A node stores every ballot and acceptance it receives rather than refusing a late one; a ballot is void only against the winning seating; never unseat on arrival order
The small-room floor is the smaller of two voices and the roster size; a room of one elects itself; a founder is never locked out at zero hops
The ballot and acceptance are the rows ballot:moderator:v1 and ballot:moderator_acceptance:v1; the policy table row is moderator_election
A community may require a moderator quorum, full or live-within-window, riding its consensus_protocol applied to the moderate duty; unilateral is the default
A moderator quorum tightens the fast path without weakening the community-vote fallback; a steward or the community vote may set or change it
For a harm report the window's default outcome is removal; content survives only by an on-record keep: a moderator's or steward's approve-to-keep or a live-majority vote-to-keep
Passive survival is impossible: doing nothing in the window removes the content; surviving reported content is attributable by signature
A harm report is not a change proposal; the act that must land is the keep and the floor applies to the keep
A takedown notice under a legal basis is duty-holder-signed and executed without a window
Content the live majority flags but retains is auto-hidden behind an active interstitial
Clicking the interstitial publishes a viewer-side consent:state:granted with a consent:scope:view qualifier; every viewing is a signed act
The infohazard gate rides the content_class:infohazard or content_class:reported flag composed with the consent primitive; no new wire shape
Hard removal on the CSAM perceptual-hash tripwire, a takedown, or an undefended report; the removal action is on record and the content does not survive
Consent-gated retention after a live-majority flag puts each viewer on record by their interstitial consent row
Kept-visible content puts the approving moderator or steward, or the keep-voting majority, on record
A community with only one moderator and no steward must be warned to add a second moderator or a steward
A moderator's or steward's silence past the community's freshness window lapses the duty
Authority is reconstituted by merit auto-promotion: the highest moderation_track_record live member is auto-granted the moderate duty
note: contradiction with 1777: there no node can appoint and nobody holds a duty they never signed for; seat is by election and acceptance

gist: The protocol guarantees default-remove, attributable-keep, attributable-view; every transition is an attributable act by a named identity
A duty holder's look at reported material, or a reporter's prior exposure, is a moderation row naming duty, purpose, outcome and exposure, not a keep or view
Minimise: a known perceptual-hash match is removed and reported with no human eyes, ever; classifiers triage before a person is asked to look
Restrict: a person looks only under a named duty for a named purpose with the operator's viewer protections
Record: the look is signed as duty with its purpose and what followed; the mandated report rests on it
Report: an inadvertent exposure is reported promptly through the same channel
Where the duty holder acts for an organisation, the organisation is on the bond and the duty holder is its agent for provider protection
A keep or view that is not an act of a duty stays on the ladder, attributable and named
CEG refuses client-side scanning: detection runs only at enabled groups' publish or share seam, never over self or family private content
Presence is authority, absence forfeits it, a timer decides, at every scope; only the count set differs, which the policy table names
A lapsed steward's silence triggers merit re-auto-promotion
Every window door runs one decision shape of five numbers over a named standing set, published as a table
enact: approvals that land the change at once; a fraction of the base, strictly more; never below a strict majority; default two-thirds
cancel: objections that void the change at the window; at least the fraction; default one-third
floor: approvals the change must carry before silence may land it at the window; at least the fraction; default one-third
In a community the floor is never fewer than two voices, so one voice never decides who is in a room
Under invitation no single vote admits; the second voice is the invitee's own acceptance; a room of one grows by founder's proposal and newcomer's yes
Under open admission no single vote excludes; the two-voice guarantee attaches to removal

founder_only is a protocol for a family, a subscriber list and a room's own listing; a community naming it is refused federation_community_consensus_protocol_violation, recorded as hard_case:community_consensus_protocol_violation
window by sensitivity: 86400 s reversible content, 259200 s roster and standing, 604800 s irreversible
irreversible: no instant landing; the change waits its whole window even at full approval
The floor is a reverse-path predicate only: nothing lands before the window closes except at enact
The base is the standing roster at or below the count minimum, above it the member-only census expected-active count, falling at most a tenth per period, never below floor
A community may set its policy stricter than the defaults, up to a floor at enact, which switches the reverse path off
A policy is refused if cancel, floor or enact is reachable by one voice, the window is under its class, or cancel or floor exceeds enact (CLM-policy-corridor)

The governance policy table is published as data with decision function (policy, base, approvals, objections, elapsed) to lands, pending or cancelled, replayed rather than re-read (CLM-governance-policy-table)
Every two-path row is an instance of the two-path model the build regenerates and checks; a row breaking its invariants fails the build
Table rows: the three defaults by class; community invitation (invitee's acceptance still required) and removal (forward only, cosigned)
The self roster row: one person's keys, a floor of one key and its own 24 h window
Three rows run under their own rule: the moderation fallback, the halt's fire-and-fuse, and the custodian's cosigned replacement
Every window is measured by each node from the instant it first held the proposal, never from a signed instant; cosigned_at decides nothing
Two nodes may close a window at different moments; nothing lands early at either
Votes travel on objection:{state}: proposal, assent, raised
cancel_over is the cancel denominator: the base with the proposer counted for a community; the other keys for a self roster
at_window: cancelled for every community row; stay_open for the self roster, cleared by the proposer's withdrawal or the target's act; the halt lapses; a moderation proposal is tallied
A node's state is the set of rows it holds, each with the instant it first held it, and nothing else
The first-held instant is the node's own receipt, outside the signed row and never replicated; every window runs from it
An object's state, a person's standing toward it and a room's seated roles are folds over the held set, never stored verdicts
The step takes the held set, one row and the instant; answers enabled for the signer's standing or refused by name; an admitted row is appended, nothing rewritten
Queue, preview and door are one function run over enabled transitions, a row before signing, or an arriving row; the preview is exact because it is the door
A transition under a policy of more than one voice is admitted as a row at once and moves the object only when the fold meets the policy's numbers
The instant is the one input from outside, for windows; the processor keeps no clock
The impact an item shows is the difference between the fold before and after, with the family's columns for undo, never a stored field
Counts and standings are the same on every node holding the same rows; window answers are this node's; the clock gates admission and never the count
The processor does not model signatures, transport, other nodes' holdings, projections, text, or any reader's weighting, which is composition and never admission
Every decision a person is asked to make is one choice_item object; its context says which kind
An item carries context, facts displayed never chosen with provenance wire, by_rule or not_sent, a policy row of the governance table, and options each with a non-empty benefit and downside
A first-run or consent item runs the self row, one voice of one, no window; a room's item runs the room's row
An option's impact is derived from the family model for the rows it writes: what moves, where, widen or narrow, undoable; never written by hand
Four kinds and no more: choice, act, entry, notice; consent is not a kind but a choice whose writes are consent rows
A first run has no separate class of consents; nothing in it is required except what the node needs to run
The node keeps one queue of items awaiting the person's signature; the person signs, the row lands; an agent signs no item of a person's queue
A node holding the person's pen may re-sign a chosen row to refresh or supersede it only as the same row: same scope, prefixes and peer, or a later-allowed peer
A re-signed row is never wider, which is a new choice needing an item, and never after the person withdrew it; a withdrawal stands until answered again
A vote counts once per person whatever their devices: a roster seats a key, the person is the fedID of its self roster, and a tally counts fedIDs
Every vote row is admitted and kept; the count is a permutation-invariant clock-free fold: agreeing rows one voice, disagreeing rows no voice until a withdrawal leaves one
Nothing is refused at the door for arriving second; no instant orders two devices' rows; every node holding the same rows reaches the same count
An agent signs its own rows under its own key and steward binding; a person may delegate goals or roles to it by a row the person signs
An answer records the state (served, held, signed, deferred, changed), the value, the digest of the item as shown, and the rows once they exist
Declining is a complete answer and never a failed vote
A choice that sends the person's content or their agent's traces beyond their own circle starts unanswered and is never preselected
Announcing starts on with its cost on screen; it sends the binding and delegations to trusted roots, never content; content keeps the smallest cohort scope by default
A default is otherwise admissible only for a choice that narrows or keeps things as they are, and every default's cost is on screen
Relay offering is on by default for servers and home nodes under the device policy; it carries sealed rows and discloses the route only; it may be turned off
An unanswered choice the node does not need never blocks: it is deferred, nothing leaves on its account, and it waits in the queue
An option that cannot be undone is never a default and is confirmed before signing; a narrowing option takes one step
An outward-writing item answered before a claim is held and not applied, no owner key existing, and lapses if the claim never comes
An item writing nothing outward applies at once; the owner's signed row supersedes the local record after the claim
A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone
A client renders two served shapes and nothing else: the view (view.cddl) and the queue
The view is one object's rows and the atoms the node folded through the person's policies, each with provenance: the rows read and the rule run
Every string the client shows is a node-served text reference resolved for the asked locale; the client holds no copy; an unlocalizable string is served in source language, marked
While a bundle lacks a locale the node serves the reference with source text marked; a consumer may resolve the id from a held bundle, preferring the node's localized text
The client holds the deployment's keys (user, node, agent), each signing only its own rows, and no policy; a view is read through the person's trust set
For an object the person can see the node holds its family, lifecycle state and the person's standing: author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness
A family's lifecycle is its transitions in the family model, each a verb with states, roles that may sign, governance row and whether it widens
The queue is exactly the transitions enabled for this person in this state, one item each; the door is the same predicate, so queue and door never disagree
A stranger to an object sees no item on it; an item that moved the object is gone from the next view
A widening item is confirmed before it is signed and a narrowing one takes one step
A node derives the queue from the same held rows and policy it admits by, never from a separate list
An item never crosses between nodes; only the rows an answer signs travel; other devices learn by the row; each node keeps its own queue and none is synchronised
The queue never blocks: transport carries signed rows and cosignatures and reports a decision row landed; the host decides from the rows which items present
A missing key, unreachable peer or evicted chunk resolves to less access and an honest miss, never silent plaintext downgrade or fabricated success
Per-subscriber key_grant cascade distributes the 32-byte epoch key to the community roster against a rotating key
The epoch-DEK key_grant cascade wraps a DEK only for a kept stream
A wrapped DEK MUST be wrapped with wrap_algorithm v2 (X25519 + ML-KEM-768), never v1
A consumer MUST reject a streaming epoch grant carrying wrap_algorithm v1
Streaming PQC envelope: content AES-256-GCM, DEK wrap X25519+ML-KEM-768, authenticity Ed25519+ML-DSA-65, hashes SHA-256, transit E1 hybrid
The hybrid wrap construction has exactly one wire identifier x25519_mlkem768_aes256_gcm_hkdf_sha256; producer, substrate and consumer MUST serialize and accept only that byte string
Streaming epoch wrap, self/family at-rest wrap and media-DEK wrap are one construction under one identifier; a consumer MUST NOT treat them as distinct or define a field-local spelling
The hyphenated form and every case, separator or ordering variant of the wrap identifier MUST be rejected as an unknown wrap_algorithm under closed-set fail-secure decode
A consumer MUST NOT normalize case or separators of a vocabulary identifier before comparison
An assurance rung presented across communities MUST NOT become a cross-service correlation handle; presentation unlinkability is a required property
No presentation surface may bake a mandatory stable identifier across verifiers into the wire contract; the unlinkable upgrade MUST remain a format addition, never a re-issuance
Every wire-vocabulary identifier is lowercase ASCII snake_case and matched by exact byte comparison
Domain-separation constants (KEY_GRANT_V1_INFO, stream-nonce label, symbol label, HPKE_SUITE_ID) MUST be used exactly as written, never snake_cased, never compared against vocabulary identifiers
The epoch index is monotonic per stream_id and a separate addressing axis from key_grant.rotation_chain
Content-addressed grant rotation is addressed by (at_rest_sha256, attested_key_id); rotation_chain is an informative trail; no row supersedes or removes a wrap
Stream/epoch grant rotation is addressed by (stream_id, epoch, recipient); a rotation is a new row under a new axis identity with the same rotation_chain trail
Once a member leaves, subsequent content is sealed under an epoch key they cannot derive (forward secrecy)
Member removal from a gated roster forces a mandatory epoch rotation (coalesced; exempt for ungated public broadcasts)
Member addition advances the epoch; a joiner derives only current and later epochs; for a kept stream earlier epochs reach it as key_grant:stream:v1 wraps within the catch-up bound
Time or byte-count hygiene rotation is optional operator policy, default off
The substrate MUST coalesce all removals admitted within one STH cadence window T (default 2 s) into a single epoch rotation; a removed member's exposure is at most T
For a live_stream with an ungated roster (open admission on a public community, grants to any requester) member removal MUST NOT force rotation; hygiene and nonce bounds still apply
Rotation on member removal is mandatory for every gated roster (bounded membership or admission ceremony)
Epoch-DEK rekey on member change is MLS TreeKEM (RFC 9420): O(log N) path rekey, commit signed once, blank-node and parent-hash handling; the hybrid KEM is the ciphersuite's HPKE KEM
One DEK per (stream_id, epoch): for live participants the group's MLS exporter secret for the epoch is the epoch DEK; MLS is the only live distributor, no second key
The same epoch DEK is wrapped as key_grant:stream:v1 rows (one per recipient, wrap v2) for late joiners and recordings, only for a kept stream (recorded or history_on_join full)
An unrecorded live call wraps nothing; its DEK exists only inside the live MLS group
DEK(stream_id, epoch) = HKDF-SHA256 over MLS-Exporter(label ciris-stream-dek/v1, empty context, 32), empty salt, info = label || stream_id_utf8 || epoch_be8, length 32
epoch_be8 is the u64 epoch big-endian; no length prefix on stream_id is needed in the DEK info
A key_grant:stream:v1 wraps the per-stream DEK and opens exactly one stream; the MLS exporter secret itself is never wrapped
Conformance of the per-stream DEK derivation is proven by a known-answer test set published with CIRISVerify
history_on_join is set per stream by its producer; a call is N streams; no room policy makes another producer's stream kept
Turning kept on mid-stream wraps the current and later epochs only; earlier epochs' DEKs were never wrapped and are gone
Turning kept off is forward-only: wraps already issued are not unmade (withdraws on a key_grant is refused) and wrapping stops from the next epoch
A stream is kept when its genesis envelope carries history_on_join full or when key_grant:stream:v1 wraps exist for it; recorded is not a field
A recording is an after-the-fact video blob with derived_from stream_id; any retention promise rides the producer's consent:deletion_sla
MLS (ciphersuite 0x004D X-Wing) exporter keys scope only two things: addressing (record and destination secrets) and live call media (the stream DEK seed)
Content at rest (chat bodies, files, kept streams) is sealed under content DEKs carried by the flat per-recipient key_grant cascade on three axes: epoch, stream, content
The MLS group never keys a chat body
Which key mechanism applies is fixed by the content's class, never a deployment setting; the split is wire-invisible (tree position rides the opaque key_grant payload)
Forward secrecy is forward-only by default; post-compromise security is not provided by default; a deployment MAY enable it by requiring periodic TreeKEM self-updates
Catch-up bound is min(operator depth cap, chunk-eviction horizon); eviction horizon, the 72 h holding liveness and grant durability are three distinct windows
A catch-up request against an evicted epoch returns ContentMiss, fail-honest, never a silent gap
Operators MUST ship the catch-up depth cap with the cascade
For self or family cohort_scope content the substrate MUST NOT emit any holding claim observable outside the cohort; custody:ack is placed at the content's scope and replicated to members only
Self and family content bytes are delivered to admitted cohort members via the at-rest encryption flow, never via the public holder-discovery directory
A row moves to a peer only when requested, required or appropriate, never merely because it is federation-tier; federation tier means shareable, not copied to everyone
Requested means the peer's own pull for a subject or dimension; an automatic diff is not a request
Required means what a peer must hold to seal, address and take part: the consent-free set and the rows of the cohorts it belongs to
Appropriate means the row's audience names the peer (addressed to, about, or placed in its cohort), the family's replication tier and audience deciding
A consent:replication grant names the class it moves and moves that class only; it does not make a peer a mirror of the grantor's corpus
Anti-entropy over the commons runs among serve seats; a seat offers a person's node only what is required or appropriate, the rest waits on a pull
A node with no owner holds only what it must to seal and address peers it dials plus what a referred peer asks; never a copy of the mesh
What is required moves before any walk; what is offered unasked is live state; a superseded row moves only on request
A non-member peer cannot issue ContentFetch for self/family bytes because no holding claim it can observe names a holder
A non-member peer cannot discover self/family bytes exist via the substrate; the only attestations referencing them are cohort-scoped and never federate
Structural invisibility buys content-holding confidentiality only, not relationship, metadata, traffic-analysis or unobservability privacy; do not represent CEG as providing those
For self/family content the substrate MUST NOT emit a holding claim for the evidence_refs bytes outside the cohort
The substrate MUST NOT propagate self/family content beyond its scope via any other directory or discovery surface
At-rest grant recipients are all current identity_occurrences of the attesting key (self) or all current members of the named family (family)
Recipient KEM keys are resolved from the current occurrence's encryption_pubkeys
A recipient with no valid ML-KEM-768 key is excluded from the grant; the substrate MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or wrap_algorithm v1
On a fail-secure skip the substrate emits hard_case:recipient_excluded into the self/family scope with recipient, reason and the skipped envelope ref; scoped to the cohort, never federates
The substrate MUST wrap self/family content DEKs via key_grant with wrap_algorithm v2 to each recipient's x25519 and ml_kem_768 keys
Structural invisibility (holding claims never leave the cohort, no propagation beyond scope) is unconditional: no discovery attestation federates
A body written at self, family, community or affiliations tier is always sealed by the substrate under the DEK cascade with wrap_algorithm v2; no operator switch turns that off
The only plaintext bodies at those tiers are those of authorized infrastructure communities and public rooms, placed at federation scope with holding claims
Persist wraps the DEK (v2) under each admitted identity_occurrence's occurrence_key_id (self) or each member key_id in the family roster (family)
New occurrence or new family-member admission triggers retroactive key_grant emission for all extant self/family content
The wrap target is the recipient's content-KEM keys from its current non-superseded within-valid_until identity_occurrence.encryption_pubkeys, not its signing key
A recipient whose current occurrence carries no valid ML-KEM-768 key MUST be fail-secure excluded from the grant; the substrate MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or v1
To be an at-rest-encryption recipient an identity MUST have a federation-present occurrence carrying encryption_pubkeys
On every fail-secure skip the substrate MUST emit hard_case:recipient_excluded:{scope_key_id} into the affected scope carrying the excluded key_id, a reason and the skipped envelope ref
The recipient_excluded event is cohort-scoped and MUST NOT federate beyond the self/family

One audience rule at every tier: community/affiliations holding claims reach members only; federation holding claims are the holder directory; custody, replication and anti-entropy run alike in every cohort
A self Contribution promoted via supersedes to community emits holding claims at the new scope on the new Contribution at promotion; the original's bytes stay invisible at federation
Self content naming a non-self subject stays in the author's self; the subject gets no key_grant, keeps revocation authority, and gets bytes only by re-emit at a wider scope
Consumers verify witness cosignatures and the witness quorum on a log's tree heads
POST /v1/transparency/sth/cosign (public): a witness posts a cosignature on (tree_size, root_hash, signed_at)
The Registry verifies an STH cosignature's hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 against the witness pubkey in the witness directory and persists on success
STH cosign request body: tree_size, root_hash hex, canonical signed_at, witness_key_id, both signature halves, and the consistency_proof root, tree_size and path
A witness MUST sign canonical = sha256 of ciris.sth_cosign.v1 header plus tree_size, root_hash_sha256 and signed_at lines
STH cosignature: Ed25519 over canonical; ML-DSA-65 over canonical || ed25519_sig (bound payload)
The witness directory also witnesses trust-root lineage heads: the lineage's signed roster record at a version, named by the SHA-256 of its signed bytes
The Registry verifies a lineage-head cosignature against the witness's key record in the charter's witness directory for that lineage, never a directory of its own
The Registry refuses a lineage-head witness that is not independent of the lineage under T6 at the cosignature's signed_at
The Registry rejects a lineage-head cosignature whose signed_at is more than 5 minutes from its own clock at receipt
Lineage-head cosign request body: lineage_key_id, head digest, prior head digest (empty on first), signed_at, witness_key_id, both signature halves
A witness MUST sign canonical = sha256 of ciris.lineage_head_cosign.v1 header plus lineage_key_id, head digest, prior head digest and signed_at lines
Lineage-head cosignature: Ed25519 over canonical; ML-DSA-65 over canonical || ed25519_sig; its domain label is distinct so it can never be replayed as an STH cosignature or the reverse
A witness MUST verify before signing that a lineage head descends from or equals the prior head it cosigned; equality MUST be accepted; descent follows the prev_head_digest chain
On a witness's first lineage cosignature the prior head is the lineage's genesis head from the bundle
The Registry MUST reject a lineage cosignature naming a prior it did not record for that witness, or a head that neither equals nor descends from it (LINEAGE_HEAD_INCONSISTENT)

A quorum-valid head not descending from the witnessed head is a fork attempt: recorded once per (lineage, fork point), never cosigned, further attempts counted not stored, hard_case:lineage_fork_attempt raised, nothing frozen
Two heads each reaching the charter's witness_quorum are equivocation: hard_case:lineage_equivocation is raised and head adoption freezes under T6

A lineage whose newest cosignature is older than witness_cadence_secs is silent: a T4 liveness signal never a validity leg; unattachable once attach_window_secs lapses, attachable again on re-commitment
A witness signing an STH MUST first verify a consistency proof from the prior STH it cosigned, or from genesis on its first cosignature against this log
