The Registry MUST reject an STH cosign request that omits the consistency_proof fields or whose proof does not verify against the named prior STH
The Registry anchors the consistency check against the prior (tree_size, root_hash) it recorded for that witness, never one the requester claims

A missing proof when a prior STH exists or a tree_size behind the witness's prior is MALFORMED_REQUEST; a proof not reconstructing both roots is CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID; a first cosignature is exempt
Bytes cited by SHA-256 in evidence_refs travel via Edge ContentFetch, ContentBody and ContentMiss; holders are discovered via custody:ack here rows at the content's scope; node-mode peers serve bytes
A reasoning trace is durable only when anchored on the record of an act
Every execution path producing an external effect MUST close with a terminal result row; the trace it anchors is carried as trace:complete:v1 or its post-scrub trace_summary
An in-flight trace with no terminal row is working state; the substrate MUST purge it after a declared bounded age (orphan sweep) and MUST export a count of traces purged
A substrate MUST NOT be read as having lost evidence when an unacted deliberation ages out; any such loss is a defect of the action-emission path, not the purge
Until terminal-row totality over effect-producing paths is tested, the invariant MUST be represented as a named wager wherever the control is claimed; the register carries its status
An operator needing interrupted-path forensics MUST enable a bounded privacy-scoped incomplete-receipt plane as an explicit opt-in; it is never the default
A custody:ack here report is live for 72 hours from its instant; after that the holder reads unknown
A consumer MUST attempt at most 2 holders in parallel and accept the first successful full-SHA verification
On ContentMiss a consumer MUST NOT withdraw the holder's report; only its signer retracts a holding claim
On ContentMiss the consumer records the miss and downweights the holder in its own holder resolution; the holder's next acknowledgement reports none
For a chunked object the 2-holder cap applies per chunk: no chunk is requested from more than 2 holders in parallel; in-flight depth per holder is the implementer's
Local-tier signature deferral: a producer's self-attestation skips the hybrid signature locally and signs only at federation-tier promotion
A row is local-tier-eligible iff it is the producer's own act under its own authority; the discriminator is whose act the row is, not whether subject_key_ids is empty
A producer's own-act row MAY name a subject in subject_key_ids and remain local-tier-eligible
Every listed subject keeps withdrawal authority over the row; a subject's later withdraws or consent:state:revoked is that subject's own signed Contribution, never a durable local row
A subject's consent:state:revoked or withdraws against a Contribution naming it MUST NOT use local-tier deferral and MUST promote to federation-tier within the window (24 h default, operator-tunable)
The substrate MUST emit hard_case:consent_revocation_promotion_overdue when a subject-side revocation has been local-tier longer than the window without promotion
LensCore composes detection:consent:promotion_delay_pattern on overdue emissions for operator monitoring; not a slashing trigger on its own
An agent's consent:partnered self-attestation MAY ride local tier; the user's consent:state:revoked against it MUST NOT
A subject-side revocation is federation-tier by classification: it MAY transit the local write path but MUST NOT rest there; its only terminal state is promoted, never a durable local row
The substrate MUST drive a subject revocation to federation-tier promotion within the window; overdue-flagged is a recorded breach, not a resting state
When the window lapses without promotion the substrate MUST emit hard_case:consent_revocation_promotion_overdue
The consent-promotion gate and the local read-gate read the same overdue state, so a subject revocation is never both invisible to federation and un-flagged
Merge policy is a normative property of the subject_kind declared here; the substrate MUST NOT infer policy per record type
organization and org_membership merge lww_skew_bounded with withdrawal_forward_only: an admitted withdraws is forward-only and a later non-withdrawn write does not resurrect
organization and org_membership: latest asserted_at wins; tie-break smallest attestation_id
The forward-only withdrawal on org rows is a lightweight authz flag, not the DEK-cascade crypto path; Commons tier, no DEK exists
The licence (licensure:{authority_id}) merges monotonic_quorum on license_id: a write whose revision decreases never enters the merge
Licence MergeBallot comparator: quorum_weight, then signed timestamp, then content hash; quorum above time
On licence conflict the more restrictive state wins: revoked over suspended over active
revocation and the three membership revocations merge monotonic_quorum with the same anti-rollback and comparator as the licence row
key:revocation:v1 merges on its digest subject revoked_key_sha256_ed25519_raw; membership revocations merge on the member key_id

Keys, attestations, occurrences, families, communities and location_proofs admit content-addressed and idempotent: same content same envelope_hash dedups; rotation collisions rejected non-destructively
For every lww_skew_bounded subject_kind the substrate MUST reject at admission an envelope with asserted_at later than now plus the 5-minute skew tolerance (CLOCK_SKEW_VIOLATION)
The steward-signature admission quorum (M-of-N over identical JCS bytes, Verify's layer) is not the region merge quorum (quorum_weight, substrate's layer); neither counts the other
A tier is recorded substrate state on an attestation, not a new primitive; the 1+4 surface is unchanged
A write is local-tier-eligible iff it is the producer's own act under its own authority
A listed subject's own withdraws or consent:state:revoked MUST go signed and promote within the window, never a durable local row
witness_relation MUST be self for any local-tier write
Promotion computes the hybrid signature and flips the row federation-visible; it is idempotent (promoting a federation row returns it unchanged)
At promotion the tiered-scope promotion and the holding claim at the new scope fire as for any federation write; promotion is the federation-emit moment
The promotion signature MUST cover JCS(contribution_envelope), the identical bytes a natively federation row signs; a promoted row is byte-indistinguishable with no was-promoted marker
Substrate columns (tier, promoted_at, storage bookkeeping) are never in the canonical bytes; only the envelope member set is canonicalized
Promotion MUST canonicalize the exact member set committed at local write; a field omitted MUST NOT be materialized at promote and vice versa; the substrate MUST NOT re-default
Registry owns the envelope member set and the verifier recomputes identical JCS bytes; the verifier's length-prefixed signing_bytes framing is never used for a promoted attestation
A local-tier row's signature MAY be absent (deferred); it is not federation-visible
A local-tier row is readable only by the producing occurrence; every other caller, even an authorized family or community peer, sees nothing
A federation-tier row carries the hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signature, is federation-visible per cohort_scope and the 5.2 rule, written by direct signed write or promotion
The substrate MUST enforce tier = federation implies hybrid signature present; nothing crosses to federation-visible unsigned
A local row is labelled local and MUST NOT be served as federation-authoritative
The read-gate (local implies caller is the producing occurrence) is an additional filter orthogonal to cohort_scope, composing with the 5.2 membership predicate

Every federation-tier admission gate MUST verify both halves, Ed25519 over JCS(envelope) and ML-DSA-65 over JCS(envelope) || ed25519_sig, and MUST reject a Contribution carrying only the classical half
The hybrid-at-admission rule binds all operational-authority gates: operational_admit (key_grant, partner, org-membership, license), the transport_destination binding, and founder-quorum gates
The hybrid-required check is immediate and always-on: no opportunistic window, no fleet-floor trigger, no require_hybrid false posture, never an operator toggle
A key without a valid ML-DSA-65 half is not conformant for federation-tier emission and is confined to local tier until it is
The hybrid mandate applies at the federation admission boundary only; local-tier rows MAY still defer the signature
A federation-tier trace written to the durable replicated corpus MUST carry the ML-DSA-65 half and a verifier MUST check it on ingest; no testimony-leaf exemption
A substrate persisting or replicating a federation-tier row whose signature lacks a valid ML-DSA-65 half MUST reject it at the ingest gate; store-then-quarantine is non-conformant
The uniform read filters on (dimensions[], valid_at, confidence_floor, subject_key_id?, scope)
dimensions[] is an open-vocabulary set of prefix strings matched by hierarchical prefix, not a closed enum; an exact string matches exactly
The bounded query surface is the closed set of five predicates with no caller-composed SQL or projections; open data, closed operators
valid_at filters asserted_at <= valid_at < COALESCE(expires_at, infinity); confidence_floor filters weight >= floor
The scope predicate applies both the 5.2 target-membership gate and the tier read-gate; reads are gated by scope, not by dimension authority
Write-side reserved-prefix emitter gates are unaffected by the query surface
A conforming consumer MUST verify the full SHA-256 of received bytes against evidence_refs before handing them to any consumer, regardless of how it found the holder
Bytes that fail the full-SHA check MUST be discarded and the holder reported per consumer policy (a negative score)
A failed fetch is never answered by a withdraws of another device's holding claim
Every descriptor that cites a blob (multimedia Source, chunk descriptor, SkillImportManifest entries, build manifest_size) carries the blob's byte length beside its digest
A bare evidence_refs string carries no size; a consumer fetching it enforces the 2.6.1.3 cap and MUST NOT invent a size field on the envelope
The consumer MUST compare received length to the declared size before computing the digest; a mismatch is a refusal without reading the rest; an overrunning ContentFetch is refused
A live stream in progress is the one descriptor with no total size; each chunk and the init segment carry their own; the recording is an ordinary blob with one
A conforming consumer MUST decide whether and how to render a blob from the verified bytes and its own policy, never from a claim in the descriptor
After verification the consumer MUST sniff the leading bytes and require the sniffed essence to equal the declared format; a mismatch is a refusal, not a correction
For a sealed descriptor the sniff runs where the bytes decrypt, by the opener, against the format inside the seal; a holder that cannot open does not sniff
Declared format and codec are inputs to the sniff comparison and capability checks, never authorisations
The renderable set is recommended consumer policy, not normative; a consumer MAY adopt a narrower set; a wider one is its own risk
image/jpeg, png, gif: Tier A render; at most 16 MB and 33 Mpx; GIF pixel and frame caps; reject bytes after IEND or FFD9
image/webp: Tier A conditional; at most 10 MB; node runs a WebP sanitizer and re-encodes on ingest
text/plain: Tier A; valid UTF-8, at most 1 MB, bidi controls rendered visibly
video/mp4: Tier A conditional; codec present and avc1 up to L4.1 plus mp4a.40.2 only; caps; node runs hardened MP4 sanitiser; unlisted tracks rejected
audio/mp4 (mp4a.40.2) and audio/mpeg: Tier A; ID3v2 ignored, APIC never decoded
AVIF, HEIC, JXL, WebM, MOV, MKV, Ogg, FLAC, WAV, ADTS, Markdown: Tier B; sender converts to a Tier-A form before hashing; raw arrival is Tier C
image/svg+xml: Tier C for the bytes, never a client renderer or WebView; a node MAY emit a derived PNG rendition from a hardened isolated rasteriser, which is Tier A
application/pdf: Tier C download; a node MAY rasterise pages to attested PNG in an isolated process
model_3d (glTF, USDZ, FBX, splats): Tier C download; a node MAY rasterise a PNG poster in an isolated process
HTML, Office, fonts, archives, TIFF, PSD, BMP, ICO and everything else: Tier C refuse; generic card, external handoff, dangerous-extension block on save
The ingest pipeline (size, then full-SHA, then sniff on verified bytes, memory-safe decode, re-encode, strip metadata, emit rendition) runs on the node; clients render only node-produced bytes
Decoders for every Tier-A format MUST be memory-safe; images, SVG and audio decode in memory-safe code; for video memory-safe code validates container and stream, hardware decodes
The delivery axis is an endpoint, envelope and composition extension; the 1+4 primitive set is untouched
Observer-share directed delivery: a single Contribution to a subscriber set, no stream_id, riding per-subscriber key_grant and Policy M membership
Media multicast: a live_stream chunk DAG keyed per (stream_id, epoch), live media keyed from the group exporter, kept epochs carried by per-recipient key_grant:stream:v1 wraps
Per-chunk sealing is SFrame's per-frame AEAD (RFC 9605) with KID = stream_id, CTR = counter, AEAD AES-256-GCM, keys per MLS epoch
The 12-byte chunk nonce is the STREAM layout: prefix[7] || counter_be[4] || last_flag[1]
prefix[7] is derived not transmitted: HKDF-SHA256(epoch_dek; info)[0..7], info = ciris-stream-nonce/v1 || stream_id_utf8 (lowercase hex of the 32-byte digest) || epoch_be8
The nonce-prefix info encoding (epoch as u64 big-endian, no length prefix on stream_id) MUST be byte-identical across producer, substrate and every consumer
counter_be[4] is 32-bit big-endian with a hard ceiling of 2^32-1 chunks per epoch; the substrate MUST force an epoch roll before wrap
Recommended operational cap MAX_CHUNKS_PER_EPOCH = 2^24, operator-tunable
last_flag is 0x01 on the final chunk of an epoch and 0x00 otherwise; set by the epoch terminator, not a header field; every holder derives it from the epoch's seal
Within one epoch the counter is strictly monotonic and never wraps; across epochs the counter reset is nonce-safe because the DEK changes
The counter space of a (stream_id, epoch) is owned by exactly one sender, the producer; two senders MUST NOT seal chunks under the same (stream_id, epoch) DEK
In group video each participant emits their own live_stream with their own stream_id, so the nonce prefix is per-sender unique
The substrate MUST reject a chunk append whose (stream_id, seq) collides with an existing sealed chunk
Realtime group communication composes from community, live_stream, chat_message and member/transport resolution with zero new structural primitives
In a group call each participant emits a live_stream of their A/V scoped to the channel community and subscribes to peers
Screen sharing is a live_stream whose source is a screen capture, one-to-N within the channel, same chunk seal and epoch DEK
Channel text chat is chat_message at cohort_scope community with community_id the channel; threads via topical_relation replies_to
A channel is a persistent community whose roster gates who can join the call or read the chat
Sub-channels are nested community membership; a sub-channel's members are a subset of the parent space roster
Presence is the reachable set: node-local, never an attestation, never logged
Invite is membership:proposal:v1; join is admission by widening on the invitee's own membership:acceptance:v1; decline is membership:decline:v1; leave is a forward-only withdraws
Broadcast (1:N large N) is pull-only ContentFetch with no relay tree
Realtime small or medium groups (calls, huddles, about 50 or fewer) use direct Reticulum Links between participants, symmetric mesh, no relay tree
Realtime large groups (well over 50 in one A/V room) use pull-only ContentFetch as for broadcast; no selective-forwarding relay role
A live chunk and a stored chunk are the same sealed object; recording is retention over existing chunks, VOD is pulling from offset zero, a licence is an owner-issued key_grant
For realtime groups PQC is unchanged and mandatory: epoch DEK wrapped wrap_algorithm v2 at rest, hybrid KEX in transit
A persistent channel is a long-lived community; an ad-hoc call is an ephemeral community with short valid_until torn down on last leave; no session primitive
The realtime chunk payload codec is opaque to the substrate; codec_id is a 1-byte clear discriminator on the transport chunk header, not on the attestation envelope
codec_id (1 byte) plus ChunkLayer (3 bytes) form a 4-byte block at SealedAvChunk header offset 48..52, clear metadata outside the AEAD; a peer serves one layer without opening the seal
codec_id 0x01 is AV1 SVC (3 spatial x 4 temporal x N SNR layers, base required); the production default
codec_id 0x02 is JPEG XS layered; reserved
codec_id 0x03 is symmetric MDC, the substrate design target; reserved, no production encoder assumed
codec_id 0x04 is temporal-layered with one spatial layer: ChunkLayer {0, t, 0}, base t = 0; the codec is named by the stream's binding, the id carries layer semantics only
codec_id 0xFF is opaque with no scalable semantics; its ChunkLayer MUST be {0,0,0}; default for non-layered streams and audio
codec_id 0x05 to 0x7F are reserved for future CEG-assigned standardized codecs
codec_id 0x80 to 0xFE are experimental per-deployment with no cross-federation meaning guaranteed
Every client decodes codec_id 0xFF (audio) and 0x01 (production default); a client SHOULD decode 0x04
A publisher MAY emit codec_id 0x04 only where it cannot encode 0x01 in real time
A receiver that cannot decode a stream's video keeps its audio and the client says so
Shedding reads the layer never the codec id: the base of a layered stream is its ChunkLayer base and an opaque stream is base
The substrate (Edge) never picks the codec; choice is upstream at the agent or server tier; SubStreamPath is reserved for amendment
Any high-frequency mutable shared state rides the same realtime transport with an application-defined payload codec; the wire (epoch DEK, STREAM nonce seal, per-stream STH) is identical
Convergent-merge logic for shared mutable state (CRDT, OT, LWW) is application-layer, not a CEG primitive; CEG carries the ops and the application converges them
A codified merge primitive, if ever added, routes through the amendment process
SealedAvChunk layout: stream_id 32 bytes (sha256 of stream_meta), epoch u64 BE, chunk_seq u64 BE, codec_id u8, layer spatial/temporal/quality u8 each, then double_sealed_ciphertext
CHUNK_HEADER_LEN is 48 (stream_id, epoch, chunk_seq) and CHUNK_CODEC_LAYER_LEN is 4
The 4-byte codec block is always present: the header is 52 bytes; a shorter wire or a ciphertext lacking its AEAD tag is refused as malformed
codec_id and layer are clear metadata, not AEAD inputs; a peer serves one layer without touching the inner DEK; tampering causes mis-decode or drop, never a crypto break
A sealed A/V chunk rides the RNS Link whole under the outer seal inside the E1 transit seal; it is never fragmented into symbols
The sender checks a chunk against the link's channel MDU and refuses an oversize chunk as ChunkTooLarge, never splitting; no symbol envelope, XChaCha20-Poly1305 or K_symbol on this path
The epoch DEK proves membership not authorship; every chunk format carries a StreamKeyBinding and a trailer, and a chunk lacking either is refused

StreamKeyBinding encoding is fixed big-endian: version 0x01, room, publisher (u16-length UTF-8), join_nonce 32, stream_id 32, epoch u64, chunk_key 32, sig_ed25519 len 64, sig_ml_dsa_65 len 3309; at most 8192 bytes
A call stream_id MUST equal SHA-256 of ciris-edge:call-stream:v2 || room || publisher || join_nonce with no length prefixes

The binding's signing bytes are ciris-edge:av-stream-key:v1 || body; Ed25519 over them, ML-DSA-65 over them plus the Ed25519 signature, by the publisher's federation key; ML-DSA checked by verification never byte equality
A receiver accepts a binding in order: parse; known bindings not re-verified; room equals the call's; stream id re-derives; publisher in the MLS group; hybrid signature verifies; then install
A receiver keeps a stream's two newest binding epochs and a publisher's four newest streams; a binding older than both held epochs is refused; refusals are not cached
A binding travels in parts CSKB || 0x01 || id || index || count || payload, at most 64 parts, four reassembling per link; no stream id begins CSKB 0x01
A binding part takes no outer seal and no hop sequence; the link's E1 seal covers it like every frame
A binding is sent on every new leg after the transit KEX and hello before fan-out, at every epoch roll in fixed order under one lock, and every ten seconds
On a new leg a member relay also sends every binding it holds except the dialled member's own, once
Bindings travel only on member-to-member legs: a node dials only MLS members at derived call addresses, removes a departed member's leg at the roll, closes non-member inbound links unread
A member relay forwards a verified binding to every other leg only when the binding's publisher is the peer it heard it from, so re-sends cannot loop
A non-member forwarder never receives, verifies or forwards a binding; it carries sealed frames opaque
The trailer is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key after the inner ciphertext inside the outer seal, over ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v1 || header fields || inner_aead
note: ambiguity: v1 form stated; shipping v2 form with source_ms pinned from gated submission

gist: A member relay verifies without the DEK: parse, open the outer seal, look up the bound key, strictly verify the trailer, forward re-sealing only the outer layer
A relay forwards a chunk only when the link's hello named the stream and the verified publisher is the link's peer
A receiver verifies as a relay does then opens the inner seal with the DEK; the frame's publisher is the binding's never the hello's; no store read, no hybrid verification
A frame's plaintext budget is the link channel limit less 148 bytes (252 at MTU 500, 1148 at MTU 1400); an over-budget frame is refused before sealing

Refusal tokens are one closed vocabulary identical at relay and receiver, each counted under its own name and an aggregate (av_binding_*, av_chunk_unbound, av_chunk_trailer_missing, av_chunk_trailer_invalid)
The binding and trailer known-answer vectors (publisher node-kat-a, room room-kat, epoch 5) are normative and carried by CIRISVerify
The chunk key is classical and ephemeral per stream and epoch; the long-lived binding that names it is hybrid-signed; the residual is bounded to one member, one stream, one epoch
ChunkLayer is three u8 axes (spatial, temporal, quality), each monotonic with 0 the always-required base; a receiver reconstructs from the prefix of cells; {0,0,0} is the blinking-dot minimum
For codec_id 0xFF the ChunkLayer MUST be {0,0,0}

ReceiverLayerPolicy (max_spatial, max_temporal, max_quality) is advertised over the existing federation_session / key_grant entitlement surface, not a new wire; the sender drops chunks above the cap without re-encoding
admits(layer) is the per-axis test spatial, temporal and quality each at most the policy cap; a codec_id 0xFF chunk MUST be admitted unconditionally before consulting admits
Canonical policies are BLINKING_DOT {0,0,0} and UNCAPPED {255,255,255}; the inner seal runs once per chunk and the outer seal only for admitted (receiver, chunk) pairs

double_sealed_ciphertext is outer-AEAD(inner-AEAD(plaintext)), two AES-256-GCM layers (12-byte nonce, 16-byte tag); inner is end-to-end epoch-DEK, outer is per-link transit; a relay sees only the outer; both nonces deterministic, never transmitted
The inner seal is the 5.3.3.1 chunk seal with counter = chunk_seq (below 2^32 per epoch) and last_flag on the final chunk; no second inner nonce
outer_nonce = SHA-256(CIRIS-AV-OUTER-V1 || link_id || link_seq_be8)[0..12]; the label is a pinned domain separator; link_seq is u64 big-endian monotonic per RNS Link
Neither nonce input rides the frame: last_flag comes from the epoch terminator and link_seq is a per-(link, stream) counter both ends keep, starting at 0 and advancing one per frame
The sender advances link_seq once per frame sealed; the receiver advances only on a frame that authenticates and never opens a counter below next, so a replay never opens
After loss the receiver reports its dropped count on its next frame; the sender tries next plus dropped, next, then a bounded slack (eight counters); beyond it the hop ends
Outer-nonce and to_bytes conformance is proven by the vector set published with CIRISVerify; the inner seal's vectors are 5.3.3.1's; codec_id and ChunkLayer stay outside both AEADs
A call is live by default and nothing of it is held past forwarding
Each stream is kept by its own publisher and by nobody else; durability is the owner's per item
A room's policy row MAY forbid keeping streams in that room, never require it
Every participant is told at joining whether streams in the room may be kept, before they publish
A screen share is its publisher's stream and is kept the same way; a room that forbids keeping forbids it for a share as for a camera
A later joiner reads a kept stream only from the epochs whose keys they hold, nothing earlier; a publisher who wants a newcomer to see more re-shares by own act
A publisher changes keep mid-stream only at an epoch boundary and the change reaches forward only
A live stream is its own transparency log; its signed roots commit the producer to a single chunk history
log_id is the string stream:<stream_id>; chunks are leaves; the stream-root is a SignedTreeHead with that log_id, tree_size = chunk_count, root_hash, timestamp, signature
A live stream produces signed roots at the cadence whether or not anyone records it
The producer MUST sign the stream STH; signing bytes with no domain label, little-endian: u32 len(log_id) || log_id || u64 tree_size || root_hash[32] || i64 timestamp seconds || u32 nanoseconds
root_hash is the RFC 6962 Merkle root over the first tree_size chunk SHA-256 leaves in seq order, leaves under 0x00 and inner nodes under 0x01
An inline file is a stream of one leaf: stream_id is the inline blob's stream id and tree_size is 1
The stream STH signature is hybrid: Ed25519 over the signing bytes then ML-DSA-65 over signing_bytes || ed25519_sig; the 5.3.1 cosign digest is the witness input only

Witness cosign of a stream root is optional: best-effort open media uses the producer-signed root only; accountable streams (paid, registry propagation, emergency) take witness cosign with consistency proof
The producer publishes a signed root every K chunks or T seconds, always at an epoch boundary and at sealed_at; witness cosign runs per epoch; defaults K=64, T=2s, operator-tunable
A subscriber verifies chunk K's inclusion against the nearest signed STH at or past K via the consistency path; no new commitment structure
The accountable-stream witness quorum is Policy E locality-scaled, not a fixed N
The durable record of who is entitled and the ephemeral fact of who is reachable are never conflated
The entitlement roster is Persist-owned evidence: a signed envelope, Edge-propagated, durable, logged; it MUST propagate and be auditable
The live-reachability set is Edge-owned and node-local; it is never an attestation, never a holding claim, never replicated, never logged
fan_out(C) = entitled(C) intersect reachable(now)
A member MAY take each layer of a stream from a different parent of the member relay tree, pulling an undelivered chunk from a sibling before asking the parent again
Every codec_id class defines a presence-floor layer (a colour tile blinking once a second at a few tens of bytes a second)
A receiver in a call of N senders subscribes each at the highest layer fitting budget/N; a relay forwards only layers asked; a call never excludes a sender for bandwidth
Entitled-but-unreachable members fall back to pull on reconnect; the substrate does not keep retrying push, does not emit a delivery_failed attestation, does not log liveness state
Reconnect-then-pull catch-up rides history_on_join; under the one chunk seal pulled chunks open with the same nonce as pushed ones
E2: broadcast and large-group delivery is pull-only (producer seals, emits holding claims at the stream's scope, subscribers pull via ContentFetch); no relay tree; small groups push on direct links
E1: the transit key is a hop-by-hop wrap under the end-to-end epoch DEK, two independent layers
E3: Persist owns durable entitlement, Edge owns reachability via a node-local tracker, fan-out is the intersection; reachability is never an attestation, holding claim, replicated or logged
E4: durable entitlement (roster and epoch-key grants) rides the existing federation-attestation Edge path; net-new transport is only the streaming-log endpoints
The per-link seal is a KEM-authenticated handshake (X-Wing): nobody signs to open a link; a relaying node's static is the transit pair its signed binding publishes, rotated by superseding it
note: planned v62; normative when the edition lands

gist: Handshake is two messages in one flight: initiator sends ephemeral key, encapsulation to the responder's static and sealed identity; responder answers with encapsulations and key confirmation

Known initiator: both statics used, both ends authenticated by the handshake; unknown initiator: encapsulation to the initiator's static omitted, authenticated only by the first-contact plane, promoted later
A node that publishes no transit pair (a client-only phone) is always an unknown initiator
The handshake runs before shaping begins and charges no shaped-link budget; the E1 relay rule binding a non-member's static against the initiator's ephemeral stands
Responder decapsulation runs outside any node-wide lock and behind the per-link, per-sender and node-wide receiver rates
The transit key is a hop-by-hop wrap under the end-to-end epoch DEK and MUST NOT replace the cascade; a relay never sees plaintext; relay means frame-forwarding, never media fan-out
The RNS link layer is classical and is not relied on for post-quantum confidentiality
Every byte an edge sends over an RNS link MUST be under a hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 transit seal bound to the link_id and a transit pair authenticated to the dialled identity
Every content key is wrapped X25519 + ML-KEM-768 and every federation record is signed Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65
The transit seal is the 3.3.6.2 transit KEX, run once per link as its first frame and covering every later frame (replication, membership, pairing, device-join, chat headers, A/V outer seal)
On the pairing plane the initiator has no owner yet; the seal still binds its self-signed node key, never an anonymous one
A dialler holding no pair sends as its first frame a route request naming the dialled key; the responder answers with only its own hybrid-signed transport_destination row and key record
A record received over a route request authenticates nothing by itself; the dialler binds it to a prior anchor (code commitment, key-plane record, Rooted binding) and fails closed holding none
The dialler checks signer and subject of each received row equal the dialled key, admits the key record through the key door and the route row, then handshakes
The responder answers a route request at most once per link and rate-limits route requests node-wide before parsing past their tag
The public self-authenticating route row is the only thing besides the handshake that crosses a link unsealed
The three receiver rates (per-link, per-sender, node-wide) run as a set, each charging only its own budget, so a frame refused by one spends no node-wide budget
The responder serves nothing until the seal completes; keying-link frames sit in a bounded hold refusing on overflow, never trimming; a link whose first frame is anything else is dropped
With no reachable responder the pairing pin is the failover, the only path for two nodes that cannot exchange a public frame
No classical-only fallback for any content and no advisory phase; a node not running the seal cannot talk to the mesh; no public classical lane; unsealed LXMF clients not served
The in-transit KEX identifier names a different construction from the at-rest wrap_algorithm; the two MUST NOT be compared, substituted, or accepted in each other's field
A non-member relay is bound by the transit KEX pair on its signed transport_destination binding, static against the initiator's ephemeral; never a KeyPackage key or ephemeral-only; no pair, no relay
A delivery_receipt:{stream_id} Contribution is a subscriber's signed acknowledgement of receiving chunk K under the named stream and epoch; best-effort by default, opt-in for accountable profiles
A receipt has two encodings at two layers: JCS bytes covered by the scores row's envelope signature, and the length-prefixed receipt payload the subscriber signs inside that row
receipt_signing_bytes = ciris-delivery-receipt/v1 (25 ASCII bytes) || u32_le len + subscriber_key_id || u32_le len + stream_id || epoch u64 LE || chunk_root 32 || K u64 LE
The receipt and the stream-root signing bytes are the only two little-endian layouts in this Part; every other integer is big-endian; a producer MUST NOT carry either byte order elsewhere
The receipt's signed order is as written (subscriber_key_id before stream_id); each length-prefixed field MUST fit a u32 and a longer field is refused, never clamped
received_at is the receiving node's local note and no part of the receipt preimage
Both epoch and K with chunk_root are required in a receipt; each names a distinct authorization scope
A receipt's subscriber signature (hybrid, ML-DSA-65 over bytes || ed25519_sig) must be valid; necessary but not sufficient

A receipt's chunk_root MUST equal a SignedTreeHead.root_hash actually published for log_id stream:<stream_id> at tree_size at least K; a phantom root is rejected; for accountable streams published means witness-cosigned
For accountable streams an inclusion proof of chunk K into chunk_root is recommended, upgrading the receipt to provable commitment to chunk K
A delivery receipt proves delivery, not consumption; consumers MUST NOT overclaim it as proof the subscriber decrypted the bytes
Verify validates and emits the receipt as an attestation on delivery_receipt:{stream_id}; the delivered verdict is consumer policy, not Verify's
The accountable-stream receipt quorum is Policy E locality-scaled, the same shape as the STH quorum
A live_stream is its own per-stream log instance and MUST NOT append chunks into the federation provenance log
The streaming path reuses the 5.3.1 SignedTreeHead, ConsistencyProof, WitnessConsistencyProof and cosign abstractions per stream under the same RFC 6962 algorithm
No new attestation_type values: chunks ride content addressing, stream-roots ride SignedTreeHead, delivery receipts ride scores against the delivery_receipt:{stream_id} reserved prefix
The streaming surface changes no primitive, bundles no substrate implementation, keeps multicast fan-out pull-only, and leaves K, T, MAX_CHUNKS_PER_EPOCH and the accountable quorum operator-tunable
A consumer verifies the GenesisBundle quorum against its own records before promoting any field to a trust root.
Nothing a serving install signs on its own account is a trust root.
A registry publishing its own key as its own root is the weakest producer claim; the registry is a conferred slice of a canonical node, not a root.
GET /v1/trust-root/bundle and /v1/steward-key serve the same GenesisBundle body.
Trust-root authority lives inside the bundle member and nowhere else in the response.
The bundle is tamper-evident, not authentic: a self-consistent attacker bundle under the same identifiers verifies identically.
A consumer holds an out-of-band anchor (pinned bundle_fingerprint or pinned accord-holder key fingerprints) before accepting a bootstrap bundle.
A consumer compares the received bundle against its pinned anchor at attach time.
ciris-canonical and humanity-accord are names, not anchors; a consumer with no anchor promotes nothing in the response to a trust root.
With the anchor held, the consumer re-derives the bundle quorum from its own records (verify_bundle_quorum) before trusting it.
A trust root once verified is valid until revoked (T4).
Everything outside bundle (served fingerprint, charter root id, served_by) is unsigned convenience the consumer recomputes or ignores; the served bundle_fingerprint is never the anchor.
The trust-root bundle response carries no response_signature over the wrapper.
hardware_class, signature_mode and threshold_policy never appear on the outer bundle envelope; custody class rides each holder's signed key record.
served_by.accepts_this_root false is legitimate: a node may relay a root it has not accepted (T3).
A consumer pins community anchor ciris-canonical and accord family humanity-accord, resolves the live member set via resolve_community, and never hard-pins a serving install's fingerprint.
A root is valid until revoked, never until a timer lapses; freshness gates attaching only (T4a).
The genesis head of each lineage and the charter carrying attach_window_secs, witness_cadence_secs, witness_quorum, witnesses[] are members of bundle.attestations, pinned by bundle_fingerprint.

The route serves a lineage_head member outside bundle: every head version, charter bytes and cosignatures since genesis; the same chain at GET /v1/trust-root/lineage-head with ?since=digest, objects fetchable by digest.

A consumer walks prev_head_digest from the genesis head, checking each head's quorum against its parent's fold and cosignatures against its parent's directory, never the head's own charter_digest; independent witnesses only.

Fewer than witness_quorum counted cosignatures is trust_root_head_unwitnessed; newest counted cosignature older than attach_window_secs is trust_root_head_stale; the consumer fetches a fresher head or refuses, never attaching on the stale one.
A consumer obtains at least one counted cosignature from the witness directly.
With witnessed mode off (witness_quorum 0, no directory) a root attaches by the pinned bundle_fingerprint with attach_window_secs 604800.
The accord's charter carries halt_fuse_secs 86400 (24 hours).
Witnessed mode is turned on by an amendment signed by a strict majority of the standing accord roster.

Witnessed-mode defaults for ciris-canonical and humanity-accord: attach_window_secs 604800, witness_cadence_secs 86400, exactly three independent witnesses, witness_quorum 2 (floor(n/2)+1); all four are charter members changed only by re-scrub.
Once attached, T4 governs: the served head's age is a liveness signal, never an expiry.
A node dials only a peer whose transit pair it holds authenticated to the identity meant: its hybrid-signed transport_destination row, a Rooted binding, or a pairing pin.
A canonical node is one source of route rows, never a required party; two peers holding each other's signed route rows seal, exchange allegiance facts and root each other directly.

The bundle member serve_transport_destinations carries the seated serve nodes' signed transport_destination rows with transit pairs, inside the authorization_digest preimage so the holders' quorum authorizes the exact set.
At bundle verification each serve_transport_destinations row is signed by a serve node listed in serve_nodes and carries a pair passing in-row separation; any failure fails the bundle closed.
At first open the bundle's route rows are seeded through ordinary transport-destination admission and land Rooted, so a fresh node dials a canonical first under the seal.
A fresh genesis is the final-genesis ceremony: every holder signs the charter, the genesis records and the authorization; unanimity; any change to charter or roster takes it.

An amend carries the pinned bundle's charter, grants, lifecycle, serve-node records, genesis records and produced_at forward byte for byte, adds serve_transport_destinations, signs only the new authorization_digest.
An amend finishes at M distinct holder authorizations (charter quorum 2/3); verification requires max(M, strict majority of roster); it refuses if any carried byte differs from the pinned input.
The rows the bundle carries are signed transport_destination rows, each the serve node's own signed self-emission.

The first transit-pair seed is emitted offline: a seated canonical's operator emits the node's hybrid-signed row from custody with no network; the pair derives deterministically from the custody seed.
Bundle verification checks each route row's signature and signer's seat, never its age (valid until revoked).
A seated node's live transport_destination row supersedes the bundle-seeded one on the first sealed link, same pair, later asserted_at.
Overlap rule: a seated serve node keeps the pinned-bundle pair valid until a re-minted bundle with the new pair has propagated, or makes the rotation a re-mint; early retirement refused.
A canonical's pair rotation is a holders' quorum act via the accord-signed address update, landing Rooted and superseding the seeded pair; a re-mint changes only what a fresh node seeds.
Before the first sealed link a transit pair reaches a node only from the bundle, the owner's pairing payload (pinned for that link alone), or the pre-seal route fetch.
A trust decides what a node serves, never whether two keys may speak privately (T8).
On a sealed link to a non-Rooted peer there still cross: bootstrap kinds, allegiance facts, the pairing plane, rows addressed to the peer, and cohort rows delivered to it.
What waits for Rooted is what the node serves to a third party: a federation-tier row and any self-authored row about someone other than the peer.

GET /v1/accord-holders returns three named holders with hybrid pubkeys, per-holder hardware_class and provisioned flag; an unprovisioned holder carries a placeholder fingerprint and provisioned false.
note: hardware_class per holder here; 574 bars it on the bundle outer envelope only

gist: Consumers never honor constitutional invocations against placeholder (unprovisioned) holders.
/v1/accord-holders is a projection of bundle.holders; a consumer cross-checks it against the bundle rather than trusting the projection.
/v1/accord/holders carries no response signature and no authority; a consumer cross-checks every shown holder against bundle.holders under its anchor; accord_emissions[] are verified individually.
GET /v1/rotation-history returns chronological rotation events of the Registry's signing keys.

GET /v1/builds/{version} returns BuildRecordResponse with federation_provenance; /v1/verify/build-manifest/... returns the verbatim signed BuildManifest; /v1/agent_files/{kind} returns trust-composition layers; /v1/partner/{key_id} composes ProfileScorecard.
All CEG endpoints return application/json; Accept honored; other types answer 406 Not Acceptable.
Every CEG response carries CEG-Version: <spec major.minor>.
Clients echo CEG-Accept-Version naming the version they were built against.
MAJOR version mismatch is a wire-incompatible reject; MINOR mismatch is compatible and clients MAY warn.
Every CEG response carries X-CEG-Server-Time in rfc3339_canonical for client clock-skew bounds.
Paginated endpoints take ?cursor= and ?limit= and return next_cursor (null when exhausted) and total_estimate.
All error responses conform to the error envelope: code, http_status, message, request_id, details.
400 MALFORMED_REQUEST: invalid JSON, missing required field, bad field type.
400 CANONICAL_BYTES_VIOLATION: date-time, hex or encoding does not match the canonical byte rules.
401 UNAUTHENTICATED: bearer token missing or invalid.
403 RESERVED_PREFIX_VIOLATION: producer emitted under a reserved prefix without authority.
404 UNKNOWN_WITNESS: witness key_id not registered in the directory.
404 NOT_FOUND: generic resource not found (build, partner, key).
409 IDEMPOTENT_CONFLICT: replay detected, e.g. duplicate (tree_size, witness_key_id) cosignature with different signatures.
422 SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILED: Ed25519 or ML-DSA-65 failed; details.algorithm names which.
422 CLOCK_SKEW_VIOLATION: signed_at exceeds the ±5 minute tolerance.
422 WITNESS_QUORUM_NOT_MET: insufficient cosignatures to validate.

422 CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID: a witness cosignature's consistency proof against its prior cosigned STH is absent or fails; missing proof with a prior STH, or tree_size behind it, is MALFORMED_REQUEST.

422 LINEAGE_HEAD_INCONSISTENT: cosignature names an unrecorded prior head or one not descending by prev_head_digest; a quorum-signed head not descending from the witnessed head is instead recorded uncosigned as hard_case:lineage_fork_attempt.

413 ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE: canonical JCS bytes exceed 1 MiB; raised at every write path (HTTP, capsule, FFI, tier-ingest) as an admission bound; storage spelling federation_envelope_too_large maps to this wire code.
429 RATE_LIMITED: X-RateLimit-* headers set; Retry-After honored.
500 INTERNAL_ERROR: server-side fault; request_id usable for support.
503 WITNESS_DIRECTORY_UNAVAILABLE: substrate replication lag exceeds liveness bound.

Admission refusal tokens (attestation_type_unregistered, federation_malformed_row, federation_set_semantics_unsorted, asserted_at_stale, trust_root_head_unwitnessed, trust_root_head_stale, census tokens) are refusal reasons in the row's refusal, not HTTP statuses.
Every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset.
The scope-privacy primitives are additive to the wire layer; the 1+4 surface is unchanged.

record_id is a deterministic group-keyed HMAC commitment: every MLS group member derives the identical 32-byte tag, non-members see an unlinkable tag; it is a pure function, never a queryable authority.
record_id_input (CBOR dCE four-entry map), the K_record_id derivation and the resulting HMAC tag are byte-identical across producer, substrate and every consumer.
K_record_id derives in two stages: MLS exporter under the record label, then bare HKDF-Expand; K_symbol is the second stage of the same chain under its own label.
S_record = MLS-Exporter(ciris-scope-record-v1, context empty, 32); K_record_id and K_symbol = HKDF-SHA256-Expand(S_record, info ciris-edge/scope-privacy/record-id/v1 or symbol/v1, 32).
Implementations derive S_record by the exporter call under ciris-scope-record-v1, and K_record_id and K_symbol by bare HKDF-SHA256-Expand over S_record.
The second-stage labels are never routed through RFC 9420 MLS_Exporter(); the raw exporter_secret is never used directly.
S_dest is a separate exporter under its own label.
record_id_input = CBOR_dCE({v:1, epc:mls_group_epoch, iid:internal_id, typ:record_type}); record_id = HMAC-SHA3-256(K_record_id, record_id_input).
CBOR_dCE is RFC 8949 4.2.1 Core Deterministic Encoding, map keys ordered by encoded length then lexicographically; the v=1 map serializes keys v, epc, iid, typ.
Map keys are CBOR text strings; v, epc, typ values are unsigned integers; iid is a CBOR byte string (major type 2), never text.
RecordType integers: reserved 0, SelfRecord 1, FamilyRecord 2, CommunityRecord 3, FederationRecord 4.
Additional record types extend the RecordType table only by amendment.
With K_record_id = 0x11 x32, conforming implementations reproduce the three published record_id preimage and tag vectors exactly.
The deterministic CBOR profile is normative; vectors are published with CIRISVerify.
In the InvisibleEncrypted and CommunityDek tiers stored content moves and rests as encrypted chunks, replicated per item to holders and never split by any node.
On the scope-privacy plane each chunk crosses a shaped link as symbols, real and cover alike, each symbol sealed under its own AEAD key.
The realtime A/V plane emits no symbol: a sealed A/V chunk rides its link whole under the E1 seal.
Self/family and community/affiliations content emit holding claims only within the cohort; outsiders cannot discover the bytes exist.
The substrate seals every symbol it emits with the symbol AEAD framing.
A holder lacking both K_symbol and record_id is unable to distinguish a real symbol envelope from a cover symbol envelope.
record_id = HMAC-SHA3-256(K_record_id, CBOR_dCE({v,epc,iid,typ})); K_symbol and K_record_id are per-scope subkeys of one derivation chain; both rebind on MLS Add/Remove.
symbol_key = HKDF-SHA3-256(salt=record_id, ikm=K_symbol, info=label||u16_be(symbol_index), 32); symbol_envelope = (record_id, u16_be(symbol_index), nonce, XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext, tag).
Producer, substrate and every consumer recompute symbol_key byte-identically: salt record_id, ikm K_symbol, info exact ASCII label followed by u16_be(symbol_index), len 32.
The symbol AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 with 24-byte nonce and Poly1305 tag; the same suite seals real and cover fragments; no separate cover cipher, cleartext cover marker or length distinguisher.
The fragment set rebinds on MLS Add/Remove: a removed member's symbol keys do not open post-epoch fragments; honest holders delete past-epoch keys per the community's archive policy.
symbol_envelope field order is fixed (record_id, u16_be(symbol_index), nonce, ciphertext, tag); cleartext record_id and symbol_index are addressing only, not authority-bearing.
The symbol AEAD composes with and never substitutes for the at-rest DEK cascade: symbols are protected in transit and at relays, the DEK cascade at rest.
Every fragment on the wire, real or cover, is the same size and the same AEAD shape.
On a shaped link every frame is one constant size: 1,400 bytes before the E1 seal including header, or the channel MDU where smaller; larger payloads fragmented, smaller padded.
The shaped frame size is not a per-link tuning knob and not a class or negotiated value; it is one constant for the fleet.
An unshaped link carries no padding requirement; there is no fixed envelope size for all outbound traffic.
Shaping is negotiated per link immediately after the E1 handshake under its keys, never set per node.
Each end offers a budget class (server, home, phone-wifi, phone-cellular, off); the link runs at the lower of the two offers.
note: seat class of 776/780 absent from this offer list

gist: On a shaped link both directions are shaped at the negotiated rate; a responder shapes its replies; a node that cannot meet an offer declines the link, never half-shaped.
Every frame on a shaped link is a constant-size sealed frame, cover indistinguishable from real under the seal; frames leave on a per-link Poisson timer at the negotiated rate.
Real traffic is at most fraction rho of the stream over window W: at most target_rate = ceil(rho*lambda*W) real frames per window, counted locally at each end.
rho and W are explicit per-node settings with fleet defaults.
Maintenance traffic (anti-entropy, replication, witness, repair) and ordinary rows are shaped; the real-time audio and video plane is never shaped.
Shaping runs only inside established links and hides timing and volume within a shaped link, never which links exist; link setup stays observable.
A link opened for one exchange is shaped like a standing one for its life.
A node opens short-lived links on a schedule that does not depend on whether it has something real to send.
The shaping claim is stated against an observer of the link; an adversary that drops or delays frames is outside it.
Shaping is on by default for the server class and off by default for every other class; a node that activates the Anonymous Tier shapes its layer links regardless.
A client offering shaping states at the choice what it hides and does not, the latency added (frame size over class budget) and the cover bytes; no silent default.
A node that turns shaping on offers its budget class with the fleet-default rho, W and byte budget of the table.
server class: rho 0.5, W 600 s, 7,000 B/s per link.
home class: rho 0.5, W 600 s, 2,800 B/s per link.
phone-wifi class: rho 0.5, W 600 s, 1,400 B/s per link.
phone-cellular class: rho 0.5, W 3,600 s, 350 B/s per link.
seat class: rho 0.5, W 600 s, 33,000 B/s per link.
A shaped link is one direct hop, never forwarded through a third node; a peer with no direct path gets no shaped link, only a forwarder, sealed and unshaped.
Shaped links form among offering nodes (servers by default, homes and phones whose owners turned shaping on) and with any node that asks, i.e. a shaped-only node.
Shaped links carry identity and consent rows, the public set, cover, Anonymous Tier packets and proxy traffic; offering nodes homed on a canonical are its shaped peers and proxies.
Chat and files ride a shaped link only when one end is shaped-only; any other pair's chat and bulk cross one direct unshaped link even beside a shaped one.
A large file (more than 64 KiB whole) never crosses a shaped link, whole or in chunks.
A shaped-only node refuses to fetch a large file by name with the served string 'This file is too large to access over shaped links'; other nodes fetch it unshaped.
A/V and bulk are unshaped only; a failed bulk dial never falls back onto shaped frames: the sender refuses by name, retries on schedule or uses a consenting carrier.
A node's shaping setting says whether it offers shaping, never whether it accepts; a node with shaping off still gives a shaped link to any asker at its own class.
A node with shaping off drops an asked-for shaped link ten minutes after the last real frame, cover not counting (operator-settable); the asking peer dials again on demand.
Beyond eight shaped peers a new peer's link is not covered: its size and timing are visible, and that the node talks to more than eight peers is visible.
Relays of the Anonymous Tier forward packets across several shaped links, each one direct hop.
A node runs at most eight shaped links, each at its class's full rate; a further shaping peer is admitted by displacement or refused, never run below its class.
Displacement: when a higher-class peer needs the slot, the node moves its lowest-class shaped peer to a shaping home or server below it with a slot; it keeps shaping.
A peer no higher than the lowest held takes no shaped slot: a shaped-only or Anonymous Tier node refuses it a row link; any other node runs the link unshaped.
A refusal is never bare: it carries routes of up to three announced nodes offering relay with a free shaped slot; a referral is a hint, next tried on refusal.
Every refusal may refer: a throttled pull, shed serve or seat under load answers with up to three referrals; a canonical sheds load to its shaped peers as proxies.
A referral names a node with its free-slot report and its own count of unsolicited inbound dials, a self-reported live report never an attestation, so a referral stays a hint.
A referrer may prefer nodes with a record of serving peers sent to them; what it saw itself is no row; a shared record is a capacity: measurement by those peers.
A node is scored only with its consent and never by itself; the referral carries no score; a record orders the nodes named and excludes none.
Two axes: the class sets a shaped link's rate; the carriage (full or consent-only) sets what may ride it; any class may run either carriage.
A node offers the budget class of its hardware class and interface (server, home, phone Wi-Fi, phone cellular), the same for every node of that kind.
A relay's layer links in the Anonymous Tier count within the eight shaped links.
The seat class is offered only where both ends hold a serve seat in an infrastructure community, proved from the signed roster; its budget sits outside the eight.
A shaped link carries rows (statements, posts, messages, reactions, small images, control traffic); bulk and live media ride their own unshaped links; a link belongs to one plane.
A peer in anonymous mode is confined to the row plane: rows only, no stream and no call; the client says so when the mode is chosen.
Every envelope, real publication and synthetic cover alike, uses uniform XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD framing.
A synthetic cover envelope is marked type=cover by the first byte of its sealed body; the type discriminator lives inside the AEAD envelope, never in cleartext.
The XChaCha20-Poly1305 symbol framing, the AES-256-GCM streaming chunk seal and the HPKE-layer AES-256-GCM of the Welcome wrap are different layers and are never conflated.
A fragment is a symbol: one frame-sized piece of a real publication or one cover frame; stored content is never split; a sealed chunk travels whole, fragmented to frame size.
Each symbol is sealed independently under the 5.4.2 symbol_key derivation and envelope layout; the per-symbol KDF is HKDF-SHA3-256 for hash-family separation from the SHA-256 key schedule.
On any MLS Add or Remove the fragment set rebinds under the new epoch; a removed member cannot derive post-removal fragments; a new member gets no retroactive access beyond archive_mode.
A receiver opens each symbol_envelope under its recomputed symbol_key; a failed tag discards that symbol, never accepting partial plaintext; a record whose symbol set is not whole is dropped whole.
A reassembled chunk is handled as stored content: the consumer pulls the item's sealed chunks from any holder, decrypts with the cohort key it holds, and verifies the full digest.
When no holder is reachable the fetch resolves to ContentMiss, an honest miss, never a silent gap or a downgrade to unverified bytes.
MLS Welcome messages are wrapped by HPKE mode_base to the invitee's static X-Wing (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) public key.

Sender authentication is never claimed at the HPKE layer (X-Wing has no AuthEncap); it comes from the inviter's hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 signature over the encapsulation bytes; single-primitive signatures not admitted.
HPKE parameters: HPKE_SUITE_ID b'HPKE-xwing-hkdf-sha256-aes256gcm-v1', KDF HKDF-SHA256, AEAD AES-256-GCM.
HPKE_SUITE_ID is used byte-for-byte identically on both sides in every LabeledExtract/LabeledExpand call; it is a domain-separation literal whose hyphens are never snake_cased.
The HPKE-layer AEAD is AES-256-GCM, distinct from the XChaCha20-Poly1305 symbol framing; the live A/V chunk is AES-256-GCM at every layer.

The inviter signs encap_signing_bytes in bound hybrid form: Ed25519 over the encoding, then ML-DSA-65 over encoding||ed25519_sig, no algorithm field; the verifier checks both halves, refusing a Welcome with one.
encap_signing_bytes = x25519_ephemeral_pub (32) || u32_be(len(mlkem768_ct)) || mlkem768_ciphertext.
Inviter signature verification is a precondition to unwrapping a Welcome; omitting it forfeits sender authentication and the forwarder-side membership-opacity guarantee.
What a witness chain may commit to is scoped by tier; no chain carries a count of activity; the amount a node carries is hidden by link shaping only.
The privacy witness chain, the wholeness witness and the transparency-log witness are distinct constructions, never cross-verified and never substituted for one another.
A federation witness chain commits only to federation-scope record_ids: no per-community record_id, no count of non-federation activity, no rate counter.
Where a chain pads, a cover leaf commits to HMAC-SHA3-256(witness_signing_key, leaf_position || epoch_id), indistinguishable from a real Merkle root.

A per-community witness chain commits to the community's record_id set with member-only visibility and is signed inside the community's MLS encryption; it never federates beyond the group's encryption.
No tier's witness chain carries a rate counter.
Structural invisibility keeps self/family content off the discovery surface; the witness-content discipline keeps the witness surface from re-leaking it at federation scope.
Group-scoped destinations are resolved from a cached directory plus per-group HKDF, never from an announce.
A destination whose cohort_scope is below federation (self, family, community, affiliations) never emits a Reticulum announce, directed or broadcast; the substrate suppresses it.
Only federation/Commons-scope destinations (species, biosphere, federation, infrastructure opt-out) may announce normally; they carry no anonymity claim.

A node announces when its owner-binding is carried at cohort_scope federation, owner-signed at that audience; a person's public roster is exactly the set of their nodes with federation-scoped owner-bindings.
A fedID with no announced node is reached only by a node code handed by the owner (contact code or QR); no forwarder serves its route, no stranger finds it.
An unannounced node's owner-signed occurrence and owner binding ride sealed inside the contact request and acceptance, held by the owner's nodes and the contact alone, served by no forwarder.
An unannounced identity cannot join a public group: a public room admits by the joiner's own signature at the Commons tier; an unverifiable key is withheld, not refused.
A client states the two costs (contact only by handed code; no public group) when announcing is declined.
Un-announcing is the owner superseding the binding at cohort_scope self and withdrawing the grants that carried it; what others hold they keep; the node becomes unfindable, never unknown.
The Reticulum announce of a node's transport destination, emitted by every routing node, places nothing on the device roster.
note: 870 says every node announces its identity destination; 884 says an anonymous node announces nothing

gist: A node holding a serve seat in an infrastructure community has an announced owner: a live owner-binding at cohort_scope federation exists while it holds the seat, requestable any time.
The seat-owner test is evaluated live, never at a past instant: a binding made after seating satisfies it; a withdrawn binding stops satisfying it.
While no federation-scope owner-binding exists a seated node does not serve under the seat, refused serve_seat_owner_unannounced; the check is persist's and the server gates on it.
A node that boots seated and owned but unannounced announces itself if its owner's key is present and otherwise raises an alarm.
A node whose owner-binding is held only at self is reachable by the owner's nodes and v3-code holders, never listed; no directory, serve policy or read route enumerates it.
A roster is never enumerable outside its cohort; re-signing the binding at federation scope is the opt-in.
A node whose owner resolves to the minor band never carries a federation-scope owner-binding; admission refuses the promotion; the minor is reachable only on the derived plane; nothing lifts this.

A node offers an identity:occurrence:v1 row to a peer only when it would also relay the attester's federation-announced owner-binding; an unverifiable attester's row is withheld, not served to be refused.
An agent attester's key carries a live steward binding and is relayable exactly when its owner-binding is announced, by the per-node rule, like any device of a person.
Every participating L1 peer maintains a complete local copy of the federation directory's X-Wing public keys, refreshed via federation_keys anti-entropy; the directory stays federation-public.
A group destination is resolved deterministically from cached directory entry plus per-group HKDF; every member derives the same; outsiders cannot.
No per-invitation or per-resolution directory query is emitted.
Phone-class peers that cannot hold the full directory resolve through their L1-relay parent over a relay-blinded path.

Destination derivation: S_dest = MLS-Exporter(ciris-scope-destination-v1); k_destination = HKDF-SHA256-Expand(S_dest, destination/v1 label, 32); destination = HKDF-SHA3-256(k_destination, salt empty, label||u32_be(len(member_key_id))||member_key_id, 16).
The expand step is bare HKDF-SHA256-Expand, not RFC 9420 ExpandWithLabel; S_dest is a separate exporter from S_record; storage holds the record secret, only transport holds the destination secret.
A destination is derived once per (group, epoch) at a membership or epoch change, never per packet; it rotates by install-next, activate, seal, never silencing a group.
Announce suppression hides a group's content, membership and address-to-group mapping; it does not hide that a node opens links to derived destinations or the shape of that traffic.
note: 'Every node announces its identity destination' vs 845/884 unannounced and anonymous nodes

gist: The anonymity target is outsiders holding no cohort envelope, including a subpoena against the directory; in-group members see the group fully; the on-path forwarder claim is 1.13.3.1's.
A peer with a stale or incomplete directory cache resolves fewer destinations and reports an honest miss; it never falls back to a group-scoped announce or a per-destination query.
Absence of per-destination announce control fails toward suppression, never toward announce.
A directed (targeted) announce inherits the group-scope prohibition; the object is the emission class, not the broadcast; the targeted per-destination query is banned likewise.
A reading never spends a claimable guarantee (no emission exists) to purchase an unclaimable one (traffic-analysis privacy).
In-group distribution of addressing material over MLS is not an announce and is not prohibited.

Multi-hop reach for a group-scoped destination is an amendment-plane question with the bar: no outsider-observable emission, no outsider-retained path state, no epoch-correlated wave; never a reading of this clause.

Where no direct path exists a scoped body may ride the members' identity-plane link through a forwarder: end-to-end encrypted, room discriminated inside the link, admitted against the derived-address table.
A forwarder's sanctioned role is reachability, never custody of the conversation: it carries link ciphertext only and retains nothing beyond the transport table kept for every forwarded link.
Where endpoints can bring the link direct (shared interface or direct dial on an address the path exchange revealed) the link is brought direct and the forwarder drops out.
A forwarder is never handed anything that names the room.
A node stands to a frame as an end, as a carrier that said yes (contact offering relay, serve seat, non-opted-out Anonymous Tier relay), or as a stranger.

A stranger carries on a shaped link only what needs no consent: link setup and cover; public self-authenticating rows (key records, revocations, occurrences, allegiance, unowned routes); sealed consent asks; halt; tombstones
A row of the stranger-carried set carries no context member and is of bounded size, so a carrier checks what it carries without opening it.
A scoped body (room body, live stream chunks included) crosses a forwarder only one that said yes, a consented contact or last-resort serve seat; a stranger is offered none.
An Anonymous Tier relay is a carrier that said yes, carrying a fixed-length packet it cannot read; it is a relay, not a forwarder; the forwarder rule misses it.
Carriage is a property of the link, not its class: any link may be set consent-only, including between two serve seats; the two ends or a consenting carrier choose it.
Nothing narrows what two ends send each other; every road to a consent (first contact, adding a device, joining a room, halt, key revocation) runs on strangers alone.
A consenting forwarder may carry a live stream's chunks between two members lacking a direct path; never a fan-out node of the relay tree, buffering only the frame, no binding.
A publisher's stream binding and each chunk's authentication are verified by members, the tree's relays and receivers, never by a forwarder.
The stream binding fixes the tree root: the named publisher is the only member at depth zero; an offer claiming depth zero from another key or before the binding drops.
A substrate prefers the derived address whenever a direct link exists and never routes a scoped body through a forwarder when a direct path is available.
Minors are unaffected by forwarding: reachability still requires the federation-scope announce a minor's node cannot carry.
A peer that wants to be reachable publishes its owner binding at federation scope; a stranger reaches it by its federation identity and the first message crosses a forwarder.
An owned node's signed route is handed by its owner and never served by a forwarder.
Offering relay is handing the node's route to strangers for first contact and consent, three at a time to peers a full node refuses; relay off reports no capacity.
Relay is offered by default on every owned node; turning it off is the owner's choice made with its cost on screen (the node carries nobody, refers nobody).
A referred peer is a proxy: it serves the asker from what it holds, pulling a missing federation-tier row from the seat as its own pull; non-federation rows never proxied.
A proxy is an offering node under its public identity, named in referrals with its route; an anonymous node proxies nothing and relays nothing; wanting both means two nodes.
A phone offers relay while charging on an unmetered network and reports no capacity otherwise; a node reporting no capacity is never referred and never counted as a parent.
A route rides inside the sealed first-contact request and sealed acceptance; a forwarder serves an owned node's route to nobody, holds no contact grant, never gets the consent readable.
A forwarder serves openly key records, identity occurrences and the routes of unowned nodes (itself, a bare server), which carry no person.

A responder serves a stranger the announced testimony (binding, key records, public kinds) of any subject whose live federation-scope owner binding it holds, regardless of publish set; no owned route.
A forwarder holds about a pair only that a link between two announced endpoints crossed it, or ciphertext waiting in a mailbox for a sleeping peer, bounded in retention.
A requester shows its route to the one it asks before consent, disclosing nothing the pre-seal route fetch does not already hand any dialler.
Consent is the acceptance itself: a route reaches a peer only from its owner and only a peer the owner addressed; no forwarder gate is needed or permitted.
A superseding route after contact is handed the same way the first was.
Whether a peer answers a contact request is the peer's; the first-contact receiver order (per-sender, per-link, node-wide rate) is the anti-spam; a refused request gets no answer.
First contact under a flood is not promised; a client that cannot reach a peer says so rather than retrying on a fixed beat (jittered, not fixed).
The asked person may ignore a contact request: a private, local, undoable act of their own node; the asker is never told and sees exactly what a pending request shows.
Either party may block the other: a private act of their own node; further requests from the blocked key are dropped unanswered, forwarder learning nothing; lifted only by its maker.
The Anonymous Tier hides who published a federation-scope item from storing nodes, the directory and, with shaping, a network observer; packet layout, KDF label and AEAD not yet pinned.
Anonymous mode is a property of a node, not of a publication: using the tier and being anonymous are one thing.
An anonymous node is a separate dedicated identity: fresh user key and node key, no self roster shared with and no row linking it to any announced identity.
A person may later prove an anonymous identity and an announced one are both theirs by a signed statement under both keys, and is never found out otherwise.
An anonymous node announces nothing, publishes everything at federation scope through the tier under publication keys, is reached only at its rendezvous, holds only shaped layer and rendezvous links.
An anonymous node may be any device class, a phone on Wi-Fi included, and sends end-to-end cover packets by default at the item-8 rate.
A node is anonymous from its first run or never: an announced node never enters anonymous mode and an anonymous node never announces; wanting both means two nodes.
Anonymous mode is offered only when rooms can be carried through the tier; until then a client lists the mode and does not enable it.
An anonymous node holds one identity; a person who wants two rooms kept apart runs two nodes; an ordinary node carries as many signers as it hosts.
In a room riding the tier an anonymous identity may hold moderate, takedown and review duties by the same appointment as any member; the holder is the node's identity.
An anonymous moderation-duty holder is blocked, contested by reconsideration:{grounds}, revoked by the room and tracked by moderation_track_record as any holder is.
An anonymous node is not a relay: it uses the tier and carries nothing for it, since a relay's route must be live and announced.
Every announced node that runs the substrate relays onion traffic for others by default, whether or not anyone on it uses the tier.
A node holding no serve seat may opt out of relaying by publishing the opt-out marker and withdrawing its hop key on the same superseding row.
A serve node never opts out of relaying: a seat carrying the marker is out of conformance as seat_opted_out, and a seat without a valid hop key as seat_without_hop_key.
A node with no hop key and no marker is not yet capable of relaying and is simply not placed.
Device policy: a phone relays by default only on Wi-Fi while charging; the user may override either way, the client stating each cost; servers and homes relay by default.
note: 880 phone relay default 'charging on unmetered network' is the same policy in other words

gist: The tier carries federation-scope publication and rooms: anonymous members exchange a room's rows through the tier, each reaching its mailbox by own route; such a room is private, never public.
An onion packet is fixed-length and layered, each hop's layer encapsulated to that hop's X-Wing hop key; each hop removes one layer, learns only the next; one KEM ciphertext per hop.
Every onion layer is post-quantum: a construction whose per-hop key agreement is classical alone is not conformant.
The onion packet's byte layout, KDF label and AEAD are pinned by this section from the implementer's submission with known answers in the verification library; residual at 1.13.3.1 until then.
The hop KEM is X-Wing as the normative reference defines it; another combiner over the same key shapes is another construction under another identifier.
The onion body is tagging-resistant: a hop that alters any byte leaves the packet unreadable at every later hop and at exit; wide-block satisfies, per-layer body seal does not.
An onion route has exactly three hops, one from each of three layers.
A relay for a period is a node whose signed transport_destination row is live and announced, with valid hop key and no opt-out marker, owner-bound under a bundle-charter root; unowned never.
At use a relay's layer links are shaped and an unshaped link carries no onion packet; activating the tier turns shaping on for the node's layer links.
Relay links are standing shaped links assigned by hash from the fold; a route is a walk over them and nothing is dialled per route.
Hop one is a sticky guard from the sender's own consented contacts offering relay (two for reach), outside any room the route serves; with none, a serve seat.
A guard is kept for as long as it answers, never rotated on a schedule.
A long-lived mailbox pins its second hop as well.
Other hops are drawn from the fold over standing links, filtered by the sender's local delivery probes (never a shared row), owner age from the witnessed head, one per owner.
There is no steward cap on who relays; the bound is per sender, not per layer.
Fewer than three answering relays in any position makes the tier unavailable for that period; the tier never runs thin.
A relay counts as answering when within the period it completed a shaped handshake, answered a route request, forwarded a packet the next hop acknowledged, or returned a self-addressed probe.

The tier is available at a node when the floor holds on the deal (else onion_tier_unavailable_floor) and at least three relays per layer answer (else onion_tier_unavailable_liveness); the client shows counts.
Every tier rule is a pure function of the fold, never of arrival order: no coordinator assigns layers and two nodes holding the same rows deal the same layers.
Onion packets travel as bodies of shaped frames; a longer packet is fragmented and reassembled at the next hop at the packet's own constant length; each hop a sealed attributed link.
The storage node sees the last relay, never the publisher.
A receiver accepting targeted anonymous delivery publishes its route as a rendezvous:route:v1 row signed by a fresh rendezvous key each hour, the route reused within that hour.
For federation-scope targeted delivery the rendezvous node holding the receiver's mailbox is a serve seat; one seat holds each mailbox, hour-scale ciphertext only.
A room's mailbox is two member-owned always-on nodes chosen by the room, each holding the full row set, placed by replication consent; with none, a seat (two-hour wake warning).
A phone is never a mailbox and never a hop a reused route runs through; a route through a sleeping node is lost.
A sender builds its own three-hop header from the directory's hop keys and appends the receiver's route.
Hop keys, layer assignments and rendezvous indexes rotate on global clocks, never on group events.
End-to-end cover (a steady rate of packets to a random relay) is on by default for an anonymous node, costing about a third of a home's shaped share.
User-facing copy says the anonymity set is small when few users share a relay; shaping is a prerequisite of the tier.

A federation-scope item published through the tier is signed by a fresh hybrid pseudonym key whose key:record:v1 travels inline, identity_type pseudonym, no occurrence, no standing, refused as an identity.
A reader composes a pseudonym's rows as a stranger's; no ring signature, a sender is never unattributed; a person may later bind a pseudonym to themselves by a signed row.
An anonymous peer is reached at its rendezvous route and answers a contact request through its own circuit; a route held for an announced contact is its circuit's exit, never dialled.

The direct-link contact exchange never runs over a circuit and a forwarder offers no reflexive address on one; announced-to-anonymous contact never goes direct, and the announced peer's client says so.
For any future multi-hop amendment, rotation clocks are global, never group-event-driven.
An item its owner marks durable is held by a chosen number of nodes in its own cohort, chunk by chunk, and repaired when that number falls
Nodes and relays never encode or decode stored content; they hold and forward sealed chunks whole; the ChunkLayer stack is stored per layer
Each node measures what it holds (per scope and plane: count and hybrid-signed Merkle root) and how deeply (holders, own chunk share, gap to target)
A node must not read an absent or lapsed claim as none; anything unclaimed within a claim's liveness window is unknown, never zero
Every inventory instrument is a pure fold over signed inputs, integer and permutation-invariant; disagreement is detected by comparing witness roots, never argued from counts
What the mesh as a whole holds is learned only through the census, never by reading another node's inventory
Measurement never enlarges what a node does: the census reaches node behaviour only through the mesh-config plane, which relieves and never expands; the base is a denominator
